children.title: Degree-Constrained Arborescences
children.top_down_role: Rooted directed spanning structures subject to vertex-degree restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Degree-Constrained Arborescences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hardness boundary created by vertex outdegree caps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a digraph \(D=(V,A)\), a root \(r\), and upper bounds \(b_v\), the degree-constrained arborescence feasibility problem asks for a spanning out-arborescence \(T\) rooted at \(r\) satisfying \(d_T^+(v)\le b_v\) for every \(v\in V\). When \(b_v=1\) for every vertex, any feasible \(T\) has \(|V|-1\) arcs, no branching vertex, and therefore is a directed Hamiltonian path beginning at \(r\). Conversely, every such Hamiltonian path is feasible. Hence this restricted feasibility problem is NP-complete, assuming the standard NP-completeness of fixed-start directed Hamiltonian path.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outdegree-one rooted arborescences are exactly directed Hamiltonian paths from the root, making degree-constrained feasibility NP-complete.
assumptions_latex: \(D=(V,A)\) is a finite digraph with prescribed root \(r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Degree-constrained spanning out-arborescence feasibility is NP-complete even under uniform outdegree bound \(1\).

notation.meaning: outdegree of v in arborescence T
outdegree upper bound at v

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reduction to fixed-start directed Hamiltonian path is mathematically plausible and the complexity content kind fits, but the NP-completeness premise and claimed restricted hardness have no source locator.

children.title: Hop-Constrained Arborescences
children.top_down_role: Rooted directed spanning structures subject to root-distance limits.

knowledge_statements.title: Hop-Constrained Arborescences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rooted arborescences with bounded root-to-vertex path length.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\), let \(r\in V\), and let \(H\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}\). An \(H\)-hop-constrained spanning out-arborescence is a spanning out-arborescence \(T\subseteq A\) rooted at \(r\) such that the unique directed path \(P_T(r,v)\) satisfies \[|P_T(r,v)|\le H\qquad\text{for every }v\in V.\] Equivalently, the depth of \(T\) from \(r\) is at most \(H\). The constraint is global: whether an entering arc is admissible depends on the depth induced by all predecessor choices, not solely on that arc.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hop-constrained arborescence limits every unique root-to-vertex path to at most H arcs, coupling each local parent choice to global depth.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\) is \(H\)-hop-constrained exactly when \(\max_{v\in V}|P_T(r,v)|\le H\).

notation.meaning: unique directed r-to-v path in T
maximum permitted number of arcs on a root path
spanning out-arborescence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is internally precise and distinguishes the global depth variant, but no authoritative source with a locator supports the selected hop-constrained convention.

children.title: Resource-Constrained Arborescences
children.top_down_role: Rooted directed spanning structures subject to budgets or resource capacities.

knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Constrained Arborescences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global additive-resource version of constrained rooted arborescences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each arc \(a\in A\) consume a nonnegative resource vector \(q_a\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}^{p}\), and let \(B\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}^{p}\). A globally resource-constrained spanning out-arborescence is a spanning out-arborescence \(T\) rooted at \(r\) satisfying \[\sum_{a\in T}q_a\le B,\] where the inequality is componentwise. In incidence variables this predicate is \(\sum_{a\in A}q_a x_a\le B\) together with the rooted-arborescence constraints and \(x\in\{0,1\}^{A}\). This definition selects global budgets; pathwise root-to-vertex resource bounds constitute a distinct variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A globally resource-constrained arborescence must respect one or more additive budgets over all selected arcs; pathwise budgets are a separate variant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility requires \(T\) to be a rooted spanning out-arborescence and \(\sum_{a\in T}q_a\le B\).

notation.meaning: nonnegative resource-consumption vector of arc a
componentwise global resource budget
binary arc-incidence vector

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The global additive-budget definition is coherent and explicitly separated from pathwise variants, but the selected resource-constrained convention lacks an authoritative source locator.

children.title: Combined-Constraint Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Model behavior when multiple arborescence side constraints are imposed simultaneously.

knowledge_statements.title: Combined-Constraint Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complexity inheritance when degree, hop, and resource restrictions are combined.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider feasibility of a rooted spanning out-arborescence subject simultaneously to outdegree bounds \(d_T^+(v)\le b_v\), hop bound \(\max_v|P_T(r,v)|\le H\), and global resource bounds \(\sum_{a\in T}q_a\le B\). This combined family contains the degree-constrained family as the special case \(H=|V|-1\), \(q_a=0\) for every \(a\), and \(B=0\). With \(b_v=1\) for every \(v\), feasibility is therefore equivalent to a directed Hamiltonian path beginning at \(r\). Consequently, the combined feasibility problem is NP-complete, even when its hop and resource constraints are nonbinding.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The combined family remains NP-complete because nonbinding hop and resource limits leave the NP-complete outdegree-one arborescence problem as a special case.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Combined degree-, hop-, and resource-constrained arborescence feasibility is NP-complete.

notation.meaning: outdegree upper bound at v
root-path hop bound
arc resource vectors and global budget

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The special-case inheritance argument is coherent and failure_boundary fits the container, but the NP-completeness conclusion depends on the unsourced degree-constrained hardness premise.

children.title: Shortest R–S Biconnectors

knowledge_statements.title: Shortest R–S Biconnectors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut formulation of the minimum-weight directed two-sided connector problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\), let \(R,S\subseteq V\) be disjoint and nonempty, and let \(w\in\mathbb R_+^A\). An \(R\)–\(S\) biconnector is an arc set \(B\subseteq A\) such that every vertex of \(R\) reaches some vertex of \(S\) in \((V,B)\), and every vertex of \(S\) is reachable from some vertex of \(R\). Equivalently, its incidence vector satisfies \(x(\delta^+(X))\ge1\) whenever \(X\cap R\ne\varnothing\) and \(X\cap S=\varnothing\), and \(x(\delta^-(X))\ge1\) whenever \(X\cap S\ne\varnothing\) and \(X\cap R=\varnothing\). The shortest-biconnector value is \[\min\{w^\top x:x\in\{0,1\}^A\text{ satisfies these inequalities}\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose minimum-weight arcs so every root reaches the opposite side and every opposite-side terminal is reachable from a root.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{opt}_{RS}(D,w)=\min\{w^\top x:x\text{ is the incidence vector of an }R\text{–}S\text{ biconnector}\}.\)

notation.meaning: arcs leaving and entering X, respectively

knowledge_statements.title: Longest R–S Biforests
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted maximization over the standard directed biforest family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\), let \(R,S\subseteq V\) be disjoint and nonempty, and let \(c\in\mathbb R^A\). Denote by \(\mathcal F_{R,S}(D)\) the family of \(R\)–\(S\) biforests in \(D\), in the standard two-sided directed-forest sense. The longest-biforest problem is the finite set optimization problem \[\max\{c(F):F\in\mathcal F_{R,S}(D)\},\qquad c(F):=\sum_{a\in F}c_a.\] An optimizer is any \(F^\star\in\mathcal F_{R,S}(D)\) attaining this maximum. The exact independence axioms defining \(\mathcal F_{R,S}(D)\) require confirmation from the cited source before promotion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The problem selects an R–S biforest of maximum total arc weight; the precise source-specific biforest axioms remain to be confirmed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F^\star\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{F\in\mathcal F_{R,S}(D)}c(F).\)

knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Size Bibranchings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cardinality minimization using the standard two-sided reachability cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) have a bipartition \(V=S\mathbin{\dot\cup}T\) with both classes nonempty. A bibranching is an arc set \(B\subseteq A\) such that every vertex of \(S\) reaches some vertex of \(T\) in \((V,B)\), and every vertex of \(T\) is reachable from some vertex of \(S\). Its minimum size is \[\tau(D;S,T)=\min\{|B|:B\subseteq A\text{ is an }S\text{–}T\text{ bibranching}\}.\] Equivalently, feasible incidence vectors satisfy \(x(\delta^+(X))\ge1\) for every nonempty \(X\subseteq S\) and \(x(\delta^-(Y))\ge1\) for every nonempty \(Y\subseteq T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimum-size bibranching uses the fewest arcs while connecting every S vertex toward T and every T vertex from S.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tau(D;S,T)=\min\{\mathbf1^\top x:x\in\{0,1\}^A,\ x(\delta^+(X))\ge1,\ x(\delta^-(Y))\ge1\}.\)

notation.meaning: minimum cardinality of an S–T bibranching

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Min–max formula for minimum-size R–S bibranchings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A cardinality min–max theorem under reachability assumptions guaranteeing the existence of an R–S bibranching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let D=(V,A) be a digraph with V=R\mathbin{\dot\cup}S. Suppose every vertex in R can reach S and every vertex in S is reachable from R. Then the minimum size of an R-S bibranching equals \max\{|U|:U\subseteq V,\ A[U]\cap\delta^{\mathrm{out}}(R)=\varnothing\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every R vertex can reach S and every S vertex is reachable from R, the minimum size of an R–S bibranching equals the largest cardinality of a vertex subset that spans no arc of the outgoing cut of R.
assumptions_latex: \forall r\in R,\ \exists s\in S:\ r\leadsto s\text{ in }D
\forall s\in S,\ \exists r\in R:\ r\leadsto s\text{ in }D
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min\{|B|:B\subseteq A\text{ is an }R-S\text{ bibranching}\}=\max\{|U|:U\subseteq V,\ A[U]\cap\delta^{\mathrm{out}}(R)=\varnothing\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: R–S Bicut
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut family used in minimum-length R–S bibranching optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a digraph whose vertex set is partitioned as \(V=R\mathbin{\dot\cup}S\). An arc set \(C\) is an \(R-S\) bicut if \(C=\delta^{\mathrm{in}}(U)\) for some nonempty proper subset \(U\subsetneq V\) such that \(U\subseteq S\) or \(S\subseteq U\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimum Bibranching Min–Max Theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integral min–max characterization of minimum-length R–S bibranchings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a digraph, let \(V=R\mathbin{\dot\cup}S\), and let \(l:A\to\mathbb{Z}_{+}\). The minimum length \(\sum_{a\in B}l(a)\) of an \(R-S\) bibranching \(B\) equals the maximum cardinality of a family \(\mathcal C\) of \(R-S\) dicuts, with repetitions allowed, such that each arc \(a\in A\) belongs to at most \(l(a)\) members of \(\mathcal C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nonnegative integer arc lengths, the minimum length of an R–S bibranching equals the largest size of a possibly repeated family of R–S dicuts in which each arc occurs at most as many times as its length permits.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{B\text{ an }R-S\text{ bibranching}}\sum_{a\in B}l(a)=\max\left\{|\mathcal C|:\mathcal C\text{ is a family of }R-S\text{ dicuts},\ |\{C\in\mathcal C:a\in C\}|\leq l(a)\ \forall a\in A\right\}

knowledge_statements.title: Bifurcation Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut-packing dual associated with the weighted bibranching covering program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the shortest-bibranching program on \(V=S\mathbin{\dot\cup}T\), assign \(p_X\ge0\) to each nonempty \(X\subseteq S\) and \(q_Y\ge0\) to each nonempty \(Y\subseteq T\). Its bifurcation dual is \[\max\left\{\sum_{\varnothing\ne X\subseteq S}p_X+\sum_{\varnothing\ne Y\subseteq T}q_Y:\sum_{X:a\in\delta^+(X)}p_X+\sum_{Y:a\in\delta^-(Y)}q_Y\le w_a\quad(a\in A)\right\}.\] Whenever the primal bibranching program is feasible and bounded, linear-programming duality gives equality of these values. An integral or combinatorial interpretation of an optimal dual support is called a bifurcation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bifurcation duality equates shortest-bibranching cost with the maximum feasible packing of outgoing S-cuts and incoming T-cuts under arc weights.
assumptions_latex: The primal bibranching covering program is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min(P_{\mathrm{bi}})=\max(D_{\mathrm{bif}}).\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Maximum R–S Bifurcation Min–Max Theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong-component characterization of maximum bifurcation cardinality under the condition that no arc enters R.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a digraph with \(V=R\mathbin{\dot\cup}S\) and \(\delta^{\mathrm{in}}(R)=\varnothing\). Then the maximum cardinality of an \(R-S\) bifurcation equals \(\min_{\mathcal L}(|V|-|\mathcal L|)\), where \(\mathcal L\) ranges over collections of strong components \(K\) of \(D\) such that each \(K\) satisfies either \(K\subseteq R\) and \(\delta^{\mathrm{out}}(K)\subseteq\delta^{\mathrm{out}}(R)\), or \(K\subseteq S\) and \(\delta^{\mathrm{in}}(K)\subseteq\delta^{\mathrm{in}}(S)\), and no arc connects two distinct components in \(\mathcal L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If no arc enters R, the maximum size of an R–S bifurcation is the minimum of the number of vertices minus the number of selected strong components, over collections satisfying the stated R-side or S-side boundary condition and with no arc joining two selected components.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max\{|B|:B\text{ is an }R-S\text{ bifurcation}\}=\min_{\mathcal L}\bigl(|V|-|\mathcal L|\bigr)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: R–S Bifurcation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acyclic two-sided directed structure associated with bibranching duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a digraph with \(V=R\mathbin{\dot\cup}S\). An arc set \(B\subseteq A\) is an \(R-S\) bifurcation if it contains no undirected circuit, every vertex in \(R\) is left by at most one arc of \(B\), every vertex in \(S\) is entered by at most one arc of \(B\), and \(B\) contains no arc directed from \(S\) to \(R\). Equivalently, contracting \(R\) yields a branching and contracting \(S\) yields a cobranching, where a cobranching is an arc set whose reversal is a branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An R–S bifurcation is an arc set with no undirected circuit, at most one selected arc leaving each R vertex, at most one selected arc entering each S vertex, and no selected arc from S to R. Equivalently, contracting R gives a branching and contracting S gives a cobranching.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B\text{ is an }R-S\text{ bifurcation}\iff\left(B\text{ has no undirected circuit},\ d_B^{\mathrm{out}}(r)\leq1\ \forall r\in R,\ d_B^{\mathrm{in}}(s)\leq1\ \forall s\in S,\ B\cap\delta^{\mathrm{out}}(S,R)=\varnothing\right)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Integral min–max theorem for maximum-length R–S bifurcations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted bifurcation duality for a digraph whose partition admits no arcs from S to R.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a digraph, let \(V=R\mathbin{\dot\cup}S\), assume that no arc goes from \(S\) to \(R\), and let \(l\in\mathbb Z_+^A\). Define \(\mathcal U=\{U\ne\varnothing:U\subseteq R\text{ or }U\subseteq S\}\). The maximum \(l\)-length of an \(R\)-\(S\) bifurcation equals
\[
\min\left\{\sum_{v\in V}y_v+\sum_{U\in\mathcal U}z_U(|U|-1):\ y\in\mathbb Z_+^V,\ z\in\mathbb Z_+^{\mathcal U},\ \sum_{v\in R}y_v\chi^{\delta^{\rm out}(v)}+\sum_{v\in S}y_v\chi^{\delta^{\rm in}(v)}+\sum_{U\in\mathcal U}z_U\chi^{A[U]}\ge l\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If V is partitioned into R and S with no arc from S to R and the arcs have nonnegative integral lengths, then the maximum length of an R–S bifurcation equals the stated minimum integral covering value over vertex variables and variables indexed by nonempty subsets lying wholly in R or wholly in S.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max\{l\text{-length of an }R\text{-}S\text{ bifurcation}\}=\min\left\{\sum_{v\in V}y_v+\sum_{U\in\mathcal U}z_U(|U|-1):y\in\mathbb Z_+^V,\ z\in\mathbb Z_+^{\mathcal U},\ \sum_{v\in R}y_v\chi^{\delta^{\rm out}(v)}+\sum_{v\in S}y_v\chi^{\delta^{\rm in}(v)}+\sum_{U\in\mathcal U}z_U\chi^{A[U]}\ge l\right\}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arc-disjoint packing characterized by two families of separating cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) and let \(R,S\subseteq V\) be disjoint and nonempty. Consequently, the maximum packing number is the minimum cardinality among these two classes of directed separating cuts.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Characterization of edge covers by k R–S biforests
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A necessary-and-sufficient pair of local sparsity inequalities for covering all edges by k R–S biforests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let G=(V,E), let V=R\mathbin{\dot\cup}S, and let k\in\mathbb Z_+. The edge set E can be covered by k R-S biforests if and only if, for every nonempty U\subseteq R and every nonempty U\subseteq S, |E[U]|\le k(|U|-1) and |E[U]|+|\delta(U)\cap\delta(R)|\le k|U|.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All edges can be covered by k R–S biforests exactly when every nonempty subset of either side satisfies both the induced-edge sparsity bound and the induced-plus-crossing-edge bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E\text{ is coverable by }k\ R-S\text{ biforests}\iff \forall U,\ |E[U]|\le k(|U|-1)\ \land\ |E[U]|+|\delta(U)\cap\delta(R)|\le k|U|

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $D=(V,A)$ be a digraph whose vertex set is bipartitioned as $V=S\dot\cup T$. A bibranching is a subdigraph containing a directed path from $S$ to every $t\in T$ and a directed path from every $s\in S$ to $T$. If $|S|=1$, this notion is equivalent to root-connectivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a digraph with vertex bipartition S and T, a bibranching contains a directed path from S to each vertex of T and a directed path from each vertex of S to T. When S is a singleton, this is equivalent to root-connectivity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B\text{ is a bibranching}\iff\bigl(\forall t\in T,\ S\leadsto_B t\bigr)\land\bigl(\forall s\in S,\ s\leadsto_B T\bigr);\quad |S|=1\Rightarrow\text{bibranching is equivalent to root-connectivity}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Characterization of Arc Coverability by R–S Bifurcations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A necessary-and-sufficient degree and induced-arc characterization for covering a partitioned digraph by k R–S bifurcations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a digraph whose vertex set is partitioned into \(R\) and \(S\), with no arc directed from \(S\) to \(R\). Then \(A\) can be covered by \(k\) \(R\)-\(S\) bifurcations if and only if: (i) \(\deg^{\mathrm{out}}(v)\le k\) for every \(v\in R\); (ii) \(\deg^{\mathrm{in}}(v)\le k\) for every \(v\in S\); and (iii) \(|A[U]|\le k(|U|-1)\) for every nonempty \(U\subseteq R\) and every nonempty \(U\subseteq S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a digraph's vertices are partitioned into R and S and there is no arc from S to R, then its arc set can be covered by k R–S bifurcations exactly when every vertex of R has outdegree at most k, every vertex of S has indegree at most k, and every nonempty vertex subset lying wholly in either side induces at most k times one less than its cardinality arcs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A\text{ is coverable by }k\text{ R--S bifurcations}\iff\left[\forall v\in R,\ \deg^{\mathrm{out}}(v)\le k;\ \forall v\in S,\ \deg^{\mathrm{in}}(v)\le k;\ \forall\varnothing\ne U\subseteq R\text{ or }\varnothing\ne U\subseteq S,\ |A[U]|\le k(|U|-1)\right].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Disjoint Bibranchings Cut Characterization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Packing characterization for edge-disjoint bibranchings in a digraph with vertex bipartition $S,T$.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $D=(V,A)$ be a digraph with $V=S\dot\cup T$, and let $k$ be a nonnegative integer. Then $D$ contains $k$ pairwise edge-disjoint bibranchings if and only if $\varrho_D(X)\ge k$ for every $\varnothing\ne X\subseteq T$ and $\delta_D(X)\ge k$ for every $\varnothing\ne X\subseteq S$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A digraph with vertex bipartition S and T contains k edge-disjoint bibranchings exactly when every nonempty subset of T has at least k entering edges and every nonempty subset of S has at least k leaving edges.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D\text{ contains }k\text{ edge-disjoint bibranchings}\iff\left[\forall\varnothing\ne X\subseteq T,\ \varrho_D(X)\ge k\right]\land\left[\forall\varnothing\ne X\subseteq S,\ \delta_D(X)\ge k\right].

knowledge_statements.title: Biforest Coverings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-cover formulation for covering arcs by directed biforests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) and let \(\mathcal F_{R,S}(D)\subseteq2^A\) be its source-defined family of \(R\)–\(S\) biforests. A biforest covering is a finite indexed family \((F_i)_{i=1}^m\) with \(F_i\in\mathcal F_{R,S}(D)\) and \(A\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^mF_i\). Its covering number is \[\chi_{\mathrm{bf}}(D;R,S)=\min\left\{m:A\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^mF_i,\ F_i\in\mathcal F_{R,S}(D)\right\}.\] If no such family exists, the value is \(+\infty\). The exact structural axioms for the intended biforest family require source confirmation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A biforest covering is a collection of R–S biforests whose union contains every arc; its covering number is the smallest collection size.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\chi_{\mathrm{bf}}(D;R,S)=\min\{m:A\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^mF_i,\ F_i\in\mathcal F_{R,S}(D)\}.\)

knowledge_statements.title: Bifurcation Coverings

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tree and 1-Orientable Spanning-Subgraph Packing Criterion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Includes the explicitly allowed degenerate partitions involving the distinguished part \(V_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k,k_1\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\) and let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected graph. The graph contains \(k\) spanning trees and \(k_1\) 1-orientable spanning subgraphs that are pairwise edge-disjoint if and only if, for every partition \(\mathcal P=\{V_0,V_1,\ldots,V_q\}\) of \(V\) in which only \(V_0\) may be empty, \[ e_G(\mathcal P)+i_G(V_0)\geq k(q-1)+(k+k_1)|V_0|. \] The condition also applies when \(V_0=V,q=0\) and when \(\varnothing\subset V_0\subset V,q=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An undirected graph has pairwise edge-disjoint copies of k spanning trees and k1 spanning subgraphs admitting an orientation of indegree exactly one if and only if the stated partition inequality holds for every partition with only the distinguished part V0 allowed to be empty, including the specified degenerate cases.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal P=\{V_0,V_1,\ldots,V_q\}\text{ is a partition of }V\text{ and only }V_0\text{ may be empty}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G\text{ contains the stated pairwise edge-disjoint spanning structures}\iff \forall\mathcal P,\ e_G(\mathcal P)+i_G(V_0)\geq k(q-1)+(k+k_1)|V_0|.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tutte–Nash-Williams Tree-Packing Criterion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partition-cut characterization of the existence of edge-disjoint spanning trees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $G$ be an undirected graph and let $k\ge 1$. Then $G$ contains $k$ pairwise edge-disjoint spanning trees if and only if, for every partition $V(G)=X_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}X_p$ into nonempty sets, $|\delta(X_1,\ldots,X_p)|\ge k(p-1)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An undirected graph contains k edge-disjoint spanning trees exactly when every partition of its vertices has at least k times one less than the number of blocks crossing edges.
assumptions_latex: V(G)=X_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}X_p\text{ ranges over partitions into nonempty sets}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G\text{ contains }k\text{ pairwise edge-disjoint spanning trees}\iff \forall(X_1,\ldots,X_p),\ |\delta(X_1,\ldots,X_p)|\ge k(p-1)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: k-Tight Partitions and k-Rich Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions associated with the k-forest covering formula and spanning-tree packings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $G=(V,E)$ be an undirected graph and $k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}$. A partition $\mathcal P^*$ of $V$ is $k$-tight if it minimizes $k(|V|-|\mathcal P|)+e_G(\mathcal P)$ over all partitions $\mathcal P$ of $V$. A nonempty set $X\subseteq V$ is $k$-rich if the induced graph $G[X]=(X,I_G(X))$ contains $k$ pairwise edge-disjoint spanning trees. It is strictly $k$-rich if $G[X]-e$ contains $k$ pairwise edge-disjoint spanning trees for every $e\in I_G(X)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A k-tight partition minimizes the partition expression in the k-forest covering formula. A nonempty vertex set is k-rich when its induced graph contains k edge-disjoint spanning trees, and strictly k-rich when this remains true after deletion of any induced edge.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal P^*\text{ is }k\text{-tight}\iff \mathcal P^*\in\arg\min_{\mathcal P}\{k(|V|-|\mathcal P|)+e_G(\mathcal P)\};\quad X\text{ is }k\text{-rich}\iff G[X]\text{ contains }k\text{ edge-disjoint spanning trees};\quad X\text{ is strictly }k\text{-rich}\iff \forall e\in I_G(X),\ G[X]-e\text{ contains }k\text{ edge-disjoint spanning trees}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inductive Construction of Graphs with k Edge-Disjoint Spanning Trees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constructive characterization allowing parallel edges.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}$. A graph $G$ contains $k$ pairwise edge-disjoint spanning trees if and only if it can be obtained from a single vertex by repeatedly applying any of the following operations: (A') add an edge between existing vertices; (B') add a new vertex $z$ together with $k$ possibly parallel edges joining $z$ to existing vertices; or (C') choose an integer $j$ with $0<j<k$, pinch $j$ edges together at a new vertex $z$, and add $k-j$ possibly parallel edges joining $z$ to existing vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A graph has k edge-disjoint spanning trees exactly when it can be constructed from one vertex using edge additions, addition of a new vertex incident with k edges, and pinching j edges at a new vertex followed by adding k minus j further incident edges, where 0 < j < k.
assumptions_latex: G\text{ is an undirected graph; parallel edges are permitted in the construction}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G\text{ contains }k\text{ pairwise edge-disjoint spanning trees}\iff G\text{ is constructible from one vertex by operations }(A'),(B'),(C').

children.title: Partition Connectivity
children.top_down_role: Partition structure governing spanning-tree packings.

knowledge_statements.title: Partition Connectivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partition inequality governing edge-disjoint spanning-tree packings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite undirected multigraph and let \(k\in\mathbb Z_+\). For a partition \(\mathcal P\) of \(V\), let \(e_G(\mathcal P)\) be the number of edges whose endpoints lie in distinct blocks. The graph is \(k\)-partition-connected when \[e_G(\mathcal P)\ge k\bigl(|\mathcal P|-1\bigr)\] for every partition \(\mathcal P\) of \(V\). By the Tutte–Nash-Williams theorem, this condition is equivalent to the existence of \(k\) pairwise edge-disjoint spanning trees in \(G\). Parallel edges are counted with multiplicity; loops never cross a partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A graph is k-partition-connected when every vertex partition has at least k times one fewer crossing edges; equivalently, it packs k edge-disjoint spanning trees.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G\text{ contains }k\text{ edge-disjoint spanning trees}\iff e_G(\mathcal P)\ge k(|\mathcal P|-1)\) for every partition \(\mathcal P\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Double-Partition of a Subset
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the construction, its ground-degree, and its partition and co-partition boundary cases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \{Z_1,\ldots,Z_t\} be a partition of Z. For each i, let \{Z_i^1,\ldots,Z_i^{t_i}\} be a partition of S\setminus Z_i, where t_i\ge1. Then \mathcal D:=\{S\setminus Z_i^j:1\le i\le t,\ 1\le j\le t_i\} is a double-partition of Z. It is a composition of Z with ground-degree \sum_{i=1}^t(t_i-1). If t=1 it is a co-partition of Z, and if t_i=1 for every i it is a partition of Z.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A double-partition is obtained by taking, for every block of a partition of Z, the sets in a co-partition of that block. Its ground-degree is the sum of t_i minus one. It reduces to a co-partition when the outer partition has one block and to a partition when every inner partition has one block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal D=\{S\setminus Z_i^j\}_{i,j}\text{ is a composition of }Z\text{ with }d_{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathcal D)=\sum_{i=1}^t(t_i-1).

knowledge_statements.title: Tight Partition Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality partitions certifying saturation of the tree-packing bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite \(k\)-partition-connected multigraph, and let \(T_1,\ldots,T_k\) be pairwise edge-disjoint spanning trees. A partition \(\mathcal P\) of \(V\) is tight when \[e_G(\mathcal P)=k\bigl(|\mathcal P|-1\bigr).\] For every tight partition \(\mathcal P\), each packed tree satisfies \[|E(T_i)\cap\delta(\mathcal P)|=|\mathcal P|-1\qquad(i=1,\ldots,k),\] and every edge in \(\delta(\mathcal P)\) belongs to exactly one of the packed trees. Thus the tight partition certifies saturation of the partition bound by the packing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tight partition meets the tree-packing inequality with equality and certifies that every packed tree uses exactly one fewer crossing edges than the number of partition blocks, with all crossing edges saturated by the packing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e_G(\mathcal P)=k(|\mathcal P|-1)\Rightarrow |E(T_i)\cap\delta(\mathcal P)|=|\mathcal P|-1\) for every \(i\), and \(\delta(\mathcal P)\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^kE(T_i)\).

notation.meaning: edges whose endpoints lie in distinct blocks of the partition
cardinality of the partition-crossing edge set

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Extremal k-Tight Partitions from Maximal Rich Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Describes the finest and coarsest tight partitions and the sparsity of their contractions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $G=(V,E)$ be an undirected graph and $k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}$. The maximal strictly $k$-rich subsets of $V$ form a partition $\mathcal P_0$, and contracting every class of $\mathcal P_0$ yields a $k$-sparse graph. The maximal $k$-rich subsets form a partition $\mathcal P_1$, and contracting every class of $\mathcal P_1$ yields a strictly $k$-sparse graph. Both $\mathcal P_0$ and $\mathcal P_1$ are $k$-tight; moreover, $\mathcal P_0$ is the unique finest $k$-tight partition and $\mathcal P_1$ is the unique coarsest $k$-tight partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximal strictly k-rich sets partition the vertices and contract to a k-sparse graph, while maximal k-rich sets partition the vertices and contract to a strictly k-sparse graph. These are respectively the unique finest and unique coarsest k-tight partitions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal P_0\text{ and }\mathcal P_1\text{ are respectively the unique finest and unique coarsest }k\text{-tight partitions, with }G/\mathcal P_0\text{ }k\text{-sparse and }G/\mathcal P_1\text{ strictly }k\text{-sparse}.

It is cardinality-minimal if \(|\mathcal P|\le |\mathcal Q|\) for every \(\mathcal Q\in\mathfrak C_k\).

children.title: Capacitated Tree Packing
children.top_down_role: Tree packing under edge-capacity multiplicities.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite connected undirected multigraph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \tau_c(G)=\min_{\mathcal P}\left\lfloor\frac{c(\delta_G(\mathcal P))}{|\mathcal P|-1}\right\rfloor\), where the minimum ranges over partitions with at least two blocks.

notation.meaning: Total capacity of an edge set
Maximum size of a capacity-feasible spanning-tree packing

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integral capacitated form of the Tutte–Nash-Williams packing theorem.

source_refs.locator: Section 6.4. Packing Spanning Trees and Arborescences p. 147

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A capacitated packing of size \(k\) is a multiset of spanning trees \(T_1,\ldots,T_k\) such that every edge \(e\) occurs in at most \(c(e)\) members. Such a packing exists exactly when, for every partition \(\mathcal P\) of \(V\),
\[c(\delta_G(\mathcal P))\ge k(|\mathcal P|-1).\]
Hence the maximum feasible integer value equals
\[\tau_c(G)=\min_{\mathcal P:\,|\mathcal P|\ge2}\left\lfloor\frac{c(\delta_G(\mathcal P))}{|\mathcal P|-1}\right\rfloor.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integral edge capacities support k spanning trees exactly when every vertex partition has capacity at least k times its block count minus one.
knowledge_statements.title: Capacitated Tree Packing

children.title: Fractional Tree Packing
children.top_down_role: Relaxed tree packings with fractional structure weights.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite connected undirected multigraph.
\(c:E\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\) is a nonnegative capacity vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The fractional packing optimum, its covering dual optimum, and \(\displaystyle\min_{|\mathcal P|\ge2}c(\delta_G(\mathcal P))/(|\mathcal P|-1)\) are equal.

notation.meaning: Set of spanning trees of G
Nonnegative weight assigned to spanning tree T
Nonnegative dual length of edge e

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fractional packing LP, covering dual, and partition-density formula.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 10. Trees and arborescences: packing and covering p. 339

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The fractional tree-packing value is
\[\max\left\{\sum_{T\in\mathcal T(G)}x_T:x_T\ge0,\ \sum_{T\ni e}x_T\le c(e)\ \text{for every }e\in E\right\}.\]
Its linear-programming dual is
\[\min\left\{\sum_{e\in E}c(e)y_e:y_e\ge0,\ \sum_{e\in T}y_e\ge1\ \text{for every }T\in\mathcal T(G)\right\}.\]
Both optima equal
\[\min_{\mathcal P:\,|\mathcal P|\ge2}\frac{c(\delta_G(\mathcal P))}{|\mathcal P|-1}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fractional spanning-tree packing equals both its edge-length covering dual and the minimum capacity-to-partition-deficit ratio.
knowledge_statements.title: Fractional Tree Packing

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For integral edge capacities, the fractional and integral tree-packing optima satisfy \[\rho_c(G)=\min_{\mathcal P:\,|\mathcal P|\ge2}\frac{c(\delta_G(\mathcal P))}{|\mathcal P|-1},\qquad \tau_c(G)=\min_{\mathcal P:\,|\mathcal P|\ge2}\left\lfloor\frac{c(\delta_G(\mathcal P))}{|\mathcal P|-1}\right\rfloor=\lfloor\rho_c(G)\rfloor.\] Thus allowing fractional tree weights changes the optimum by less than one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With integral edge capacities, the maximum integral tree packing is exactly the floor of the fractional packing value.

children.title: Minimum-Weight Unions of Spanning Trees
children.top_down_role: Weighted optimization over unions of multiple spanning trees.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite connected undirected graph.
\(w:E\to\mathbb R\) assigns an edge weight and \(k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimum is \(\displaystyle\min\{\sum_{e\in U}w(e):U=T_1\dot\cup\cdots\dot\cup T_k,\ T_i\text{ spanning trees}\}\), when the feasible family is nonempty.

notation.meaning: Union of the packed spanning trees
Total weight of an edge set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses edge-disjoint trees and charges each selected edge once.

source_refs.locator: Section 6.4. Packing Spanning Trees and Arborescences p. 147

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A feasible union of \(k\) spanning trees is an edge set \(U\subseteq E\) admitting a disjoint decomposition
\[U=T_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}T_k,\]
where every \(T_i\) is a spanning tree of \(G\). The minimum-weight-union problem minimizes \(w(U)=\sum_{e\in U}w(e)\) over all such decompositions. Feasibility is equivalent to
\[|\delta_G(\mathcal P)|\ge k(|\mathcal P|-1)\]
for every partition \(\mathcal P\) of \(V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose k edge-disjoint spanning trees and minimize the total weight of their union; partition inequalities characterize feasibility.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Maximum Edge Set Coverable by k Forests
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partition min-max formula for the maximum size of a union of k forests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be an undirected graph and $k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1}$. The maximum cardinality of an edge set $F\subseteq E$ that can be covered by $k$ forests is
\[
\max |F|=\min_{\mathcal P=\{V_1,\ldots,V_q\}\text{ a partition of }V}\bigl(k(|V|-q)+e_G(\mathcal P)\bigr),
\]
where $e_G(\mathcal P)$ is the number of edges of $G$ joining distinct classes of $\mathcal P$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The largest number of edges that can be covered by k forests equals the minimum, over all q-class vertex partitions, of k times |V| minus q plus the number of edges crossing between classes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max\{|F|:F\subseteq E\text{ is coverable by }k\text{ forests}\}=\min_{\mathcal P=\{V_1,\ldots,V_q\}}\{k(|V|-q)+e_G(\mathcal P)\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: (≤1)-Orientable and 1-Orientable Graphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions for an undirected graph or its edge set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\), or its edge set, is \((\leq 1)\)-orientable if there exists an orientation \(D\) of \(G\) such that \(\varrho_D(v)\leq 1\) for every \(v\in V\). knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A graph is (≤1)-orientable if its edges can be oriented so that every vertex has indegree at most one, and is 1-orientable if every vertex can be given indegree exactly one.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Connected Graphs, Trees, and Forests
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary undirected spanning-structure terminology.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A graph is connected if every pair of its vertices is joined by a path. A tree $G=(V,T)$ is a connected graph with no cycles. A forest is a collection $F=\{(V_1,T_1),\ldots,(V_k,T_k)\}$ of pairwise vertex-disjoint trees. The tree $(V,T)$ spans $V$, and the forest $F$ spans $\bigcup_{i=1}^k V_i$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A graph is connected when every two vertices are joined by a path. A tree is a connected acyclic graph. A forest is a collection of vertex-disjoint trees. A tree spans its vertex set, while a forest spans the union of the vertex sets of its component trees.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G\text{ is a tree}\iff G\text{ is connected and acyclic; }F\text{ spans }\bigcup_{i=1}^kV_i.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The arboricity \(a(G)\), defined as the least \(k\) for which \(E\) is the union of \(k\) forests, satisfies
\[a(G)=\max_{H\subseteq G,\,|V(H)|\ge2}\left\lceil\frac{|E(H)|}{|V(H)|-1}\right\rceil.\]
Equivalently, \(E\) decomposes into \(k\) forests if and only if every subgraph \(H\) with at least two vertices obeys
\[|E(H)|\le k(|V(H)|-1).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The arboricity equals the largest rounded-up edge density using vertices minus one, taken over all nontrivial subgraphs.

children.title: Pseudoforest Decompositions

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite loopless undirected multigraph with at least one edge.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E\) decomposes into \(k\) pseudoforests if and only if \(|E(H)|\le k|V(H)|\) for every nonempty subgraph \(H\subseteq G\).

notation.meaning: Minimum number of pseudoforests partitioning E
A subgraph of G containing at least one edge

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pseudoforests have at most one cycle in each connected component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A pseudoforest is a graph in which every connected component contains at most one cycle. The edge set \(E\) can be partitioned into \(k\) pseudoforests if and only if every nonempty subgraph \(H\subseteq G\) satisfies
\[|E(H)|\le k|V(H)|.\]
Consequently, the pseudoarboricity is
\[p(G)=\max_{H\subseteq G,\,|E(H)|>0}\left\lceil\frac{|E(H)|}{|V(H)|}\right\rceil.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Edges split into k pseudoforests exactly when every nonempty subgraph has at most k times as many edges as vertices.

children.title: Bounded-Outdegree Orientations

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite loopless undirected multigraph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An orientation with \(d_D^+(v)\le k\) for every vertex exists exactly when \(|E(X)|\le k|X|\) for every \(X\subseteq V\).

notation.meaning: Outdegree of v in orientation D
Edges having both endpoints in X

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform outdegree bound; parallel edges are allowed and loops are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
There exists an orientation \(D\) of every edge of \(G\) such that
\[d_D^+(v)\le k\qquad\text{for every }v\in V\]
if and only if
\[|E(X)|\le k|X|\qquad\text{for every }X\subseteq V.\]
The necessity follows by charging each edge induced by \(X\) to its tail in \(X\); the displayed inequalities constitute the complete feasibility predicate for the bounded-outdegree orientation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A graph admits an orientation of maximum outdegree k exactly when every vertex subset induces at most k times its size edges.
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Outdegree Orientations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bounded-outdegree orientation criterion is standard and fits the condition leaf, but no source or locator is supplied. The statement also contains a necessity argument that must be removed when a sourced replacement is prepared.

knowledge_statements.title: Decomposition–Orientation Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite loopless multigraph version of the pseudoforest decomposition correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite loopless undirected multigraph and let \(k\ge 1\). Then \(E\) can be partitioned into \(k\) pseudoforests if and only if the edges of \(G\) admit an orientation \(D\) satisfying \(d_D^+(v)\le k\) for every \(v\in V\). knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E\text{ partitions into }k\text{ pseudoforests}\iff \exists D\;\forall v\in V,\ d_D^+(v)\le k.\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Huck's openly disjoint arborescence-path theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constructs one arborescence from each source of a simple acyclic digraph under a uniform in-degree condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $D=(V,A)$ be a simple acyclic digraph whose source set is $R=\{r_1,\ldots,r_k\}$, and let $U=V\setminus R$. If every $u\in U$ has in-degree at least $k$, then for each $i=1,\ldots,k$ there is an $r_i$-arborescence $F_i$ spanning $U\cup\{r_i\}$ such that, for every $u\in U$, the unique $r_i$-$u$ paths in $F_1,\ldots,F_k$ are openly disjoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a simple acyclic digraph with k sources and in-degree at least k at every other vertex, one can construct a spanning arborescence from each source so that the k source-to-u paths are internally vertex-disjoint for every nonsource u.
assumptions_latex: R=\{r_1,\ldots,r_k\}\text{ is exactly the set of source vertices}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists F_1,\ldots,F_k\text{ such that each $F_i$ is an $r_i$-arborescence spanning $U\cup\{r_i\}$ and, for every $u\in U$, the paths $P_{F_i}(r_i,u)$ are openly disjoint.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent Characterizations of Packing Rooted Arborescences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence among rooted-arborescence packing, directed cut conditions, local path packings, and a spanning-tree representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a digraph, let \(r\in V\), and let \(k\in\mathbb Z_+\). The following are equivalent: (i) there exist \(k\) pairwise arc-disjoint \(r\)-arborescences; (ii) \(d^{\mathrm{in}}(U)\geq k\) for every nonempty \(U\subseteq V\setminus\{r\}\); (iii) for each \(s\neq r\), there exist \(k\) arc-disjoint directed \(r\)-\(s\) paths in \(D\); (iv) there exist \(k\) edge-disjoint spanning trees in the underlying undirected graph such that, for each \(s\neq r\), exactly \(k\) arcs entering \(s\) are covered by these trees.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each positive integer k, packing k arc-disjoint r-arborescences is equivalent to the k-entry cut condition, to having k arc-disjoint paths from r to every other vertex, and to the stated edge-disjoint spanning-tree representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{(i)}\Longleftrightarrow\text{(ii)}\Longleftrightarrow\text{(iii)}\Longleftrightarrow\text{(iv)}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Extension criterion for partial rooted arborescences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes when given arc-disjoint partial arborescences with a common root extend to spanning ones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let D'=(V,A') have root r_0, and let F_1,\ldots,F_k be pairwise arc-disjoint arborescences rooted at r_0, allowing empty arc sets but always containing r_0. Let D=(V,A) consist of the arcs of D' unused by all F_i, and define p(X)=|\{i:V(F_i)\cap X=\varnothing\}|. The F_i can be extended to k pairwise arc-disjoint spanning arborescences of D' if and only if \varrho_D(X)\ge p(X) for every \varnothing\neq X\subseteq V\setminus\{r_0\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given edge-disjoint partial arborescences with a common root, they extend to edge-disjoint spanning arborescences exactly when every nonempty set excluding the root receives enough unused edges to serve all partial arborescences that currently avoid that set.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lower- and upper-bounded root multiplicities in arborescence packings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut-and-partition characterization under vertexwise lower and upper bounds on root occurrences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $D=(V,A)$ have $k$ arc-disjoint arborescences, and let $l,u\in\mathbb Z_+^V$ satisfy $l\le u$. There exist $k$ arc-disjoint arborescences such that, for each $v\in V$, at least $l(v)$ and at most $u(v)$ are rooted at $v$ if and only if, for every nonempty $U\subseteq V$ and every partition $\mathcal P$ of $V\setminus U$ into nonempty sets, $$u(U)+d^{\mathrm{in}}(U)\ge k\quad\text{and}\quad l(U)+\sum_{W\in\mathcal P}\bigl(k-d^{\mathrm{in}}(W)\bigr)\le k.$$
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assume the digraph has k arc-disjoint arborescences. A packing can be chosen so that the number rooted at each vertex lies between prescribed nonnegative integer bounds if and only if both stated inequalities hold for every nonempty vertex set and every partition of its complement into nonempty classes.
assumptions_latex: D=(V,A)\text{ is a digraph having }k\text{ arc-disjoint arborescences}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\,k\text{ arc-disjoint arborescences with }l(v)\le \#\{i:v\text{ is the root of }B_i\}\le u(v)\ \forall v\in V\iff \left(u(U)+d^{\mathrm{in}}(U)\ge k\ \land\ l(U)+\sum_{W\in\mathcal P}(k-d^{\mathrm{in}}(W))\le k\right)\ \forall\,\varnothing\ne U\subseteq V,\ \forall\mathcal P\text{ partitioning }V\setminus U\text{ into nonempty sets.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Capacitated Integral Arborescence-Packing Min–Max Theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Capacitated integral form of the rooted-arborescence packing and cut min–max theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a digraph, let \(r\in V\), and let \(c\in\mathbb Z_+^A\) be an arc-capacity function. The minimum capacity of an \(r\)-cut equals \[\max\left\{\sum_B\lambda_B:\lambda_B\in\mathbb Z_+\text{ for every }r\text{-arborescence }B,\ \sum_B\lambda_B\chi^B\leq c\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nonnegative integral arc capacities, the minimum capacity of an r-cut equals the maximum total integral multiplicity of r-arborescences packable without exceeding any arc capacity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min\{c(C):C\text{ is an }r\text{-cut}\}=\max\left\{\sum_B\lambda_B:\lambda_B\in\mathbb Z_+\text{ for each }r\text{-arborescence }B,\ \sum_B\lambda_B\chi^B\leq c\right\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sufficient Conditions for Packing Steiner Arborescences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Terminal-cut and nonterminal degree conditions ensuring a common-root Steiner packing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let D=(V,A) be a digraph, r_0\in V, T\subseteq V\setminus\{r_0\}, and k\ge1. Suppose \varrho_D(X)\ge k whenever X\subseteq V\setminus\{r_0\} and X\cap T\ne\varnothing, and suppose \varrho_D(v)\ge\delta_D(v) for every v\in V\setminus(T\cup\{r_0\}). Then D contains k pairwise arc-disjoint arborescences rooted at r_0, each containing every vertex of T.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every root-avoiding set meeting the terminal set has at least k entering arcs, and each nonterminal nonroot vertex has indegree at least its outdegree, then there are k pairwise arc-disjoint arborescences rooted at r0, each of which contains all terminals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\text{ }k\text{ pairwise arc-disjoint }r_0\text{-arborescences }F_1,\ldots,F_k\text{ such that }T\subseteq V(F_i)\ \forall i.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong disjoint rooted-arborescences theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut characterization for distinct-root arborescences, each spanning all terminals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let D=(V,A), where V is partitioned into R=\{r_1,\ldots,r_k\} and T=V\setminus R, and suppose no arc enters R. There exist pairwise arc-disjoint arborescences F_1,\ldots,F_k such that F_i is rooted at r_i and spans T\cup\{r_i\} for every i if and only if \varrho_D(X)\ge |R\setminus X| for every X\subseteq V with X\cap T\neq\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When no edge enters the distinct roots, one arborescence from each root can be packed so that every arborescence spans all terminals exactly when each set containing a terminal has at least one entering edge for every root outside that set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\text{ pairwise arc-disjoint }F_i\text{ rooted at }r_i\text{ spanning }T\cup\{r_i\}\iff \forall X\subseteq V\ (X\cap T\neq\varnothing\Rightarrow\varrho_D(X)\ge |R\setminus X|).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partition characterization for bounded root outdegree
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The deletion is restricted to arcs leaving \(r_0\); \(\varrho_{D-r_0}(X_i)\) denotes the indegree of \(X_i\) in the digraph obtained by deleting the root.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be rooted \(k\)-edge-connected from \(r_0\). Let \(\gamma\ge k\) be an integer and \(f:V\setminus\{r_0\}\to\mathbb Z_+\), and suppose that the number of parallel \(r_0v\)-arcs is at least \(f(v)\) for every \(v\ne r_0\). Some arcs leaving \(r_0\) can be deleted so that the resulting digraph \(\widehat D\) remains rooted \(k\)-edge-connected, still has at least \(f(v)\) parallel \(r_0v\)-arcs for every \(v\ne r_0\), and satisfies \(\delta_{\widehat D}(r_0)\le\gamma\), if and only if \(\widetilde f(V\setminus\{r_0\})\le\gamma\) and, for every partition \(\{X_0,X_1,\ldots,X_t\}\) of \(V\setminus\{r_0\}\) with \(t\ge1\), with only \(X_0\) allowed to be empty, \[\widetilde f(X_0)+kt-\sum_{i=1}^t\varrho_{D-r_0}(X_i)\le\gamma.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Root-outgoing arcs can be deleted while preserving rooted k-edge-connectivity, all prescribed lower bounds on parallel root-to-vertex arcs, and root outdegree at most gamma exactly when the total lower bound is at most gamma and the stated inequality holds for every admissible partition of the nonroot vertices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}&\exists\widehat D\text{ obtained by deleting arcs leaving }r_0:\ \widehat D\text{ is rooted }k\text{-edge-connected},\ |A_{\widehat D}(r_0,v)|\ge f(v),\ \delta_{\widehat D}(r_0)\le\gamma\\&\iff \widetilde f(V\setminus\{r_0\})\le\gamma\ \land\ \left(\forall\{X_0,\ldots,X_t\}\right)\left[\widetilde f(X_0)+kt-\sum_{i=1}^t\varrho_{D-r_0}(X_i)\le\gamma\right].\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Disjoint arborescences with prescribed root sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subpartition characterization when each packed arborescence must choose its root from a specified vertex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $D=(V,A)$ be a digraph and let $R_1,\ldots,R_k\subseteq V$. There exist disjoint arborescences $B_1,\ldots,B_k$, where $B_i$ has its root in $R_i$ for $i=1,\ldots,k$, if and only if, for every subpartition $\mathcal P$ of $V$ with nonempty classes, $$\sum_{U\in\mathcal P}\bigl(k-d^{\mathrm{in}}(U)\bigr)\le \left|\left\{i\mid R_i\cap\bigcup\mathcal P\ne\varnothing\right\}\right|.$$
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Disjoint arborescences can be chosen so that the root of the ith arborescence lies in its prescribed set Ri if and only if every subpartition satisfies the stated inequality comparing aggregate in-cut deficits with the number of eligible root sets meeting the union of its classes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\text{ disjoint arborescences }B_1,\ldots,B_k\text{ with }\operatorname{root}(B_i)\in R_i\ \forall i\iff \sum_{U\in\mathcal P}(k-d^{\mathrm{in}}(U))\le \left|\{i:R_i\cap\bigcup\mathcal P\ne\varnothing\}\right|\ \forall\mathcal P\text{ subpartitioning }V\text{ into nonempty classes.}

knowledge_statements.title: Common-Root Arborescence Packing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Edmonds cut characterization for arc-disjoint spanning out-arborescences with one prescribed root.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a finite digraph, let \(r\in V\), and let \(k\ge 1\). There exist \(k\) pairwise arc-disjoint spanning out-arborescences rooted at \(r\) if and only if \(\lvert\delta_D^-(X)\rvert\ge k\) for every nonempty set \(X\subseteq V\setminus\{r\}\), where \(\delta_D^-(X)\) is the set of arcs entering \(X\) from \(V\setminus X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: There are k arc-disjoint spanning out-arborescences rooted at r exactly when every nonempty set excluding r has at least k entering arcs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\ k\text{ arc-disjoint spanning }r\text{-out-arborescences}\iff \lvert\delta_D^-(X)\rvert\ge k\quad\forall\varnothing\ne X\subseteq V\setminus\{r\}.\)

notation.meaning: Arcs entering X from its complement.

knowledge_statements.title: Prescribed Multiple-Root Packings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arc-disjoint spanning out-arborescences with an ordered, possibly repeated root prescription.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a finite digraph and let \((r_1,\ldots,r_k)\in V^k\), with repetitions allowed. There exist pairwise arc-disjoint spanning out-arborescences \(T_1,\ldots,T_k\), where \(T_i\) is rooted at \(r_i\), if and only if every nonempty \(X\subseteq V\) satisfies \(\lvert\delta_D^-(X)\rvert\ge \lvert\{i:r_i\notin X\}\rvert\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arborescences with prescribed, possibly repeated roots can be packed exactly when every vertex set receives enough arcs for the roots outside it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\,(T_i)_{i=1}^k\text{ as prescribed}\iff \lvert\delta_D^-(X)\rvert\ge\lvert\{i:r_i\notin X\}\rvert\quad\forall\varnothing\ne X\subseteq V.\)

knowledge_statements.title: Designated Root-Set Packings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Packing whose selected roots must belong to a fixed designated vertex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\), let \(R\subseteq V\), and let \(k\ge 1\). An \(R\)-designated packing of size \(k\) is a family of pairwise arc-disjoint spanning out-arborescences \((T_1,\ldots,T_k)\) together with roots \((r_1,\ldots,r_k)\in R^k\), such that \(T_i\) is rooted at \(r_i\) for every \(i\). Root repetitions are permitted unless distinctness is imposed separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A designated-root-set packing consists of arc-disjoint spanning arborescences whose chosen roots all lie in a specified vertex set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((T_i,r_i)_{i=1}^k\text{ is designated}\iff r_i\in R\text{ and }T_i\text{ is a spanning }r_i\text{-out-arborescence, pairwise arc-disjoint}.\)

knowledge_statements.title: Flexible Root-Location Packings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Root locations are selected jointly with the arborescences from an admissible family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\), let \(k\ge 1\), and let \(\mathcal R\subseteq V^k\) be a family of admissible ordered root tuples. A flexible root-location packing is a tuple \(((r_1,\ldots,r_k),T_1,\ldots,T_k)\) such that \((r_1,\ldots,r_k)\in\mathcal R\), each \(T_i\) is a spanning out-arborescence rooted at \(r_i\), and the arc sets \(A(T_1),\ldots,A(T_k)\) are pairwise disjoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A flexible packing chooses an admissible root tuple and simultaneously packs one spanning out-arborescence from each chosen root.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((r_1,\ldots,r_k)\in\mathcal R,\quad T_i\text{ is rooted at }r_i,\quad A(T_i)\cap A(T_j)=\varnothing\text{ for }i\ne j.\)

knowledge_statements.title: Root-Selection Feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut feasibility condition for selecting an admissible root tuple before packing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\), let \(k\ge1\), and let \(\mathcal R\subseteq V^k\). A flexible root-location packing exists if and only if there is a tuple \((r_1,\ldots,r_k)\in\mathcal R\) such that \(\lvert\delta_D^-(X)\rvert\ge\lvert\{i:r_i\notin X\}\rvert\) for every nonempty \(X\subseteq V\). Thus root selection is feasible precisely when some admissible tuple satisfies all multiple-root cut inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Root selection is feasible exactly when some admissible root tuple satisfies every entering-cut requirement induced by roots outside each set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\text{ flexible packing}\iff\exists(r_1,\ldots,r_k)\in\mathcal R\;\forall\varnothing\ne X\subseteq V,\ \lvert\delta_D^-(X)\rvert\ge\lvert\{i:r_i\notin X\}\rvert.\)

knowledge_statements.title: Capacitated Arborescence Packing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integral-capacity extension of the common-root arborescence-packing theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\), let \(r\in V\), let \(k\ge1\), and assign each arc an integral capacity \(u(a)\ge0\). There exist \(k\) spanning out-arborescences rooted at \(r\), with every arc \(a\) used by at most \(u(a)\) members of the family, if and only if \(u(\delta_D^-(X))\ge k\) for every nonempty \(X\subseteq V\setminus\{r\}\), where \(u(F)=\sum_{a\in F}u(a)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A capacitated digraph supports k rooted spanning arborescences exactly when every cut excluding the root has total entering capacity at least k.
assumptions_latex: \(D=(V,A)\) is a finite digraph and \(r\in V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\text{ a capacity-respecting family of }k\text{ spanning }r\text{-arborescences}\iff u(\delta_D^-(X))\ge k\quad\forall\varnothing\ne X\subseteq V\setminus\{r\}.\)

notation.meaning: Sum of integral arc capacities over F.
Arcs entering X from its complement.

knowledge_statements.title: Matroid-Based Arborescence Packing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matroid-basic packing with root labels placed at vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\), let \(S\) be a finite set of root labels, let \(\pi:S\to V\), and let \(M\) be a matroid on \(S\). An \(M\)-basic arborescence packing is a pairwise arc-disjoint family \((T_s:s\in S)\) in which \(T_s\) is an out-arborescence rooted at \(\pi(s)\), and for every \(v\in V\), the set \(\{s\in S:v\in V(T_s)\}\) is a base of \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matroid-basic packing uses placed root labels and requires the arborescences containing each vertex to be indexed by a matroid base.
assumptions_latex: \(\pi:S\to V\) and \(M\) is a matroid on \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A(T_s)\cap A(T_t)=\varnothing\text{ for }s\ne t,\qquad \{s:v\in V(T_s)\}\text{ is a base of }M\text{ for every }v\in V.\)

notation.meaning: Placement mapping from root labels to vertices.
Matroid governing local coverage by root labels.
Out-arborescence indexed by root label s.

children.title: Directed-Hypergraph Arborescence Packing

knowledge_statements.title: Directed-Hypergraph Arborescence Packing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trimming-based definition for packing rooted spanning directed hyperarborescences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A directed hypergraph has hyperarcs \(e=(T_e,h_e)\) with nonempty tail \(T_e\subseteq V\) and head \(h_e\in V\setminus T_e\). A set \(F\) of hyperarcs is a spanning out-hyperarborescence rooted at \(r\) if one can select \(t_e\in T_e\) for each \(e\in F\) so that the arcs \((t_e,h_e)\) form a spanning out-arborescence rooted at \(r\). A packing is a family of such hyperarborescences having pairwise disjoint hyperarc sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the trimming convention, packed hyperarborescences are hyperarc-disjoint families that can each be trimmed to a rooted spanning out-arborescence.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) and the directed-hyperarc family are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\text{ is an }r\text{-hyperarborescence}\iff\exists(t_e\in T_e:e\in F)\text{ whose trimmed arcs form a spanning }r\text{-out-arborescence}.\)

notation.meaning: Tail set of directed hyperarc e.
Head vertex of directed hyperarc e.
Tail vertex selected when trimming e.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The trimming-based definition is coherent, but directed-hypergraph arborescences use convention-dependent notions and no source is supplied. An authoritative source with a specific definition or section locator is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rooted Directed-Hypergraph Decomposition Criterion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut characterization for decomposing a directed hypergraph into edge-disjoint spanning rooted connected factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let D=(V,\mathcal A) be a directed hypergraph whose every directed hyperedge has at least two elements, and let r_0\in V. Then D can be decomposed into k edge-disjoint spanning rooted k-edge-connected directed hypergraphs if and only if \varrho_D(X)\ge k for every nonempty X\subseteq V\setminus\{r_0\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every directed hyperedge has at least two elements, then the directed hypergraph admits the stated decomposition into k edge-disjoint spanning rooted k-edge-connected directed hypergraphs exactly when every nonempty set avoiding the root has at least k entering hyperedges.
assumptions_latex: D=(V,\mathcal A)\text{ is a directed hypergraph}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D\text{ has the stated decomposition}\iff \forall\varnothing\ne X\subseteq V\setminus\{r_0\},\ \varrho_D(X)\ge k.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Entrance of a Vertex Set

knowledge_statements.title: Disjoint Branchings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Edmonds cut characterization for arc-disjoint spanning branchings with prescribed root sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a finite digraph and let \(R_1,\ldots,R_k\) be nonempty subsets of \(V\). There exist pairwise arc-disjoint spanning branchings \(B_1,\ldots,B_k\), with the root set of \(B_i\) equal to \(R_i\), if and only if every nonempty \(X\subseteq V\) satisfies \(\lvert\delta_D^-(X)\rvert\ge\lvert\{i:R_i\cap X=\varnothing\}\rvert\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prescribed-root-set branchings can be packed exactly when every vertex set receives one entering arc for each branching having no root inside it.
assumptions_latex: \(R_i\subseteq V\) is nonempty for \(1\le i\le k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\text{ arc-disjoint spanning }R_i\text{-branchings }B_i\iff \lvert\delta_D^-(X)\rvert\ge\lvert\{i:R_i\cap X=\varnothing\}\rvert\quad\forall\varnothing\ne X\subseteq V.\)

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a digraph and let \(R_1,\ldots,R_k\subseteq V\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Root-multiplicity arborescence packing theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut characterization for packing terminal-spanning arborescences with prescribed multiplicities at the roots.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let D=(V,A), where V is partitioned into R and T=V\setminus R, and suppose no arc enters R. Let m:R\to\mathbf Z_+ and k=\widetilde m(R)=\sum_{r\in R}m(r). There exist k pairwise arc-disjoint arborescences such that, for every r\in R, exactly m(r) are rooted at r and span T\cup\{r\}, if and only if \varrho_D(X)\ge\widetilde m(R\setminus X) for every X\subseteq V with X\cap T\neq\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With prescribed root multiplicities and no edge entering the root set, the required terminal-spanning arborescences can be packed exactly when every set containing a terminal has at least the total prescribed multiplicity of the roots lying outside it in entering edges.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\ k\text{ pairwise arc-disjoint arborescences with }m(r)\text{ rooted at each }r\text{ and spanning }T\cup\{r\}\iff \forall X\subseteq V\ (X\cap T\neq\varnothing\Rightarrow\varrho_D(X)\ge\widetilde m(R\setminus X)).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Maximal Root-Set Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reachability-maximal branching for a prescribed nonempty root set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $D=(V,A)$ be a digraph and let $\varnothing\ne R\subseteq V$. A maximal $R$-branching is a branching $B$ whose vertex set is $\operatorname{Reach}_D(R)$, the set of vertices reachable from $R$ in $D$, and whose root set is $R$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonempty vertex set R, a maximal R-branching is a branching rooted exactly at R that contains precisely all vertices reachable from R in the ambient digraph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B\text{ is a maximal }R\text{-branching}\iff V(B)=\operatorname{Reach}_D(R)\ \land\ \operatorname{Roots}(B)=R

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strongly polynomial capacitated fixed-root packing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strongly polynomial optimization of total integer multiplicity under integral arc capacities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a digraph $D=(V,A)$, a root $r\in V$, and a capacity function $c:A\to\mathbb Z_+$, one can find a finite family of $r$-arborescences $B_1,\ldots,B_k$ and integers $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_k\ge0$ such that
\[
\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i\chi^{B_i}\le c,
\]
with $\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i$ maximized, in strongly polynomial time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For integral arc capacities and a prescribed root, a maximum-total-integer-multiplicity packing of rooted arborescences respecting all arc capacities can be found in strongly polynomial time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max\left\{\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i:\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i\chi^{B_i}\le c\right\}\text{ and an attaining capacitated packing can be found in strongly polynomial time}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subpartition criterion for disjoint arborescences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes the existence of k disjoint arborescences by incoming-cut inequalities over all subpartitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \text{Let }D=(V,A)\text{ be a digraph and }k\in\mathbb Z_+.\text{ Then }A\text{ contains }k\text{ disjoint arborescences if and only if }\sum_{U\in\mathcal P}d^{\mathrm{in}}(U)\ge k(|\mathcal P|-1)\text{ for every subpartition }\mathcal P\text{ of }V\text{ with nonempty classes.}
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A digraph contains k disjoint arborescences exactly when, for every subpartition into nonempty classes, the sum of the classes' incoming-cut sizes is at least k times one less than the number of classes.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal P\text{ ranges over subpartitions of }V\text{ with nonempty classes.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A\text{ contains }k\text{ disjoint arborescences}\iff \forall\mathcal P,\ \sum_{U\in\mathcal P}d^{\mathrm{in}}(U)\ge k(|\mathcal P|-1).

knowledge_statements.title: Covering by Branchings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arc covering, with decomposition reserved for pairwise disjoint covering branchings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a finite digraph. A branching cover of \(D\) is a family \(B_1,\ldots,B_k\) of branchings contained in \(D\) such that \(A=\bigcup_{i=1}^k A(B_i)\). Its size is \(k\). It is a branching decomposition when the sets \(A(B_i)\) are pairwise disjoint; equivalently, every arc of \(D\) belongs to exactly one member of the family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A branching cover contains every arc in at least one branching; it is a decomposition when each arc belongs to exactly one branching.
assumptions_latex: Each \(B_i\) is a branching contained in \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A=\bigcup_{i=1}^k A(B_i),\qquad \text{and for a decomposition }A(B_i)\cap A(B_j)=\varnothing\text{ whenever }i\ne j.\)

notation.meaning: The i-th branching in the cover.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient conditions for decomposing all arcs of a digraph among at most k branchings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a digraph and \(k\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\). The arc set \(A\) can be covered by \(k\) branchings if and only if \(\varrho_D(v)\le k\) for every \(v\in V\) and \(i_D(X)\le k(|X|-1)\) for every nonempty \(X\subseteq V\), where \(i_D(X)\) is the number of arcs with both endpoints in \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A digraph's arcs can be covered by k branchings exactly when every vertex has indegree at most k and every nonempty vertex subset induces at most k(|X|−1) arcs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A\text{ is coverable by }k\text{ branchings}\iff\bigl[\forall v\in V,\ \varrho_D(v)\le k\bigr]\land\bigl[\forall\varnothing\ne X\subseteq V,\ i_D(X)\le k(|X|-1)\bigr]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Laminar characterization of covering by arborescences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient condition for covering every arc by a prescribed number of arborescences with unrestricted roots.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $D=(V,A)$ be a digraph and $k\in\mathbb Z_+$. Then $A$ can be covered by $k$ arborescences if and only if, for every laminar family $(V_1,\ldots,V_t)$ of nonempty subsets of $V$ such that no arc enters more than one $V_i$,
\[
k\bigl(|V|-1+\lambda\bigr)\ge |A|+\sum_{i=1}^t\bigl(k-d^{\mathrm{in}}(V_i)\bigr),
\]
where $\lambda$ is the maximum cardinality of a subfamily having nonempty common intersection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The arcs of a digraph can be covered by k arborescences exactly when the stated inequality holds for every qualifying laminar family; lambda is the largest number of its members having a common point.
assumptions_latex: (V_1,\ldots,V_t)\text{ is a laminar family of nonempty subsets of }V
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A\text{ is coverable by }k\text{ arborescences}\iff k(|V|-1+\lambda)\ge |A|+\sum_{i=1}^t(k-d^{\mathrm{in}}(V_i))\text{ for every such family}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equitable Covering by Branchings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Balances the cardinalities of the branchings in an arc cover.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Root-set reassignment in a two-branching decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes when arcs partitioned by two branchings can be repartitioned into branchings with prescribed root sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \text{Let }B_1,B_2\text{ be branchings partitioning }A\text{ in }D=(V,A).\text{ Let }R_1,R_2\text{ satisfy }R_1\cup R_2=R(B_1)\cup R(B_2)\text{ and }R_1\cap R_2=R(B_1)\cap R(B_2).\text{ Then }A\text{ can be split into branchings }B'_1,B'_2\text{ with }R(B'_i)=R_i\ (i=1,2)\text{ if and only if every strong component }K\text{ of }D\text{ with }d^{\mathrm{in}}(K)=0\text{ intersects both }R_1\text{ and }R_2.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given a partition of the arcs into two branchings and compatible prescribed root sets, the arcs can be repartitioned into branchings with those root sets exactly when every source strong component meets both prescribed root sets.
assumptions_latex: B_1\text{ and }B_2\text{ are branchings that partition }A.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl(\exists B'_1,B'_2\text{ partitioning }A:\ R(B'_i)=R_i\text{ for }i=1,2\bigr)\iff\bigl(\forall K\text{ a strong component with }d^{\mathrm{in}}(K)=0,\ K\cap R_1\ne\varnothing\text{ and }K\cap R_2\ne\varnothing\bigr).

knowledge_statements.title: Covering by Rooted Arborescences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arc covering by spanning out-arborescences having a prescribed common root.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a finite digraph and let \(r\in V\). An \(r\)-rooted arborescence cover is a family \(T_1,\ldots,T_k\) of spanning out-arborescences rooted at \(r\) such that \(A=\bigcup_{i=1}^k A(T_i)\). It is an \(r\)-rooted arborescence decomposition when the sets \(A(T_i)\) are pairwise disjoint, so every arc belongs to exactly one rooted arborescence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rooted-arborescence cover covers every arc by spanning out-arborescences with the prescribed root; a decomposition assigns every arc exactly once.
assumptions_latex: \(D=(V,A)\) is a finite digraph and \(r\in V\).
Each \(T_i\) is a spanning out-arborescence rooted at \(r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A=\bigcup_{i=1}^k A(T_i),\qquad \text{and for a decomposition }A(T_i)\cap A(T_j)=\varnothing\text{ whenever }i\ne j.\)

notation.meaning: Prescribed common root.
The i-th spanning rooted out-arborescence.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Arc-Partition Criterion for T-Intersecting Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes when the arc set can be partitioned into parts covering multiple set families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a digraph and let \(T\subseteq V\) contain the head of every arc of \(D\). Let \(\mathcal F_1,\ldots,\mathcal F_k\) be \(T\)-intersecting families such that, for all \(i,j\), \[X\in\mathcal F_i,\ Y\in\mathcal F_j,\ X\cap Y\cap T\neq\varnothing\ \Longrightarrow\ X\cap Y\in\mathcal F_i\cap\mathcal F_j.\] Then \(A\) can be partitioned into \(A_1,\ldots,A_k\) so that \(A_i\) covers \(\mathcal F_i\) for every \(i\) if and only if \[\varrho_D(X)\ge p_1(X)\qquad\text{for every nonempty }X\subseteq V,\] where \(p_1(X)=|\{i:X\in\mathcal F_i\}|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Suppose T contains the head of every arc, the families F_i are T-intersecting, and intersections on T satisfy the stated mixed-family closure property. The arcs can be partitioned into parts A_i that respectively cover F_i exactly when every nonempty vertex set X has at least as many entering arcs as there are families F_i containing X.
assumptions_latex: T\subseteq V\text{ contains the head of every arc of }D
X\in\mathcal F_i,\ Y\in\mathcal F_j,\ X\cap Y\cap T\neq\varnothing\Rightarrow X\cap Y\in\mathcal F_i\cap\mathcal F_j
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl(\exists\,A=A_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}A_k:\ A_i\text{ covers }\mathcal F_i\ \forall i\bigr)\iff\bigl(\varrho_D(X)\ge p_1(X)\ \forall\varnothing\neq X\subseteq V\bigr)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Root vector of an arborescence packing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The arborescences are spanning and pairwise edge-disjoint, while their roots may differ.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a digraph on vertex set \(V\) and an integer \(k\), a vector \(z:V\to\{0,1,\ldots,k\}\) is a root vector if there exist \(k\) pairwise edge-disjoint spanning arborescences such that each \(v\in V\) is the root of exactly \(z(v)\) of them.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A root vector records, for a packing of k edge-disjoint spanning arborescences, how many of those arborescences are rooted at each vertex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z\text{ is a root vector}\iff \exists\text{ }k\text{ pairwise edge-disjoint spanning arborescences with exactly }z(v)\text{ rooted at each }v\in V

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subset-Rank Criterion for Covering by Rooted Arborescences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes a rooted-arborescence cover using the maximum intersection of one rooted arborescence with each arc subset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let D=(V,A) be a digraph, r\in V, and k\in\mathbb Z_{+}. For each A'\subseteq A, define s(A')=\max\{|B\cap A'|:B\text{ is an }r\text{-arborescence}\}. Then A can be covered by k r-arborescences if and only if k\,s(A')\geq |A'| for every A'\subseteq A.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The arcs can be covered by k arborescences rooted at r exactly when, for every arc subset, k times the largest intersection of that subset with one r-arborescence is at least the subset's cardinality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A\text{ is coverable by }k\ r\text{-arborescences}\iff\forall A'\subseteq A,\ k\,s(A')\geq |A'|
