knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mixed Intersecting-Family Edge-Cover Partition Characterization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes when separate edge classes can cover distinct intersecting set families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\), and let \(\mathcal F_1,\ldots,\mathcal F_k\) be intersecting families satisfying \(X\in\mathcal F_i,\ Y\in\mathcal F_j,\ X\cap Y\ne\varnothing\Rightarrow X\cap Y\in\mathcal F_i\cap\mathcal F_j\). Define \(p_1(X)=|\{i:X\in\mathcal F_i\}|\). Then \(A\) can be partitioned as \(A=A_1\dot\cup\cdots\dot\cup A_k\), with \(A_i\) covering \(\mathcal F_i\) for every \(i\), if and only if \(\varrho_D(X)\ge p_1(X)\) for every nonempty \(X\subseteq V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For intersecting set families satisfying the mixed intersection property, the edges can be partitioned so that class i covers family i exactly when every nonempty vertex set has at least as many entering edges as the number of families containing it.
assumptions_latex: X\in\mathcal F_i,\ Y\in\mathcal F_j,\ X\cap Y\ne\varnothing\Rightarrow X\cap Y\in\mathcal F_i\cap\mathcal F_j.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl[\exists A_1,\ldots,A_k:\ A=\dot\bigcup_{i=1}^k A_i\ \land\ (\forall i)\ A_i\text{ covers }\mathcal F_i\bigr]\iff\bigl[(\forall\varnothing\ne X\subseteq V)\ \varrho_D(X)\ge p_1(X)\bigr].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local-Connectivity Coverage by Edge-Disjoint Rooted Arborescences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence of a rooted arborescence family whose vertex coverage matches truncated local root-connectivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let D=(V,A) be a digraph with root r_0, let k\ge1, and define T'=\{x\in V\setminus\{r_0\}:\varrho_D(x)<\delta_D(x)\}. If \lambda_D(r_0,x)\ge k for every x\in T', then there is a family \mathcal F of k pairwise edge-disjoint arborescences rooted at r_0 such that every x\in V belongs to at least r(x):=\min\{k,\lambda_D(r_0,x)\} members of \mathcal F.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every vertex whose indegree is smaller than its outdegree has root-to-vertex edge-connectivity at least k, then k edge-disjoint arborescences rooted at r0 exist so that each vertex occurs in at least the smaller of k and its local connectivity from r0 of them.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\mathcal F,\ |\mathcal F|=k,\ \mathcal F\text{ pairwise edge-disjoint and rooted at }r_0,\quad |\{F\in\mathcal F:x\in V(F)\}|\ge\min\{k,\lambda_D(r_0,x)\}\ \forall x\in V.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reachability and Convex Vertex Sets in a Digraph
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines reachability between disjoint vertex sets and the associated directed-graph convexity notion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\). For disjoint \(X,Y\subseteq V\), \(Y\) is reachable from \(X\) if a directed path has its first vertex in \(X\) and its last vertex in \(Y\). A set \(U\subseteq V\) is convex if there is no \(v\in V\setminus U\) such that \(U\) is reachable from \(\{v\}\) and \(\{v\}\) is reachable from \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For disjoint vertex sets X and Y, Y is reachable from X when a directed path starts in X and ends in Y. A vertex set U is convex when no vertex outside U can both reach U and be reached from U.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U\text{ is convex}\iff\nexists v\in V\setminus U:\ U\text{ is reachable from }\{v\}\text{ and }\{v\}\text{ is reachable from }U

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Covering a Digraph by Fixed-Root Spanning Arborescences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient indegree and entrance conditions for covering all arcs by k spanning arborescences with a prescribed root.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\), let \(r_0\in V\) have no entering arc, and let \(k\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\). The arc set \(A\) can be covered by \(k\) spanning arborescences rooted at \(r_0\) if and only if \[\varrho_D(v)\le k\quad(v\in V\setminus\{r_0\})\] and \[k-\varrho_D(X)\le\sum_{v\in\Gamma^-(X)}\bigl(k-\varrho_D(v)\bigr)\quad\text{for every }X\subseteq V\setminus\{r_0\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All arcs can be covered by k spanning arborescences with root r0 exactly when every nonroot vertex has indegree at most k and every subset of nonroot vertices satisfies the stated entrance-deficiency inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A\text{ is coverable by }k\text{ spanning }r_0\text{-arborescences}\iff\left[\forall v\ne r_0,\ \varrho_D(v)\le k\right]\land\left[\forall X\subseteq V\setminus\{r_0\},\ k-\varrho_D(X)\le\sum_{v\in\Gamma^-(X)}(k-\varrho_D(v))\right]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rooted-Arborescence Covering Criterion for Acyclic Digraphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specializes rooted-arborescence covering to acyclic digraphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let D=(V,A) be an acyclic digraph, r\in V, and let k be a positive integer. Then A can be covered by k r-arborescences if and only if r is the only source of D and every vertex has indegree at most k.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an acyclic digraph, all arcs can be covered by k arborescences rooted at r exactly when r is the only source and every vertex has indegree at most k.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A\text{ is coverable by }k\ r\text{-arborescences}\iff\left[r\text{ is the unique source of }D\ \land\ \forall v\in V,\ \deg^{\mathrm{in}}(v)\leq k\right]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Supermodularity of Bi-Set Family Multiplicity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the crossing supermodularity inequality for the multiplicity induced by mixed-intersecting bi-set families, including its strict case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p_2(X)=|\{i:X\in\mathcal F_i\}|\) for bi-set families satisfying the mixed intersection property. If \(p_2(X)>0\), \(p_2(Y)>0\), and \(X_I\cap Y_I\ne\varnothing\), then \[p_2(X)+p_2(Y)\le p_2(X\sqcap Y)+p_2(X\sqcup Y).\] If some \(\mathcal F_i\) contains \(X\sqcap Y\) but contains neither \(X\) nor \(Y\), the inequality is strict.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The multiplicity of mixed-intersecting bi-set families is supermodular on pairs with positive multiplicity and overlapping inner sets. The inequality is strict when some family contains the intersection but neither original bi-set.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal F_1,\ldots,\mathcal F_k\text{ satisfy the mixed intersection property}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_2(X)+p_2(Y)\le p_2(X\sqcap Y)+p_2(X\sqcup Y),\quad \bigl[\exists i:\ X\sqcap Y\in\mathcal F_i,\ X,Y\notin\mathcal F_i\bigr]\Rightarrow\text{strict inequality}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fujishige's Criterion for Disjoint Arborescences Spanning Convex Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes the existence of edge-disjoint rooted arborescences spanning prescribed convex vertex sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a directed graph, let \(r_1,\ldots,r_k\in V\) be a list of roots that need not be distinct, and let \(U_i\subseteq V\) be convex with \(r_i\in U_i\). There exist edge-disjoint \(r_i\)-arborescences \(A_i\) spanning \(U_i\), for \(i=1,\ldots,k\), if and only if \[\varrho_D(Z)\ge p_1(Z)\qquad\text{for every }Z\subseteq V,\] where \[p_1(Z)=|\{i:U_i\cap Z\neq\varnothing\text{ and }r_i\notin Z\}|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given possibly repeated roots r_i and convex sets U_i containing their respective roots, edge-disjoint r_i-arborescences spanning the U_i exist exactly when every vertex subset Z has at least as many entering edges as the number of prescribed sets U_i that meet Z while their root lies outside Z.
assumptions_latex: U_i\subseteq V\text{ is convex and }r_i\in U_i\quad(i=1,\ldots,k)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl(\exists\text{ edge-disjoint }r_i\text{-arborescences }A_i\text{ spanning }U_i\ \forall i\bigr)\iff\bigl(\varrho_D(Z)\ge |\{i:U_i\cap Z\neq\varnothing,\ r_i\notin Z\}|\ \forall Z\subseteq V\bigr)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounded edge-multiplicity criterion for rooted arborescence families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient inequalities for lower and upper edge multiplicities across k spanning arborescences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r_0\) be a root of \(D=(V,A)\), with no edge entering \(r_0\). Let \(f:A\to\{0,1,\ldots,k\}\) and \(g':A\to\mathbb Z_+\cup\{\infty\}\) satisfy \(f\le g'\). Put \(g=g'-f\) and \(g_V(v)=k-\varrho_f(v)\) for \(v\in V-\{r_0\}\). There exist \(k\) spanning arborescences rooted at \(r_0\) such that every edge \(e\) belongs to at least \(f(e)\) and at most \(g'(e)\) of them if and only if \(g_V\ge0\) and
\[
k-\varrho_f(Z)\le\widetilde g_V(Y)+\sum_{e\in A(V-Z,Z-Y)}g(e)
\]
for every \(Y\subseteq Z\subseteq V-\{r_0\}\) with \(Z\ne\varnothing\). If \(g'\equiv\infty\), this reduces to
\[
k-\varrho_f(Z)\le\widetilde g_V(\Gamma^-(Z))
\]
for every nonempty \(Z\subseteq V-\{r_0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: There are k root-prescribed spanning arborescences realizing the given lower and upper edge-multiplicity bounds exactly when the residual vertex requirements are nonnegative and every nested pair Y contained in nonempty Z satisfies the stated residual-capacity inequality. With no finite upper edge bounds, only the entrance-set inequalities remain.
assumptions_latex: D=(V,A)\text{ has root }r_0\text{ and no edge enters }r_0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\ k\text{ spanning }r_0\text{-arborescences with }f(e)\le m(e)\le g'(e)\ \forall e\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad g_V\ge0\text{ and }k-\varrho_f(Z)\le\widetilde g_V(Y)+\sum_{e\in A(V-Z,Z-Y)}g(e)\ \forall Y\subseteq Z\subseteq V-\{r_0\},\ Z\ne\varnothing;\text{ if }g'\equiv\infty,\text{ the condition becomes }k-\varrho_f(Z)\le\widetilde g_V(\Gamma^-(Z)).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mixed Intersection Property and Multiplicity for Bi-Set Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines mixed intersection for several bi-set families and records the induced monotonicity of their membership multiplicity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Bi-set families \(\mathcal F_1,\ldots,\mathcal F_k\) have the mixed intersection property if \(X\in\mathcal F_i,\ Y\in\mathcal F_j,\ X_I\cap Y_I\ne\varnothing\Rightarrow X\sqcap Y\in\mathcal F_i\cap\mathcal F_j\). For a bi-set \(X\), define \(p_2(X)=|\{i:X\in\mathcal F_i\}|\). Consequently, if \(X\sqsubseteq Y\), \(p_2(X)>0\), and \(p_2(Y)>0\), then \(p_2(X)\ge p_2(Y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bi-set families satisfy mixed intersection when any two members with intersecting inner sets have their bi-set intersection in both corresponding families. The number p2(X) of families containing X is then non-increasing under bi-set inclusion, provided both multiplicities are positive.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal F_1,\ldots,\mathcal F_k\text{ are families of bi-sets}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{MIP}\iff\bigl[X\in\mathcal F_i,\ Y\in\mathcal F_j,\ X_I\cap Y_I\ne\varnothing\Rightarrow X\sqcap Y\in\mathcal F_i\cap\mathcal F_j\bigr],\quad X\sqsubseteq Y,\ p_2(X),p_2(Y)>0\Rightarrow p_2(X)\ge p_2(Y).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: For \(X\subseteq V'\), \(\widetilde z(X)=\sum_{v in X}z(v)\), and \(\varrho'(X)\) is the number of arcs entering \(X\) in \(D'\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pre-flow arborescence packing with local connectivity multiplicities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The arborescences share root \(r_0\), are pairwise edge-disjoint, and need not contain every vertex individually.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a pre-flow digraph rooted at \(r_0\). For every integer \(k\ge1\), there exists a family \(\mathcal F\) of \(k\) pairwise edge-disjoint arborescences rooted at \(r_0\) such that every \(v\in V\) belongs to exactly \(\min\{k,\lambda(r_0,v)\}\) members of \(\mathcal F\). In particular, for \(k=\max\{\lambda(r_0,v):v\in V\setminus\{r_0\}\}\), every \(v\) belongs to exactly \(\lambda(r_0,v)\) members.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For any positive integer k, a rooted pre-flow digraph has k edge-disjoint rooted arborescences whose coverage multiplicity at each vertex equals the smaller of k and that vertex's local edge-connectivity from the root. Choosing k as the maximum such connectivity realizes every local connectivity exactly.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\mathcal F,\ |\mathcal F|=k:\ \mathcal F\text{ consists of pairwise edge-disjoint }r_0\text{-arborescences and }(\forall v\in V)\ |\{F\in\mathcal F:v\in V(F)\}|=\min\{k,\lambda(r_0,v)\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Disjoint-Subpartition Criterion for Arborescence Packing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes packing of spanning arborescences without prescribing a common root.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Root-vector-bounded arborescence packing criterion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes feasibility of an edge-disjoint spanning-arborescence packing subject to lower and upper root-multiplicity bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $f:V^*\to\mathbb Z_+$ and $g:V^*\to\mathbb Z_+\cup\{\infty\}$ satisfy $f\le g$. A digraph $D^*=(V^*,A^*)$ contains $k$ edge-disjoint spanning arborescences whose root vector $z$ satisfies $f\le z\le g$ if and only if $\widetilde f(V^*)\le k$, every partition $\{X_0,X_1,\ldots,X_t\}$ of $V^*$ with $t\ge1$ and only $X_0$ possibly empty satisfies $\sum_{i=1}^t\varrho_{D^*}(X_i)\ge k(t-1)+\widetilde f(X_0)$, and every $\varnothing\subset X\subseteq V^*$ satisfies $\widetilde g(X)\ge k-\varrho_{D^*}(X)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A digraph has k edge-disjoint spanning arborescences with root multiplicities between f and g exactly when the total lower bound, every specified partition inequality, and every upper-bound cut inequality hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\text{ $k$ edge-disjoint spanning arborescences with }f\le z\le g\iff\begin{cases}\widetilde f(V^*)\le k,\\ \sum_{i=1}^t\varrho_{D^*}(X_i)\ge k(t-1)+\widetilde f(X_0)\text{ for every admissible partition},\\ \widetilde g(X)\ge k-\varrho_{D^*}(X)\text{ for every }\varnothing\subset X\subseteq V^*.\end{cases}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(I_1=\cdots=I_k=\varnothing\). For the current independent partition, construct the standard matroid-partition exchange digraph \(H_I\): its arcs encode moving an element between parts while preserving independence, and its sources are unused elements insertable into some part. If an augmenting path exists, perform its exchanges and increase \(\sum_i|I_i|\) by one. Otherwise stop and output \((I_1,\ldots,I_k)\). For graphic matroids, each \(I_i\) is a forest; size \(k(|V|-1)\) forces every part to be a spanning tree.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a prescribed root \(r\) and integer \(k\), minimum-cost packing of \(k\) arc-disjoint spanning out-arborescences is solvable in polynomial time through branching-packing or equivalent cut-based algorithms. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Union Closure of Intersecting Tight Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two closure rules for tight sets in the splitting-off setting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If $X$ and $Y$ are tight sets with $|X\cap Y|\ge 2$, then $X\cup Y$ is tight. If $X_1,X_2,X_3$ are tight sets such that $X_1\cap X_2\cap X_3=\varnothing$ and $|X_i\cap X_j|=1$ for every $1\le i<j\le 3$, then $X_1\cup X_2\cup X_3$ is tight.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The union of two tight sets sharing at least two elements is tight. Also, the union of three tight sets is tight when their triple intersection is empty and every pair intersects in exactly one element.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X\cup Y\text{ is tight, and respectively }X_1\cup X_2\cup X_3\text{ is tight}

children.title: Undirected Splitting-Off
children.top_down_role: Connectivity-preserving local reductions in undirected graphs.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local edge-connectivity and splittable edge pairs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the connectivity quantity preserved by undirected splitting-off and the admissibility of a pair at a distinguished vertex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $G=(V\cup\{z\},E)$ be a connected undirected graph with $|V|\ge 2$. For $u,v\in V$, the local edge-connectivity $\lambda_G(u,v)$ is the minimum cardinality of a cut separating $u$ and $v$; equivalently, it is the maximum number of pairwise edge-disjoint $uv$-paths. A pair of edges incident with $z$ is splittable if splitting off that pair leaves $\lambda_G(u,v)$ unchanged for every $u,v\in V$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a connected undirected graph with a distinguished vertex z, the local edge-connectivity of u and v is the size of a smallest cut separating them, equivalently the maximum number of edge-disjoint u-v paths. Two edges incident with z are splittable when splitting them off preserves this quantity for every pair of other vertices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda_G(u,v)=\min\{|C|:C\text{ separates }u,v\}=\max\{r:\text{there are }r\text{ edge-disjoint }uv\text{-paths}\},\quad \{e,f\}\text{ is splittable}\iff \lambda_{G^{ef}}(u,v)=\lambda_G(u,v)\ \forall u,v\in V.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Skew supermodularity of the symmetric pair-requirement function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural lemma for the cut-requirement function used in undirected splitting-off theory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let r:V\times V\to\mathbb{R}_{+} be symmetric and define
\[
R_r(X)=\begin{cases}
0,&X\in\{\varnothing,V\},\\
\max\{r(x,y):x\in X,\ y\in V\setminus X\},&\varnothing\subset X\subset V.
\end{cases}
\]
Then, for every X,Y\subseteq V, at least one of
\[
R_r(X)+R_r(Y)\le R_r(X\cap Y)+R_r(X\cup Y)
\]
and
\[
R_r(X)+R_r(Y)\le R_r(X\setminus Y)+R_r(Y\setminus X)
\]
holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The cut function obtained by taking the maximum symmetric nonnegative pair requirement crossing each nontrivial cut is skew supermodular.
assumptions_latex: R_r(X)=0\text{ for }X\in\{\varnothing,V\}\text{ and }R_r(X)=\max\{r(x,y):x\in X,\ y\in V\setminus X\}\text{ otherwise}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_r\text{ is skew supermodular.}

assumptions_latex: The finite undirected multigraph \(G=(V\cup\{s\},E)\) has even degree at \(s\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(\lambda_G(x,y)\ge k\) for every distinct \(x,y\in V\) and \(d_G(s)\) is even. Loops created by splitting are discarded, while parallel edges are permitted.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lovász Undirected Splitting Lemma
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence of an admissible partner for each edge incident to an even-degree designated vertex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $G=(V+z,E)$ be an undirected graph, let $d_G(z)>0$ be even, and let $k\ge 2$. If $\lambda_G(x,y)\ge k$ for every $x,y\in V$, then for every edge $e=zt$ there exists an edge $f=zv$ such that splitting off $e$ and $f$ yields $\lambda_{G^{ef}}(x,y)\ge k$ for every $x,y\in V$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In an undirected graph whose designated vertex has positive even degree, if all pairs of other vertices have local edge-connectivity at least k, then every edge at the designated vertex has a splitting partner whose removal by splitting-off preserves that connectivity among all other vertices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall e=zt\in\delta_G(z)\;\exists f=zv\in\delta_G(z):\ \lambda_{G^{ef}}(x,y)\ge k\quad\forall x,y\in V

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lovász Complete Undirected Splitting Theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete elimination of an even-degree designated vertex while preserving uniform edge-connectivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $G=(V+z,E)$ be an undirected graph, let $d_G(z)>0$ be even, and let $K\ge 2$. If $\lambda_G(x,y)\ge K$ for every $x,y\in V$, then the edges incident to $z$ can be partitioned into $d_G(z)/2$ pairs such that simultaneously splitting off all pairs produces a graph $G'=(V,E')$ that is $K$-edge-connected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every pair of vertices other than a positive even-degree vertex z has edge-connectivity at least K, then all edges at z can be paired and split off so that deleting z leaves a K-edge-connected graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\text{ a pairing of }\delta_G(z)\text{ whose simultaneous splitting-off yields a }K\text{-edge-connected }G'=(V,E')

knowledge_statements.title: Mader Splitting-Off Theorem Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local-connectivity admissible-pair form of Mader's undirected splitting-off theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If no edge incident with \(s\) is a bridge and \(d_G(s)\ne 3\), then there are two incident edges \(su\) and \(sv\) whose splitting-off is admissible: in the resulting multigraph \(G_{u,v}\), \[\lambda_{G_{u,v}}(x,y)=\lambda_G(x,y)\qquad\text{for all distinct }x,y\in V\setminus\{s\}.\] The operation deletes \(su,sv\), adds an edge \(uv\), permits parallel edges, and discards the added edge when \(u=v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unless the distinguished vertex has degree three or an incident bridge, some incident pair can be split without changing any remaining pairwise edge-connectivity.
assumptions_latex: The finite undirected multigraph \(G=(V,E)\) has a vertex \(s\) incident with no bridge.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Some pair of edges incident with \(s\) is admissible for all local edge-connectivities among vertices other than \(s\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constructive characterization of odd edge-connected graphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mader-type construction theorem characterizing graphs of odd edge-connectivity through edge addition and prescribed pinching operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let K=2k+1. A graph G is K-edge-connected if and only if it can be constructed from a single vertex by repeatedly applying the following operations: (A) add an edge between two existing vertices; (B) pinch k existing edges with a new vertex z and add an edge from z to an existing vertex; or (C) pinch k existing edges with a new vertex s, then choose k edges in the resulting graph, at least one of which is an original edge of G, pinch those k edges with a new vertex z, and finally add the edge zs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For odd K=2k+1, a graph is K-edge-connected exactly when it can be built from one vertex using edge additions and the two specified k-edge pinching constructions, including the condition in operation C that at least one selected edge is an original edge of the target graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G\text{ is }K\text{-edge-connected}\iff G\text{ is constructible from one vertex by operations (A), (B), and (C) as specified.}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Splitting off a pair \(su,sv\) at \(s\) deletes those two edges and adds one edge \(uv\), with parallel edges allowed and a resulting loop discardable. A complete splitting-off at \(s\) is a sequence of exactly \(d_G(s)/2\) such operations, each using two currently incident edges, whose final graph has \(d(s)=0\). If every operation preserves a specified connectivity requirement on \(V\setminus\{s\}\), the sequence is complete and admissible for that requirement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complete splitting-off pairs and replaces all edges incident with an even-degree vertex until that vertex becomes isolated, optionally preserving a stated connectivity requirement.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Complete Splitting at a Vertex
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of complete undirected splitting-off, with its connectivity-preserving consequence under the Lovász theorem hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A complete splitting at a vertex $z$ of positive even degree is the simultaneous splitting-off of $d_G(z)/2$ disjoint pairs that partition the edges incident to $z$. In particular, if $G$ is $K$-edge-connected, $K\ge2$, and $z$ has even degree, such a complete splitting can be chosen so that the resulting graph, with $z$ eliminated, remains $K$-edge-connected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complete splitting at z pairs all edges incident to z and splits off every pair, thereby eliminating z. For a K-edge-connected graph and an even-degree vertex, the Lovász theorem guarantees a choice that preserves K-edge-connectivity.
assumptions_latex: \text{For the stated existence consequence: }K\ge2\text{ and }G\text{ is }K\text{-edge-connected}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{A complete splitting consists of }d_G(z)/2\text{ simultaneous disjoint splittings; under the stated hypotheses one preserves }K\text{-edge-connectivity.}

knowledge_statements.title: Partial Splitting-Off
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a prescribed noncomplete elimination extent, independently of any admissibility condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A partial splitting-off of extent \(q\) at \(s\) is a sequence of \(q\) operations, each deleting two currently incident edges \(su,sv\) and adding an edge \(uv\). The resulting graph \(G'\) satisfies \(d_{G'}(s)=d_G(s)-2q>0\). The sequence is admissible relative to a specified family of vertex pairs if every required local edge-connectivity is unchanged after the sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial splitting-off replaces a positive number of incident edge pairs but leaves the distinguished vertex with positive degree, reducing its degree by twice the number of operations.
assumptions_latex: The finite undirected multigraph \(G=(V,E)\) has a distinguished vertex \(s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A partial splitting-off performs exactly \(q\) pair operations and leaves positive degree \(d_G(s)-2q\) at \(s\).

notation.meaning: Number of pair operations performed.
Distinguished vertex at which splitting occurs.

knowledge_statements.title: Elimination-Extent Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies undirected splitting-off sequences by how much of the incidence at the split vertex is eliminated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected multigraph and let \(s\in V\). Splitting the pair \(su,sv\) deletes these two edge copies and adds one copy of \(uv\), with a loop allowed when \(u=v\). A splitting-off sequence at \(s\) is partial if it performs any feasible number of such operations. It is complete if its pairs partition all edge copies incident with \(s\), so the resulting graph has \(d(s)=0\) and may be identified with a graph on \(V\setminus\{s\}\). Thus complete elimination is possible only when the initial degree \(d_G(s)\) is even.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial splitting removes selected incident-edge pairs; complete splitting pairs every edge at the chosen vertex and therefore requires even degree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_G(s)\) even is necessary for complete splitting at \(s\).

notation.meaning: Degree of the split vertex, counting multiplicity.

children.title: Blocking-Cut Obstructions
children.top_down_role: Cut configurations that block candidate splitting pairs.

knowledge_statements.title: Blocking-Cut Obstructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A cut certificate showing that a proposed undirected split violates a prescribed connectivity requirement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\), let \(s\in V\), and prescribe an integer cut requirement \(r(X)\) for each \(X\subseteq V\setminus\{s\}\). Assume \(d_G(X)\ge r(X)\). A set \(X\) blocks the pair \(su,sv\) if \(u,v\in X\) and \(d_G(X)-2<r(X)\). Indeed, splitting \(su,sv\) decreases \(d_G(X)\) by exactly two when both endpoints lie in \(X\), and leaves it unchanged when at most one does. Consequently, the displayed inequalities provide a directly checkable certificate that the pair is inadmissible for preserving all prescribed cut requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut containing both split endpoints blocks the pair when losing two crossing edges would make its prescribed connectivity inequality fail.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u,v\in X\) and \(d_G(X)-2<r(X)\) certify inadmissibility of \(su,sv\).

notation.meaning: Number of edges with exactly one endpoint in the set.
Required lower bound for the cut of the set.

children.title: Dangerous-Set Obstructions
children.top_down_role: Dangerous vertex-set structures restricting splitting admissibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Dangerous-Set Obstructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the standard uniform edge-connectivity specialization of an undirected blocking set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected multigraph, let \(s\in V\), and suppose \(d_G(X)\ge k\) for every nonempty proper \(X\subset V\setminus\{s\}\). For a proposed split of \(su,sv\), a nonempty proper set \(X\subset V\setminus\{s\}\) is dangerous for the pair if \(u,v\in X\) and \(d_G(X)\le k+1\). Since the split changes this cut value to \(d_G(X)-2<k\), every dangerous set obstructs preservation of \(k\)-edge-connectivity among the vertices other than \(s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dangerous set contains both split endpoints and has cut size at most one above the required connectivity, so splitting violates the requirement.
assumptions_latex: Every relevant cut initially has size at least \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A dangerous set for \(su,sv\) certifies that the pair is not \(k\)-connectivity-preserving.

notation.meaning: Size of the undirected edge boundary of the set.
Uniform edge-connectivity requirement.

children.title: Parity Obstructions
children.top_down_role: Parity-sensitive barriers to complete or admissible splitting-off.

knowledge_statements.title: Parity Obstructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The elementary parity boundary for eliminating every edge incident with an undirected split vertex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Each undirected splitting-off operation at \(s\) removes exactly two edge copies incident with \(s\), and hence preserves the parity of \(d_G(s)\). Therefore a sequence can eliminate all incidence at \(s\) only if \(d_G(s)\) is even. In particular, every multigraph with odd \(d_G(s)\)—for example, a three-edge star centered at \(s\)—admits no complete splitting-off at \(s\), irrespective of which pairs are locally admissible. Partial splitting may terminate with one unpaired edge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Because every split removes two incident edges, odd degree prevents complete elimination and leaves at least one edge unpaired.
assumptions_latex: A split always consumes two edge copies incident with \(s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_G(s)\equiv 1\pmod 2\) implies that complete splitting-off at \(s\) is impossible.

notation.meaning: Degree at the split vertex, counting multiplicity.

children.title: Directed Splitting-Off Theorem Families
children.top_down_role: Existence and admissibility theory for directed local reductions.

knowledge_statements.title: Directed Splitting-Off Theorem Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common framework underlying directed existence and admissibility theorems, without selecting one theorem’s specialized hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a directed multigraph \(D=(V,A)\) and \(s\in V\), splitting the consecutive pair \(us,sv\) deletes those arc copies and adds \(uv\). Directed splitting-off theorems seek a pair, or a sequence of pairs, for which specified connectivities between vertices of \(V\setminus\{s\}\) remain unchanged. Their hypotheses typically combine cut lower bounds, balance or degree conditions at \(s\), and exclusion of exceptional configurations; their conclusions distinguish existence of one admissible pair from existence of a complete admissible splitting. These conclusions are logically distinct because local admissibility need not supply a pairing of every arc at \(s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Directed splitting theorems separate existence of one connectivity-preserving in-arc/out-arc pair from existence of a complete pairing at the eliminated vertex.
assumptions_latex: The split pairs an arc entering \(s\) with an arc leaving \(s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Existence of one admissible pair and existence of a complete admissible splitting are separate theorem regimes.

notation.meaning: An arc entering and an arc leaving the split vertex.
Replacement arc created by the directed split.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mader's directed splitting lemma
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence of an admissible incoming partner for each chosen outgoing arc at a balanced auxiliary node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V\cup\{z\},A)\) be \(k\)-edge-connected in \(V\), where \(k\ge1\), and suppose \(\varrho_D(z)=\delta_D(z)\). For every arc \(e=zt\), there exists an arc \(f=uz\) such that splitting off \(\{e,f\}\) produces a digraph \(D^{ef}\) that remains \(k\)-edge-connected in \(V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a digraph that is k-edge-connected on V, if the auxiliary node z has equal indegree and outdegree, every outgoing arc of z has an incoming partner whose splitting-off preserves k-edge-connectivity on V.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists f=uz\in A\text{ such that }D^{ef}\text{ is }k\text{-edge-connected in }V.

children.title: Complete Directed Splitting
children.top_down_role: Directed splitting regimes aimed at full vertex elimination.

knowledge_statements.title: Complete Directed Splitting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines complete directed elimination through a pairing of all arcs incident with the split vertex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a directed multigraph and let \(s\in V\). A complete directed splitting at \(s\) is determined by a bijection between the arc copies entering \(s\) and those leaving \(s\). For every matched pair \(us,sv\), delete the two arcs and add \(uv\). After all matched pairs are split, no arc is incident with \(s\), and \(s\) may be deleted. Such a complete pairing exists only if \(d_D^-(s)=d_D^+(s)\); connectivity-preserving completeness additionally requires every split in the chosen sequence to satisfy the stipulated admissibility condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complete directed splitting pairs every entering arc with one leaving arc, requiring equal indegree and outdegree and admissibility throughout the sequence.
assumptions_latex: Arc copies are distinguished when parallel arcs occur.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Complete directed splitting requires \(d_D^-(s)=d_D^+(s)\).

notation.meaning: Indegree of the split vertex.
Outdegree of the split vertex.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Complete directed splitting at a balanced node
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mader's complete elimination theorem for a balanced auxiliary node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V\cup\{z\},A)\) be \(k\)-edge-connected in \(V\), where \(k\ge1\), and suppose \(\varrho_D(z)=\delta_D(z)\). The arcs entering \(z\) can be paired bijectively with the arcs leaving \(z\) so that splitting off all \(\varrho_D(z)\) pairs yields a digraph on \(V\) that is \(k\)-edge-connected in \(V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a balanced auxiliary node of a digraph that is k-edge-connected on V, all incoming and outgoing arcs can be paired and split off so that eliminating the node preserves k-edge-connectivity on V.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{There is a complete pairing at }z\text{ whose simultaneous splitting-off yields a }k\text{-edge-connected digraph on }V.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pinching Together Edges
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inverse construction to complete splitting at a degree-$2j$ vertex in the even-connectivity setting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose $K=2k$. To pinch together $j$ edges with a new vertex $z$, select $j$ existing edges, subdivide each once, and identify their $j$ subdivision vertices as $z$. The resulting vertex has degree $2j$, and this operation is inverse to a complete splitting at $z$. For $j=1$, pinching is ordinary subdivision of one edge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When K is even, pinching together j edges means subdividing each selected edge and identifying all new subdivision vertices into one vertex z. It is the inverse of completely splitting a degree-2j vertex; for j equal to one it is ordinary edge subdivision.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Pinching produces a new vertex }z\text{ of degree }2j\text{ and is inverse to complete splitting at }z;\quad j=1\text{ gives edge subdivision.}

children.title: Partial Directed Splitting
children.top_down_role: Selective directed splitting with residual incident arcs.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial Directed Splitting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines proper partial directed splitting that consumes selected entering and leaving arcs but does not eliminate all incidence at the split vertex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a finite directed multigraph and let \(s\in V\). A proper partial directed splitting at \(s\) chooses equally large nonempty subsets \(I'\subseteq\delta_D^-(s)\) and \(O'\subseteq\delta_D^+(s)\), together with a bijection from \(I'\) to \(O'\), such that at least one arc incident with \(s\) is unchosen. Each matched pair \(us,sv\) is replaced by \(uv\), while all unchosen arcs remain incident with \(s\). Connectivity-preserving partial splitting additionally requires each pair to be admissible when it is split in the resulting sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper partial directed splitting pairs a nonempty selection of entering and leaving arcs while leaving at least one incident arc at the split vertex.
assumptions_latex: Arc copies are distinguished when parallel arcs occur.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After splitting \(|I'|\) pairs, \(d_D^-(s)-|I'|\) entering arcs and \(d_D^+(s)-|I'|\) leaving arcs remain, with at least one of these two numbers positive.

notation.meaning: Set of arc copies entering the split vertex.

knowledge_statements.title: Arc-Pairing Feasibility Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates cardinality feasibility of directed arc pairing from connectivity-preserving admissibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a finite directed multigraph, let \(s\in V\), and let \(q\) be a nonnegative integer. Exactly \(q\) directed splits can be specified using distinct arc copies precisely when there are subsets \(I'\subseteq\delta_D^-(s)\) and \(O'\subseteq\delta_D^+(s)\) with \(|I'|=|O'|=q\), together with a bijection between them. Thus cardinality feasibility is equivalent to \(0\le q\le\min\{d_D^-(s),d_D^+(s)\}\). Complete elimination is cardinality-feasible precisely when \(d_D^-(s)=d_D^+(s)=q\). If connectivity must also be preserved, the selected pairs must admit an ordering in which each pair is admissible in the current residual digraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonnegative integer q, q pairs are cardinality-feasible exactly when q does not exceed either incident semidegree; complete pairing requires balance, and connectivity preservation imposes sequential admissibility.
assumptions_latex: Each split uses one entering and one leaving arc copy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q\) pairs are cardinality-feasible if and only if \(0\le q\le\min\{d_D^-(s),d_D^+(s)\}\).

children.title: Directed-Cut Obstructions
children.top_down_role: Directed cut configurations that prevent connectivity-preserving splitting.

knowledge_statements.title: Directed-Cut Obstructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A tight in-cut certificate obstructing a directed split under uniform strong edge-connectivity requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a directed multigraph, let \(s\in V\), and suppose every nonempty proper \(X\subset V\setminus\{s\}\) satisfies \(\rho_D(X)\ge k\). For the proposed split of \(us,sv\), the value \(\rho_D(X)\) decreases by one exactly when \(u,v\in X\); otherwise it is unchanged. Consequently, a nonempty proper set \(X\subset V\setminus\{s\}\) with \(u,v\in X\) and \(\rho_D(X)=k\) is a directed-cut obstruction: after the split its entering cut has size \(k-1\), certifying failure to preserve strong \(k\)-edge-connectivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tight entering cut containing both external endpoints loses one arc under the directed split and certifies inadmissibility.
assumptions_latex: Every relevant entering cut initially has size at least \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u,v\in X\) and \(\rho_D(X)=k\) certify that splitting \(us,sv\) violates the cut requirement.

notation.meaning: Number of arcs entering the set from its complement.
Required strong edge-connectivity level.

children.title: Admissible Splitting Pairs
children.top_down_role: Structural classes of arc pairs compatible with preserved connectivity.

knowledge_statements.title: Admissible Splitting Pairs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines directed admissibility by preservation of all local arc-connectivities away from the split vertex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\), let \(s\in V\), and let \(D'\) result from replacing \(us,sv\) by \(uv\). The pair \((us,sv)\) is admissible at \(s\) if, for every ordered pair of distinct vertices \(x,y\in V\setminus\{s\}\), one has \(\lambda_{D'}(x,y)=\lambda_D(x,y)\), where \(\lambda_D(x,y)\) is the maximum number of pairwise arc-disjoint directed paths from \(x\) to \(y\). Relative to a specified demand family, admissibility may instead require equality only for the designated ordered pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A directed pair is admissible when replacing its two arcs by the shortcut arc preserves every required ordered-pair arc-connectivity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Admissibility means \(\lambda_{D'}(x,y)=\lambda_D(x,y)\) for every required ordered pair \((x,y)\).

notation.meaning: Digraph obtained after the proposed directed split.
Maximum number of arc-disjoint directed paths from \(x\) to \(y\).

children.title: Obstruction–Admissibility Boundary
children.top_down_role: Boundary cases separating blocked pairings from admissible pairings.

knowledge_statements.title: Obstruction–Admissibility Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut characterization of admissibility for one directed split under a uniform strong-connectivity requirement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a finite directed multigraph, let \(s\in V\), and suppose \(\rho_D(X)\ge k\) for every nonempty proper \(X\subset V\setminus\{s\}\). Let \(D'\) arise by splitting \(us,sv\) into \(uv\). Then \(D'\) satisfies the same cut inequalities if and only if there is no nonempty proper \(X\subset V\setminus\{s\}\) such that \(u,v\in X\) and \(\rho_D(X)=k\). Equivalently, the proposed pair is admissible for the uniform cut requirement exactly when \(\rho_D(X)\ge k+1\) for every such set containing both external endpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A directed split preserves the uniform cut requirement exactly when no tight entering cut contains both external endpoints of the split.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho_D(X)\ge k\) holds for every relevant nontrivial set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D'\) preserves all level-\(k\) cut inequalities if and only if \(\rho_D(X)\ge k+1\) whenever \(X\) is relevant and \(u,v\in X\).

children.title: Directed Connectivity Preservation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Directed splitting under root-centered and terminal-pair connectivity targets.

children.title: Rooted Connectivity Preservation
children.top_down_role: Directed splitting under connectivity requirements centered at a distinguished root.

knowledge_statements.title: Rooted Connectivity Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preservation criterion for directed connectivities to and from a fixed root outside the split vertex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a finite directed multigraph, choose distinct vertices \(r,s\in V\), and let \(D'\) be obtained by replacing \(as,sb\) with \(ab\). The split preserves two-sided rooted local connectivity at \(r\) if, for every \(t\in V\setminus\{r,s\}\), both \(\lambda_{D'}(r,t)=\lambda_D(r,t)\) and \(\lambda_{D'}(t,r)=\lambda_D(t,r)\). Equivalently, for every such \(t\), no minimum entering cut \(X\) with \(t\in X\) and \(r\notin X\), and no minimum entering cut \(X\) with \(r\in X\) and \(t\notin X\), contains both \(a\) and \(b\). For a one-sided rooted requirement, retain only the corresponding equality and cut condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A directed split preserves two-sided rooted connectivity when every connectivity from the root to a surviving vertex and back remains unchanged; equivalently, no corresponding minimum entering cut contains both external endpoints of the split.
assumptions_latex: The root \(r\) is distinct from the split vertex \(s\).
The proposed directed split replaces \(as,sb\) with \(ab\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Rooted preservation holds exactly when the two displayed connectivity equalities hold for every \(t\in V\setminus\{r,s\}\), equivalently when none of the specified minimum entering cuts contains both \(a\) and \(b\).

notation.meaning: Designated root vertex.
External tail and head of the proposed directed split.
Digraph after the directed split.
Directed local arc-connectivity from \(x\) to \(y\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rooted connectivity-preserving directed splitting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete elimination of an auxiliary node under an asymmetric degree condition while preserving root-centered edge connectivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V\cup\{z\},A)\) be rooted \(k\)-edge-connected from a designated root \(r_0\in V\), and suppose \(\varrho_D(z)\ge\delta_D(z)\). The \(\delta_D(z)\) arcs leaving \(z\) can be paired with distinct appropriate arcs entering \(z\) so that, after simultaneously splitting off these pairs and removing \(z\), the resulting digraph on \(V\) is rooted \(k\)-edge-connected from \(r_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a rooted k-edge-connected digraph has an auxiliary node z whose indegree is at least its outdegree, every outgoing arc can be paired with a suitable incoming arc; splitting all pairs and deleting z preserves rooted k-edge-connectivity on V.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{There exists a pairing of all arcs leaving }z\text{ with }\delta_D(z)\text{ entering arcs such that splitting the pairs and deleting }z\text{ preserves rooted }k\text{-edge-connectivity on }V.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rooted Terminal-Connectivity Reduction at a Nonterminal Node
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Removal or splitting at a nonterminal, nonroot node while preserving k edge-disjoint root-to-terminal paths.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) have root \(r_0\) and terminal set \(T\subseteq V\setminus\{r_0\}\). Suppose \(\varrho(v)\ge\delta(v)\) for every \(v\in V\setminus(T\cup\{r_0\})\), and \(\lambda(r_0,u)\ge k\) for every \(u\in T\). For \(z\in V\setminus(T\cup\{r_0\})\), if \(\varrho(z)>\delta(z)\), then \(\varrho(z)-\delta(z)\) arcs entering \(z\) can be removed while preserving all inequalities \(\lambda(r_0,u)\ge k\). If \(\varrho(z)=\delta(z)\), then a splitting at \(z\) exists that preserves all these inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under nonnegative indegree surplus at every nonterminal, nonroot node and k edge-disjoint paths from the root to every terminal, the surplus incoming arcs at such a node can be deleted without losing rooted terminal connectivity; at a balanced node, a connectivity-preserving splitting is possible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \varrho(z)>\delta(z)\Rightarrow\text{one may remove }\varrho(z)-\delta(z)\text{ arcs entering }z;\quad \varrho(z)=\delta(z)\Rightarrow\text{a splitting at }z\text{ preserves }\lambda(r_0,u)\ge k\ \forall u\in T

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D'\) be obtained from \(D\) by splitting off \(xs,sy\) at \(s\). The split is pairwise-connectivity preserving on \(V\setminus\{s\}\) precisely when
\[
\lambda_{D'}(u,v)=\lambda_D(u,v)\qquad\text{for all distinct }u,v\in V\setminus\{s\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A directed split at s is pairwise preserving when it leaves unchanged the maximum number of arc-disjoint paths for every ordered pair of remaining vertices.
knowledge_statements.title: Pairwise Connectivity Preservation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Terminal paths and inner-Eulerian terminal instances
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the basic objects for terminal-set path packing in an undirected graph.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Criterion for packing edge-disjoint circuits through a vertex
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Here \(d_{G-s}(X)\) denotes the size of the cut of \(X\) in \(G-s\), and \(d_G(s,t)\) denotes the multiplicity of the edge pair \(st\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be Eulerian, let \(s\in V\), and let \(k\geq0\). For \(t\in\Gamma_G(s)\), define \[\lambda'(t):=\min\!\left\{d_G(s,t),\ \min\left\{d_{G-s}(X):X\subseteq V\setminus\{s\},\ X\cap\Gamma_G(s)=\{t\}\right\}\right\}.\] Then \(G\) contains \(k\) pairwise edge-disjoint circuits of length at least three, each passing through \(s\), if and only if \(\sum_{t\in\Gamma_G(s)}\lambda'(t)\geq2k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In an Eulerian graph, k edge-disjoint circuits of length at least three can all pass through a specified vertex s exactly when the sum of the stated local cut-connectivity quantities over the neighbors of s is at least 2k.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\ k\text{ pairwise edge-disjoint circuits of length }\geq3\text{ through }s\iff\sum_{t\in\Gamma_G(s)}\lambda'(t)\geq2k

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unified Directed Pinching Operation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A construction operation unifying node addition and partial pinching in rooted directed-connectivity constructions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an integer k\ge 1, choose j with 0\le j<k. Pinch j existing directed edges with a new node z, and add k-j possibly parallel edges entering z whose tails are existing nodes.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Pinch }j\text{ existing edges at a new node }z\text{ and add }k-j\text{ edges entering }z\text{ from existing nodes.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uncrossing identities for demand–supply tight sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure of tight sets under union, intersection, and differences when the corresponding demand interaction vanishes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(d_G(X)\ge d_H(X)\) for every vertex set \(X\). If \(A\) and \(B\) are tight, then: (a) if \(d_H(A,B)=0\), both \(A\cup B\) and \(A\cap B\) are tight and \(d_G(A,B)=0\); (b) if \(\bar d_H(A,B)=0\), both \(A\setminus B\) and \(B\setminus A\) are tight and \(\bar d_G(A,B)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Suppose every supply cut has size at least its corresponding demand cut. For two tight sets, absence of demand edges of the first indicated type implies that their union and intersection remain tight and that the corresponding supply interaction also vanishes. Absence of demand edges of the complementary indicated type similarly makes both set differences tight and forces the corresponding supply interaction to vanish.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d_H(A,B)=0\Rightarrow\bigl[A\cup B,A\cap B\text{ tight and }d_G(A,B)=0\bigr],\quad \bar d_H(A,B)=0\Rightarrow\bigl[A\setminus B,B\setminus A\text{ tight and }\bar d_G(A,B)=0\bigr].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constructive Characterization of Minimally Rooted k-Edge-Connected Digraphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An if-and-only-if construction from the root using vertex addition and edge pinching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(k\ge 1\), a digraph \(D=(V,A)\) is minimally rooted \(k\)-edge-connected with respect to root \(r_0\) if and only if it can be constructed from \(r_0\) by repeatedly applying either: \(\mathrm{(B)}\) add a new node \(z\) together with \(k\) possibly parallel arcs entering \(z\), whose tails are existing nodes; or \(\mathrm{(C)}\) choose \(j\) existing arcs with \(0<j<k\), pinch them with a new node \(z\), and add \(k-j\) possibly parallel arcs entering \(z\), whose tails are existing nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A digraph is minimally rooted k-edge-connected exactly when it can be built from its root by repeatedly adding a node with k incoming arcs, or by pinching j existing arcs at a new node and adding k−j incoming arcs, for some 0<j<k.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D\text{ is minimally rooted }k\text{-edge-connected w.r.t. }r_0\iff D\text{ is constructible from }r_0\text{ by operations (B) and (C)}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constructive Characterization of Strictly k-Sparse Graphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterization by vertex addition and edge pinching, including the restriction on parallel edges.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an integer $k\ge 2$, a loopless graph $G=(V,E)$ is strictly $k$-sparse if and only if it can be constructed from one initial vertex by repeatedly applying either: (A) add a new vertex $z$ and at most $k$ new, possibly parallel, edges incident with $z$; or (B) for some $1\le j\le k-1$, pinch $j$ existing edges with a new vertex $z$ and add $k-j$ new, possibly parallel, edges joining $z$ to other vertices. Each operation must leave no set of $k$ parallel edges in the resulting graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A loopless graph is strictly k-sparse exactly when it can be built from a single vertex using constrained vertex additions and edge-pinching operations, with no resulting class of k parallel edges.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G\text{ is strictly }k\text{-sparse}\iff G\text{ is constructible from one vertex by operations (A) and (B)}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Laman characterization of minimally rigid graphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes planar minimal generic rigidity by a global edge count and induced-subgraph sparsity inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let G=(V,E) be a loopless undirected graph with n=|V|. Then G is minimally rigid in the plane if and only if |E|=2n-3 and i_G(Z)\le 2|Z|-3 for every Z\subseteq V with |Z|\ge 2, where i_G(Z) is the number of edges induced by Z. Thus failure of minimal rigidity has a succinct certificate consisting of failure of the global edge count or a set Z violating the sparsity inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A loopless undirected graph on n vertices is minimally rigid in the plane exactly when it has 2n−3 edges and every vertex subset of size at least two induces at most 2|Z|−3 edges. A wrong total edge count or a violating subset certifies failure.
assumptions_latex: G=(V,E)\text{ is a loopless undirected graph}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G\text{ is minimally rigid}\iff \left(|E|=2n-3\ \land\ \forall Z\subseteq V,\ |Z|\ge 2:\ i_G(Z)\le 2|Z|-3\right).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constructive characterization of 3-edge-connected graphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes 3-edge connectivity through three graph-building operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An undirected graph $G=(V,E)$ is $3$-edge-connected if and only if it can be built from a single initial vertex by repeatedly applying one of the following operations: (A) add an edge between two existing vertices; (B) subdivide an existing edge by a new vertex $z$ and add an edge joining $z$ to an existing vertex; or (C) subdivide each of two existing edges by a new vertex and add an edge joining the two subdividing vertices.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G\text{ is }3\text{-edge-connected}\iff G\text{ is constructible by operations (A), (B), and (C).}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition for vertex subsets and whole loopless undirected graphs, together with the stated rigidity specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $k\ge 2$ be an integer and let $G=(V,E)$ be a loopless undirected graph. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subdivided 3-Connectivity and Removable Edges
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions used in deletion-based reductions of 3-connected graphs, including the resulting degree boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A graph \(G\) is subdivided 3-connected if it is obtained from a 3-connected graph by subdividing some edges. An edge \(e\in E(G)\) is removable if \(G-e\) is subdivided 3-connected. Moreover, if \(G\) is 3-connected and \(G-e\) is subdivided 3-connected, then only the endpoints of \(e\) can have degree \(2\) in \(G-e\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A graph is subdivided 3-connected when it arises by subdividing edges of a 3-connected graph. An edge is removable when deleting it leaves a subdivided 3-connected graph. If the original graph is 3-connected, only the deleted edge's endpoints can have degree two afterward.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence of a root-incident edge whose contraction preserves the two internally vertex-disjoint root-to-vertex path property.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Generic and minimal rigidity of a planar graph
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines rigidity for a graph realized as a generic planar bar-and-joint framework.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let G=(V,E) be a loopless undirected graph whose vertices are placed in the plane in general position and whose edges are rigid bars hinged at their endpoints. The graph is generically rigid in the plane if the resulting framework is rigid; equivalently, its generic rigidity matrix has rank 2|V|-3. It is minimally rigid if it is rigid and deleting any edge destroys rigidity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A loopless undirected graph is generically rigid in the plane when a generic bar-and-joint realization of it is rigid, equivalently when the associated generic rigidity matrix has rank 2|V|−3. It is minimally rigid when it is rigid but ceases to be rigid after any edge is removed.

\text{The vertices are placed generically in }\mathbb R^2

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pattern of a demand graph and associated graph classes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Demand-pattern simplification and small graph terminology used in path-packing classifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The pattern \(H'\) of a multigraph \(H\) is obtained by replacing every maximal class of parallel edges by one edge. A graph is a double star if at most two vertices cover all its edges. Here \(K_n\) denotes the complete graph on \(n\) vertices, \(C_5\) the five-vertex cycle, \(K_2+K_3\) the five-vertex graph with components \(K_2\) and \(K_3\), and \(3K_2\) the graph consisting of three pairwise disjoint edges.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The pattern of a demand multigraph is its underlying simple graph after each parallel-edge class is replaced by one edge. A double star is a graph whose edges can all be covered by at most two vertices. The remaining notation denotes a complete graph, a five-cycle, the disjoint union of a single edge and a triangle, and three disjoint edges, respectively.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Henneberg construction of minimally rigid graphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives an inductive constructive characterization of planar minimally rigid graphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A graph G=(V,E) is minimally rigid in the plane if and only if it can be constructed from K_2 by a sequence of the following operations: (A) add a new vertex adjacent to two distinct existing vertices; or (B) subdivide an existing edge s_1s_2 with a new vertex z and add an edge from z to an existing vertex s_3\notin\{s_1,s_2\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Directed 2-Connectivity from a Two-Vertex Root Set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut definition and its equivalent disjoint-directed-path formulation; the roots form a two-element subset of the vertex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $D=(V,A)$ be a digraph and let $R=\{r_1,r_2\}\subseteq V$. The digraph $D$ is $2$-connected from $R$ if, for every nonempty $X\subseteq V\setminus R$, at least two distinct vertices outside $X$ are tails of arcs entering $X$. Equivalently, for every $v\in V\setminus R$, there exist two directed paths from $R$ to $v$ that are vertex-disjoint in $V\setminus\{v\}$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A digraph is 2-connected from a two-vertex root set when every nonempty set avoiding the roots has arcs entering it from at least two distinct outside vertices. By Menger's theorem, this is equivalent to the existence, for each nonroot vertex, of two root-to-vertex directed paths sharing no vertex other than their endpoint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
D\text{ is }2\text{-connected from }R\iff \forall v\in V\setminus R,
 \exists\text{ two }R\text{-to-}v\text{ dipaths disjoint in }V\setminus\{v\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Distinguished edge with only star minimum cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A structural property of minimally odd-edge-connected graphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $K\ge 1$ be odd, and let $G$ be a minimally $K$-edge-connected graph with at least two vertices. Then there is an edge $e=uv$ such that every minimum cut whose edge set contains $e$ is either $\Delta_G(u)$ or $\Delta_G(v)$. Consequently, every $K$-cut containing $e$ is a star cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If K is positive and odd and G is a minimally K-edge-connected graph with at least two vertices, then G has an edge uv for which every minimum cut containing that edge is the star at u or the star at v. Thus every K-cut containing the edge is a star cut.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists e=uv\in E(G)\;\forall C\,(C\text{ is a minimum cut and }e\in C\Rightarrow C\in\{\Delta_G(u),\Delta_G(v)\}).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constructive Characterization of Rooted Directed Edge Connectivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes rooted k-edge-connected digraphs by arc addition and vertex-introduction operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let k\ge 1 and let D=(V,A) be a digraph with root r_0. Then D is rooted k-edge-connected with respect to r_0 if and only if D can be constructed from r_0 by repeatedly: (A) adding a directed edge between existing vertices; (B) adding a new vertex z together with k possibly parallel edges entering z from existing vertices; or (C) for some 0<j<k, pinching j existing edges with a new vertex z and adding k-j possibly parallel edges entering z from existing vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A digraph is rooted k-edge-connected with respect to a root r₀, for k at least one, exactly when it can be built from r₀ by repeatedly adding an arc between existing vertices, adding a new vertex with k entering arcs from existing vertices, or pinching j existing arcs at a new vertex and adding k−j entering arcs, where 0<j<k. Parallel entering arcs are allowed.
assumptions_latex: D=(V,A)\text{ is a digraph with distinguished root }r_0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D\text{ is rooted }k\text{-edge-connected with respect to }r_0\iff D\text{ is obtainable from }r_0\text{ by operations (A)--(C).}

assumptions_latex: \(D_0,D_1,\ldots,D_m\) is a recorded sequence of finite directed multigraphs in which \(D_i\) is obtained from \(D_{i-1}\) by replacing distinct arcs \(x_is_i,s_iy_i\) with a labeled shortcut arc \(x_iy_i\).
\(\mathcal Q'\) is a family of pairwise arc-disjoint directed paths in \(D_m\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input the recorded sequence \(D_0,D_1,\ldots,D_m\) and an arc-disjoint path family \(\mathcal Q'\) in \(D_m\). For \(i=m,m-1,\ldots,1\), replace every occurrence of the labeled shortcut arc \(x_iy_i\) created at step \(i\) by the two-arc segment \(x_is_iy_i\). Output the resulting family \(\mathcal Q\) in \(D_0\). The output is arc-disjoint, has the same corresponding endpoints, and satisfies
\[
|\mathcal Q|=|\mathcal Q'|.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Process the recorded splits in reverse order, replacing each labeled shortcut arc used by a path with its original two-arc segment. The lifted path family is arc-disjoint and has the same size and corresponding endpoints.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent each available augmentation end at \(v\in V(G)\) by an edge or arc incident with a new vertex \(s\). Pair compatible ends by admissible splitting at \(s\); a paired pair at \(u,v\) becomes an augmenting edge or arc joining \(u\) and \(v\). If all required cut or local-connectivity lower bounds are preserved at every split, elimination of \(s\) yields an augmentation set \(F\) such that \(G+F\) satisfies exactly those retained requirements. Reversing the splits recovers the auxiliary representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Encode augmentation endpoints as stubs at an auxiliary vertex, then split admissible pairs into actual augmentation edges while preserving the required connectivity bounds.

children.top_down_role: Realization and synthesis uses of connectivity-preserving elimination.

assumptions_latex: The total degree \(d(V)=\sum_{v\in V}d(v)\) is even and \(2d(v)\leq d(V)\) for every \(v\in V\).
The hub multigraph \(H\) has vertex set \(V\cup\{s\}\) and exactly \(d(v)\) parallel edges between \(s\) and each \(v\in V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The hub edges can be completely paired at distinct vertices and split off to produce a loopless multigraph \(G\) on \(V\) satisfying \(\deg_G(v)=d(v)\) for every \(v\in V\).

notation.meaning: prescribed degree of vertex v
sum of the prescribed degrees over V
auxiliary hub vertex
hub multigraph encoding the prescribed edge ends

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hub elimination represents loopless multigraph synthesis as pairing prescribed endpoint stubs; connectivity constraints require an additionally admissible complete pairing.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Form the hub multigraph \(H\) on \(V\cup\{s\}\) with exactly \(d(v)\) copies of \(sv\) for each \(v\in V\). If \(d(V)\) is even and \(2d(v)\leq d(V)\) for every \(v\in V\), the hub edges can be paired so that the two edges in each pair have distinct endpoints in \(V\). Replacing every paired \(su,sv\) by \(uv\) yields a loopless multigraph \(G\) satisfying
\[
\deg_G(v)=d(v)\qquad\text{for every }v\in V.
\]
If the complete pairing is also admissible for specified connectivity requirements, the resulting graph realizes those requirements as well.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Encode the prescribed degrees as stubs incident with a hub. An even degree sum and no vertex demanding more than all other vertices combined permit complete pairing at distinct endpoints, producing a loopless multigraph with the prescribed degrees. Additional connectivity requirements are retained only when the complete pairing is admissible for them.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong Connector and Strong Cut Min–Max Dualities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted integral dualities under acyclicity and source-to-sink reachability assumptions on the base digraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $D'=(V,A')$ be acyclic and suppose every source of $D'$ has a directed path to every sink of $D'$. For every digraph $D=(V,A)$: (a) for each $l:A\to\mathbb Z_+$, the minimum $l$-length of a strong connector equals the maximum cardinality of a multiset of strong cuts in which each arc $a$ occurs at most $l(a)$ times; (b) for each $c:A\to\mathbb Z_+$, the minimum $c$-capacity of a strong cut equals the maximum cardinality of a multiset of strong connectors in which each arc $a$ occurs at most $c(a)$ times.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the base digraph is acyclic and every source can reach every sink, then two integral min–max equalities hold for every second digraph on the same vertices. Minimum-length strong connectors equal maximum capacity-respecting multisets of strong cuts, and minimum-capacity strong cuts equal maximum capacity-respecting multisets of strong connectors.
assumptions_latex: \forall s\in\operatorname{src}(D')\ \forall t\in\operatorname{snk}(D'),\text{ there is an }s\text{-}t\text{ dipath in }D'
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{F\text{ strong connector}}l(F)=\max\{|\mathcal C|:\mathcal C\text{ is a multiset of strong cuts and }m_{\mathcal C}(a)\le l(a)\ \forall a\};\quad \min_{C\text{ strong cut}}c(C)=\max\{|\mathcal F|:\mathcal F\text{ is a multiset of strong connectors and }m_{\mathcal F}(a)\le c(a)\ \forall a\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semi-strongly polynomial strong-connector packing algorithm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algorithm for integer-capacitated strong-connector packing, including its fractional phase and iteration bounds but excluding the supplied complexity proof.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a source-sink connected digraph \(D_0=(V,A_0)\), a digraph \(D=(V,A)\), and \(c:A\to\mathbb Z_+\), an optimum fractional packing of strong connectors subject to \(c\) can be found in strongly polynomial time. At each outer iteration, compute \(\kappa=\min_{U\in\mathcal C}c(\delta_A^{\mathrm{in}}(U))\), where \(\mathcal C=\{U:\varnothing\ne U\subset V,\ d_{A_0}^{\mathrm{in}}(U)=0\}\); maintain tight sets \(\mathcal U\); choose a strong connector \(B\) satisfying \(d_B^{\mathrm{in}}(U)=1\) for all \(U\in\mathcal U\); select the maximal rational decrement \(\lambda\) by the stated minimum-cut updates; and replace \((c,\kappa)\) by \((c-\lambda\chi^B,\kappa-\lambda)\). There are at most \(|A|+|V|^3\) outer iterations and at most \(|B|\) inner iterations per outer iteration. Rounding the optimum fractional packing yields an optimum integer packing in semi-strongly polynomial time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a source-sink connected D0 and nonnegative integer arc capacities, repeated minimum-cut computations, tight-set maintenance, and capacity subtraction along carefully chosen strong connectors find an optimal fractional packing in strongly polynomial time. The algorithm uses at most |A|+|V|^3 outer iterations and at most |B| inner updates in an outer iteration; rounding then gives an optimal integer packing in semi-strongly polynomial time.
assumptions_latex: D=(V,A)\text{ is a digraph on the same vertex set.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{An optimum fractional strong-connector packing is computable in strongly polynomial time, and an optimum integer packing in semi-strongly polynomial time, with at most }|A|+|V|^3\text{ outer iterations and }|B|\text{ inner iterations per outer iteration.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong connectors as covers of directed augmentation cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines relative directed cuts and characterizes strong connectors by hitting all such cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_0=(V,A_0)\) and \(D=(V,A)\) be digraphs. A subset \(A'\subseteq A\) is a \(D_0\)-cut in \(D\) if \(A'=\delta_A^{\mathrm{in}}(U)\) for some \(\varnothing\ne U\subsetneq V\) satisfying \(\delta_{A_0}^{\mathrm{in}}(U)=\varnothing\). For every \(B\subseteq A\), \(B\) is a strong connector for \(D_0\) if and only if \(B\cap A'\ne\varnothing\) for every \(D_0\)-cut \(A'\) in \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A D0-cut consists of the candidate arcs entering a nonempty proper vertex set that has no entering arc in D0. A set of candidate arcs is a strong connector for D0 exactly when it intersects every such cut.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong Connectors and Strong Cuts Relative to a Digraph
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions for two digraphs sharing a vertex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $D=(V,A)$ and $D'=(V,A')$. A set $F\subseteq A$ is a strong connector for $D'$ if $(V,A'\cup F)$ is strongly connected. A set $C\subseteq A$ is a strong cut induced by $D'$ if there exists $\varnothing\ne S\subsetneq V$ such that $\delta^-_{D'}(S)=\varnothing$ and $C=\delta^-_D(S)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given two digraphs on the same vertices, a strong connector is a set of arcs from the first whose addition to the second makes it strongly connected. A strong cut is the set of arcs of the first entering a nonempty proper vertex set that no arc of the second enters.
assumptions_latex: D=(V,A)\text{ and }D'=(V,A')\text{ are digraphs on the same vertex set }V
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\subseteq A\text{ is a strong connector iff }(V,A'\cup F)\text{ is strongly connected; }C\subseteq A\text{ is a strong cut iff }C=\delta^-_D(S)\text{ for some }\varnothing\ne S\subsetneq V\text{ with }\delta^-_{D'}(S)=\varnothing.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong connectors: hardness and tractable cases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combines the defining augmentation property with stated complexity and tractability boundaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A strong connector for a digraph \(D\) is a set of new arcs whose addition makes \(D\) strongly connected. With lengths assigned to potential new arcs, finding a minimum-length strong connector is NP-complete even when \(D\) has no arcs, and remains NP-complete for lengths in \(\{0,1\}\). For source-sink connected digraphs, minimum strong connectors and strong-connector packing are tractable, with associated min-max and polyhedral characterizations obtainable through directed cut covers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strong connector is a set of added arcs that makes a digraph strongly connected. The minimum-length problem is NP-complete even for an initially arc-free digraph and zero-one lengths. Source-sink connected digraphs form a tractable case admitting min-max and polyhedral results, and their packing problem is also tractable.
assumptions_latex: \text{Each potential added arc has an assigned length}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Minimum-length strong connector is NP-complete in general, even for }A=\varnothing\text{ and lengths in }\{0,1\};\text{ source-sink connected instances are tractable.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Separation of Lower and Upper In-Degree Feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between simultaneous two-sided bounds and separate one-sided strongly connected orientations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a 2-edge-connected undirected graph and let \(l,u\in\mathbb Z_+^V\) with \(l\le u\). Then \(G\) has a strongly connected orientation \(D=(V,A)\) satisfying \(l(v)\le\deg_A^{\mathrm{in}}(v)\le u(v)\) for every \(v\in V\) if and only if it has strongly connected orientations \(D'=(V,A')\) and \(D''=(V,A'')\) such that \(l(v)\le\deg_{A'}^{\mathrm{in}}(v)\) and \(\deg_{A''}^{\mathrm{in}}(v)\le u(v)\) for every \(v\in V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simultaneous lower and upper in-degree bounds are feasible in one strong orientation exactly when the lower bounds and upper bounds are each feasible in possibly different strong orientations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}&\exists D\text{ strongly connected}:l(v)\le\deg_D^{\mathrm{in}}(v)\le u(v)\ \forall v\\&\iff\exists D',D''\text{ strongly connected}:l(v)\le\deg_{D'}^{\mathrm{in}}(v)\ \land\ \deg_{D''}^{\mathrm{in}}(v)\le u(v)\ \forall v.\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subpartition Criterion for In-Degree-Constrained k-Arc-Connected Orientations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes feasibility of a k-arc-connected orientation satisfying prescribed lower and upper vertex in-degree bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $G=(V,E)$ be a $2k$-connected undirected graph and let $l,u\in\mathbb Z_+^V$ satisfy $l\le u$. Then $G$ has a $k$-arc-connected orientation $D$ satisfying $l(v)\le \deg_D^{\mathrm{in}}(v)\le u(v)$ for every $v\in V$ if and only if, for every subpartition $\mathcal P$ of $V$ with nonempty classes, writing $W:=V\setminus\bigcup\mathcal P$, $$|E[W]|+|\delta(\mathcal P)|\ge k|\mathcal P|+\max\left\{\sum_{v\in W}l(v),\sum_{v\in W}(\deg_G(v)-u(v))\right\}.$$
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A 2k-connected undirected graph admits a k-arc-connected orientation satisfying all vertexwise in-degree bounds exactly when the stated inequality holds for every subpartition of its vertex set.
assumptions_latex: $\mathcal P$ ranges over subpartitions of $V$ with nonempty classes, with $W:=V\setminus\bigcup\mathcal P$.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists D\,\bigl[D\text{ is }k\text{-arc-connected and }l(v)\le\deg_D^{\mathrm{in}}(v)\le u(v)\ \forall v\in V\bigr]\iff\forall\mathcal P,\ |E[W]|+|\delta(\mathcal P)|\ge k|\mathcal P|+\max\left\{\sum_{v\in W}l(v),\sum_{v\in W}(\deg_G(v)-u(v))\right\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Simultaneous lower and upper indegree feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An interpolation property for supermodular-covering orientations with separate feasible lower and upper indegree bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\), let \(h\) be a nonnegative crossing \(G\)-supermodular set function, and let \(f,g:V\to\mathbb Z\) satisfy \(0\le f\le g\). Suppose there is an orientation covering \(h\) whose indegrees satisfy \(\varrho'(v)\ge f(v)\) for every \(v\in V\), and there is an orientation covering \(h\) whose indegrees satisfy \(\varrho''(v)\le g(v)\) for every \(v\in V\). Then there is an orientation covering \(h\) whose indegrees satisfy \[f(v)\le\varrho(v)\le g(v)\qquad\text{for every }v\in V.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a supermodular-covering orientation can separately meet all lower indegree bounds and all upper indegree bounds, then one covering orientation can meet both sets of bounds simultaneously.
assumptions_latex: \exists\text{ a covering orientation with }\varrho'(v)\ge f(v)\ \forall v
\exists\text{ a covering orientation with }\varrho''(v)\le g(v)\ \forall v
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\text{ an orientation covering }h\text{ such that }f(v)\le\varrho(v)\le g(v)\text{ for every }v\in V

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cut Characterization for In-Degree-Bounded Strong Orientations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient conditions for a strong orientation satisfying lower and upper in-degree bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a 2-edge-connected undirected graph and let \(l,u\in\mathbb Z_+^V\) with \(l\le u\). There exists a strongly connected orientation \(D=(V,A)\) satisfying \(l(v)\le \deg_A^{\mathrm{in}}(v)\le u(v)\) for every \(v\in V\) if and only if, for every \(U\subseteq V\), \[|E[U]|+\kappa(G-U)\le u(U)\] and \[|E[U]|+|\delta(U)|-\kappa(G-U)\ge l(U).\]

\[
