knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The digraph \(D\) is outwardly rooted \(k\)-edge-connected with root \(r\) if
\[
\lambda_D(r,v)\geq k\qquad\text{for every }v\in V\setminus\{r\}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\rho_D(X)\geq k\qquad\text{for every nonempty }X\subseteq V\setminus\{r\}.
\]
The inwardly rooted convention requires \(\lambda_D(v,r)\geq k\) for every \(v\in V\setminus\{r\}\), equivalently \(\delta_D(X)\geq k\) for every nonempty \(X\subseteq V\setminus\{r\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An outwardly rooted k-edge-connected digraph has k arc-disjoint directed paths from the root to every other vertex, equivalently at least k arcs enter every nonempty root-free set. The inward convention reverses the path directions and uses leaving cuts.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polynomial removable-edge or tight-partition procedure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses max-flow/min-cut computations to construct either a removability witness or a tight-partition obstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given the setting of the removable-root-edge characterization, a polynomial algorithm either finds a $k$-tight partition separating $r_0$ from $R$, or finds $f\in F$ together with an $r_0$-rooted $k$-edge-connected reorientation of $D-f$. Its tight-set subroutine computes $\lambda_D(r_0,v)$ by max-flow/min-cut: if $\lambda_D(r_0,v)>k$, then $v$ belongs to no tight subset of $V-r_0$; if $\lambda_D(r_0,v)=k$, it computes the smallest set $T(v)\subseteq V-r_0$ containing $v$ with $\varrho_D(T(v))=k$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polynomial max-flow/min-cut based procedure either returns a tight partition separating the root from the specified heads or deletes an appropriate root edge and produces a rooted k-edge-connected reorientation. For each queried vertex, the same routine detects whether it lies in a tight nonroot set and computes the smallest such set when one exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{In polynomial time, output either a separating }k\text{-tight partition, or }(f,D')\text{ with }f\in F\text{ and }D'\text{ an }r_0\text{-rooted }k\text{-edge-connected reorientation of }D-f.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partition connectivity and rooted orientation characterization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the undirected partition condition underlying rooted edge-connected orientations and records its characterization role.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A graph $G=(V,E)$ is $k$-partition-connected if, for every partition $\mathcal P$ of $V$ into nonempty parts, $e_G(\mathcal P)\ge k(|\mathcal P|-1)$, where $e_G(\mathcal P)$ is the number of edges joining distinct parts. A graph admits an orientation rooted $k$-edge-connected with respect to a designated root precisely when it is $k$-partition-connected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A graph is k-partition-connected when every partition into nonempty parts has at least k times one less than the number of parts crossing edges. This condition characterizes graphs admitting a rooted k-edge-connected orientation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G\text{ admits an }r_0\text{-rooted }k\text{-edge-connected orientation}\iff \forall\mathcal P,\ e_G(\mathcal P)\ge k(|\mathcal P|-1).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Root-Out-Degree Criteria for Rooted k-Connectivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives separate necessary-and-sufficient inequalities for rooted node-connectivity and rooted edge-connectivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) have root \(r_0\), put \(D^*=D-r_0\), and let \(\gamma\in\mathbb Z\). The digraph \(D\) admits a rooted \(k\)-node-connected subgraph with \(d^+(r_0)\le\gamma\) if and only if, for every family of nonempty bi-sets \(X_1,\ldots,X_q\) whose outer members lie in \(V^*\) and whose inner members are pairwise disjoint, \(\sum_i[k-(\varrho_{D^*}(X_i)+w(X_i))]\le\gamma\). It admits a rooted \(k\)-edge-connected subgraph with \(d^+(r_0)\le\gamma\) if and only if, for every family of pairwise disjoint subsets \(X_i\subseteq V^*\), \(\sum_i[k-\varrho_{D^*}(X_i)]\le\gamma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A root-out-degree-bounded rooted k-node-connected subgraph exists exactly when the stated bi-set deficit sum never exceeds the bound γ. For rooted k-edge-connectivity, the analogous condition uses every family of pairwise disjoint subsets and their in-degree deficits.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\text{ rooted }k\text{-node-connected subgraph with }d^+(r_0)\le\gamma\iff \sum_i[k-(\varrho_{D^*}(X_i)+w(X_i))]\le\gamma\text{ for every admissible bi-set family};\quad \exists\text{ rooted }k\text{-edge-connected subgraph with }d^+(r_0)\le\gamma\iff \sum_i[k-\varrho_{D^*}(X_i)]\le\gamma\text{ for every pairwise-disjoint subset family}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partition Characterization of Rooted k-Edge-Connected Orientability of a Mixed Graph
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient partition condition for orienting the undirected edges of a mixed graph to obtain rooted directed edge-connectivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=(V,A+E)\) consist of the undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\) and directed graph \(D=(V,A)\), and let \(r_0\in V\). Then \(M\) has a rooted \(k\)-edge-connected orientation with respect to \(r_0\) if and only if, for every partition \(\mathcal P=\{V_0,V_1,\ldots,V_q\}\) of \(V\) with \(r_0\in V_0\), \[ e_G(\mathcal P)\ge \sum_{i=1}^{q}\bigl(k-\varrho_D(V_i)\bigr), \] where \(e_G(\mathcal P)\) is the number of edges of \(G\) joining distinct members of \(\mathcal P\), and \(\varrho_D(V_i)\) is the number of arcs of \(D\) entering \(V_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed graph admits an orientation of its undirected edges that is rooted k-edge-connected from the designated root if and only if every vertex partition, with the root in its distinguished part, has at least the total cross-edge supply required after accounting for the directed arcs already entering each non-root part.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal P=\{V_0,V_1,\ldots,V_q\}\text{ is any partition of }V\text{ with }r_0\in V_0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\text{ has a rooted }k\text{-edge-connected orientation with respect to }r_0\iff \forall\mathcal P,\quad e_G(\mathcal P)\ge\sum_{i=1}^{q}\bigl(k-\varrho_D(V_i)\bigr).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spanning trees with degree bounds on a stable set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the source's set-function notation \(\widetilde f_S,\widetilde g_S,\Gamma(Y)\), and \(\sigma(Y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a connected undirected graph, let \(S\subset V\) be stable, and let \(f_S:S\to\mathbf Z_+\cup\{-\infty\}\) and \(g_S:S\to\mathbf Z_+\cup\{+\infty\}\) satisfy \(f_S\le g_S\). (A) There is a spanning tree \(F\) with \(d_F(v)\ge f_S(v)\) for every \(v\in S\) if and only if \(\widetilde f_S(Y)\le |Y|+|\Gamma(Y)|-1\) for every nonempty \(Y\subseteq S\). (B) There is a spanning tree \(F\) with \(d_F(v)\le g_S(v)\) for every \(v\in S\) if and only if \(\widetilde g_S(Y)\ge |Y|+\sigma(Y)-1\) for every nonempty \(Y\subseteq S\). (C) There is a spanning tree satisfying \(f_S(v)\le d_F(v)\le g_S(v)\) for every \(v\in S\) if and only if both families of inequalities hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a connected graph and a stable vertex set, lower, upper, and two-sided degree constraints on a spanning tree are characterized by the stated inequalities over every nonempty subset of the stable set.
assumptions_latex: S\subset V\text{ is a stable set}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Parts (A)--(C) give necessary-and-sufficient conditions for the corresponding spanning-tree degree bounds.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tight sets, tight partitions, removable edges, and separating partitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Terminology for rooted edge-connected reorientation theory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $D=(V,A)$ be $r_0$-rooted $k$-edge-connected. Then every partition $\mathcal P=\{V_1,\ldots,V_q\}$ of $V$ satisfies $e_D(\mathcal P)=\sum_{i=1}^q\varrho_D(V_i)\ge k(|\mathcal P|-1)$. A set $X\subseteq V-r_0$ is tight if $\varrho_D(X)=k$, while a set $X\ni r_0$ is tight if $\varrho_D(X)=0$. A partition is $k$-tight when equality holds in the partition inequality, equivalently when every part is tight. An edge $f$ is removable if $D-f$ has an $r_0$-rooted $k$-edge-connected reorientation. A partition separates $r_0$ from $R\subseteq V-r_0$ if its part containing $r_0$ is disjoint from $R$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a rooted k-edge-connected digraph, every partition satisfies the corresponding crossing-edge lower bound. Tight sets and partitions attain their relevant in-degree bounds. A removable edge is one whose deletion permits a rooted k-edge-connected reorientation, and a partition separates the root from R when the root part avoids R.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: e_D(\mathcal P)\ge k(|\mathcal P|-1),\qquad \mathcal P\text{ is }k\text{-tight}\iff \text{every }V_i\text{ is tight}.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P'\) is finer than \(\mathcal P''\) precisely under the stated block-replacement condition.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rooted Orientation and Edge-Augmentation Min–Max Theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes rooted k-edge-connectable graphs by partition inequalities and gives the exact augmentation number.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be undirected, let \(r_0\in V\), and let \(k\ge 1\). Then \(G\) has a rooted \(k\)-edge-connected orientation if and only if \(e_G(\mathcal P)\ge k(q-1)\) for every partition \(\mathcal P=\{V_1,\ldots,V_q\}\) of \(V\). Moreover, the minimum number \(\gamma\) of new edges whose addition makes such an orientation possible is \(\gamma=\max_{\mathcal P}\{k(q-1)-e_G(\mathcal P)\}\), and the new edges may all be chosen incident to \(r_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An undirected graph admits a rooted k-edge-connected orientation exactly when every q-block vertex partition has at least k(q−1) crossing edges. The minimum number of edges needed to achieve this is the maximum partition deficit, and all added edges can be incident to the designated root.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G\text{ admits a rooted }k\text{-edge-connected orientation}\iff \forall\mathcal P,\ e_G(\mathcal P)\ge k(|\mathcal P|-1);\quad \gamma=\max_{\mathcal P}\bigl(k(|\mathcal P|-1)-e_G(\mathcal P)\bigr),\text{ with all added edges incident to }r_0.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tight Refinement Separating a Non-Removable Root Edge
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Provides a tight refinement of the root-containing block when a non-removable root edge lies inside it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be rooted \(k\)-edge-connected with respect to \(r_0\). Let \(\mathcal P=\{V_1,\ldots,V_q\}\) be \(k\)-tight with \(r_0\in V_1\), and let \(f=r_0v\) be non-removable with \(v\in V_1\). Then there is a partition \(\mathcal F=\{U_1,\ldots,U_p\}\) of \(V_1\) such that \(r_0\in U_1\), \(v\notin U_1\), and \(\mathcal P'=\{U_1,\ldots,U_p,V_2,\ldots,V_q\}\) is \(k\)-tight.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a non-removable edge from the root has both endpoints in the root block of a k-tight partition, that block can be refined so the endpoints are separated while the resulting partition remains k-tight.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\mathcal F=\{U_1,\ldots,U_p\}\) partitioning \(V_1\) with \(r_0\in U_1\), \(v\notin U_1\), such that \(\{U_1,\ldots,U_p,V_2,[0m\ldots,V_q\}\) is \(k\)-tight.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Construction of the Finest Tight Partition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteratively refines a tight partition using non-removable induced edges.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Start from any \(k\)-tight partition \(\mathcal P\). For each edge \(f=uv\) induced by a block, find \(k\) edge-disjoint \(r_0u\)-paths and reorient them so that the digraph becomes \(u\)-rooted \(k\)-edge-connected. Test whether \(f\) is removable. If it is removable, continue; otherwise replace \(\mathcal P\) by the \(k\)-tight refinement that separates the relevant endpoints and continue. The procedure terminates at a \(k\)-tight partition \(\mathcal P_0\) for which every edge induced by a block is removable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting with any k-tight partition, inspect edges lying within its blocks. Reorient k edge-disjoint root-to-endpoint paths to perform a removability test; retain the partition for removable edges and refine it for non-removable ones. The process ends with a k-tight partition whose block-induced edges are all removable.
assumptions_latex: The input digraph is rooted \(k\)-edge-connected with root \(r_0\).
The required edge-disjoint paths, removability test, and tight refinement can be constructed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{The algorithm terminates with a }k\text{-tight }\mathcal P_0\text{ such that every edge induced by a block of }\mathcal P_0\text{ is removable.}\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rooted k-edge-connected orientations with vertex indegree bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the source's notation \(\widetilde f,\widetilde g,e_G,i_G,h_k\) and \(\dot\varrho\) for the vertex-indegree vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a graph with root \(r_0\), and let \(f:V\to\mathbf Z_+\cup\{-\infty\}\) and \(g:V\to\mathbf Z_+\cup\{+\infty\}\) satisfy \(f\le g\). (A) A rooted \(k\)-edge-connected orientation with \(\dot\varrho\ge f\) exists if and only if \(G\) is \(k\)-partition-connected, \(\widetilde f(Z)\le e_G(Z)\) for every \(Z\subseteq V\), and, for every partition \(\mathcal P=\{V_0,V_1,\ldots,V_q\}\) of \(V\) with \(q\ge1\), \[e_G(\mathcal P)+i_G(V_0)\ge \widetilde f(V_0)+kq-h_k(V_0).\] (B) A rooted \(k\)-edge-connected orientation with \(\dot\varrho\le g\) exists if and only if \(G\) is \(k\)-partition-connected and \(\widetilde g(X)\ge i_G(X)+h_k(X)\) for every \(X\subseteq V\). (C) A rooted \(k\)-edge-connected orientation satisfying \(f\le\dot\varrho\le g\) exists if and only if orientations satisfying the lower and upper bounds separately both exist.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a rooted graph and compatible lower and upper vertex-indegree bounds, the theorem characterizes lower-bounded and upper-bounded rooted k-edge-connected orientations by partition-connectivity and the stated subset and partition inequalities. Simultaneous bounds are feasible exactly when the lower and upper systems are separately feasible.
assumptions_latex: G=(V,E)\text{ is a graph with designated root }r_0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Conditions (A), (B), and (C) give the stated necessary-and-sufficient characterizations.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Edge-pinching construction of \((k,\ell)\)-partition-connected graphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives an inductive construction precisely characterizing the undirected graphs satisfying the asymmetric partition bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected graph and let \(0\le \ell\le k\) be integers. Then \(G\) is \((k,\ell)\)-partition-connected if and only if it can be obtained from a single vertex by repeatedly applying either: \(\mathrm{(A)}\) add an edge between two existing vertices; or \(\mathrm{(B)}\) choose \(j\) existing edges with \(\ell\le j\le k\), pinch them together at a new vertex \(z\), and add \(k-j\) possibly parallel edges joining \(z\) to existing vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An undirected graph satisfies the (k,l)-partition-connectivity condition exactly when it can be built from one vertex using arbitrary added edges and an operation that pinches j existing edges at a new vertex and adds k−j edges from that vertex to old vertices, where l≤j≤k and parallel added edges are allowed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G\text{ is }(k,\ell)\text{-partition-connected}\iff G\text{ is constructible from one vertex by operations (A) and (B) with }\ell\le j\le k.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfers rooted edge connectivity from one root to another by reversing a prescribed family of edge-disjoint root-to-node dipaths.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Root-connected orientations with vertex indegree bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the source's notation \(\widetilde f,\widetilde g,e_G,i_G,\sigma_0\) and \(\dot\varrho\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a connected undirected graph with designated root \(r_0\), and let \(f:V\to\mathbf Z_+\cup\{-\infty\}\) and \(g:V\to\mathbf Z_+\cup\{+\infty\}\) satisfy \(f\le g\). (A) A root-connected orientation with \(\dot\varrho\ge f\) exists if and only if \(\widetilde f(X)\le e_G(X)-\sigma_0(X)\) for every \(X\subseteq V\). (B) A root-connected orientation with \(\dot\varrho\le g\) exists if and only if, for every \(X\subseteq V\), \[\widetilde g(X)\ge\begin{cases}i_G(X)+1,&\varnothing\ne X\subseteq V\setminus\{r_0\},\\ i_G(X),&r_0\in X\subseteq V.\end{cases}\] (C) A root-connected orientation satisfying \(f\le\dot\varrho\le g\) exists if and only if orientations satisfying the lower and upper bounds separately both exist.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A connected graph admits a root-connected orientation meeting prescribed lower or upper indegree bounds exactly under the stated subset inequalities. Both bounds can be met simultaneously exactly when each one can be met separately.
assumptions_latex: G=(V,E)\text{ is connected and undirected, with designated root }r_0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The lower, upper, and simultaneous indegree-bound feasibility claims are equivalent to the stated conditions.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rooted \((k,\ell)\)-edge-connectivity and partition-connectivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the asymmetric rooted orientation regime, its path interpretation and special cases, root independence, and the corresponding undirected partition condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonnegative integers \(k,\ell\), a digraph \(D=(V,A)\) is \((k,\ell)\)-edge-connected with root \(r_0\) if \(\varrho_D(X)\ge k\) and \(\delta_D(X)\ge \ell\) for every nonempty \(X\subseteq V-r_0\). Equivalently, for every \(v\ne r_0\), there are \(k\) edge-disjoint \(r_0\)-to-\(v\) paths and \(\ell\) edge-disjoint \(v\)-to-\(r_0\) paths. The case \(\ell=0\) is rooted \(k\)-edge-connectivity, and \(k=\ell\) is global \(k\)-edge-connectivity. If \(\ell\le k\), reversing \(k-\ell\) edge-disjoint paths from \(r_0\) to any \(r_1\) produces a \((k,\ell)\)-edge-connected orientation rooted at \(r_1\). An undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\) is \((k,\ell)\)-partition-connected if every partition of \(V\) into \(q\ge2\) nonempty parts has at least \(k(q-1)+\ell\) crossing edges.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rooted (k,l)-edge-connected digraph has at least k arcs entering and l arcs leaving every nonempty vertex set not containing the root; equivalently it has the stated edge-disjoint paths to and from every other vertex. This includes rooted and global edge-connectivity as special cases. When l is at most k, suitable path reversals can change the root. The associated undirected partition condition requires at least k(q−1)+l crossing edges for every partition into q at least two parts.
assumptions_latex: D=(V,A)\text{ is a digraph with root }r_0
G=(V,E)\text{ is an undirected graph for the partition-connectivity definition}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D\text{ is }(k,\ell)\text{-edge-connected exactly under the stated cut conditions, equivalently the stated path conditions; if }\ell\le k\text{ its root may be changed by path reversal, and }G\text{ is }(k,\ell)\text{-partition-connected exactly under the stated partition inequalities.}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The digraph \(D\) is globally \(k\)-edge-connected, also called \(k\)-arc-connected, if
\[
\lambda_D(u,v)\geq k\qquad\text{for all distinct }u,v\in V.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\rho_D(X)\geq k\qquad\text{for every nonempty proper subset }X\subset V.
\]
An orientation of an undirected graph is a global \(k\)-edge-connected orientation when its resulting digraph satisfies these equivalent conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A digraph is globally k-edge-connected when every ordered pair has k arc-disjoint directed paths, equivalently every nontrivial set has at least k entering arcs.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reconfiguration of k-Edge-Connected Orientations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Connectivity-preserving reorientation between two global k-edge-connected orientations of the same graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $D_1$ and $D_2$ be two $k$-edge-connected orientations of a graph $G$. Then there is a finite sequence of orientations beginning with $D_1$ and ending with $D_2$ such that each step reorients a directed path or directed circuit of the current orientation and every orientation in the sequence remains $k$-edge-connected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any two k-edge-connected orientations of the same graph can be connected by successively reversing directed paths or directed circuits while preserving k-edge-connectivity at every intermediate orientation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D_2\text{ is reachable from }D_1\text{ by successive reorientations of current dipaths and directed circuits, with every intermediate orientation }k\text{-edge-connected.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence of a globally edge-connected orientation that simultaneously preserves prescribed edge connectivity on edge-partition subgraphs.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partition Criteria for Degree-Bounded k-Edge-Connected Orientations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives separate and simultaneous characterizations for lower and upper indegree bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k\ge1\), let \(G=(V,E)\) be \(2k\)-edge-connected, and let \(f:V\to\mathbb Z_+\cup\{-\infty\}\) and \(g:V\to\mathbb Z_+\cup\{\infty\}\) satisfy \(f\le g\). There is a \(k\)-edge-connected orientation with \(\dot\varrho\ge f\) if and only if \(\widetilde f(V)\le |E|\) and, for every partition \(\mathcal P=\{V_0,V_1,\ldots,V_q\}\) of \(V\), \[i_G(V_0)+e_G(\mathcal P)\ge \widetilde f(V_0)+kq.\] There is one with \(\dot\varrho\le g\) if and only if \(\widetilde g(V)\ge |E|\) and, for every such partition, \[e_G(V_0)-e_G(\mathcal P)\le \widetilde g(V_0)-kq.\] A \(k\)-edge-connected orientation satisfying \(f\le\dot\varrho\le g\) exists if and only if both partition inequalities hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a 2k-edge-connected graph and compatible vertex bounds f and g, lower-bounded and upper-bounded k-edge-connected orientations exist exactly under the stated total-sum and partition inequalities; simultaneous bounds are feasible exactly when both partition inequalities hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}\exists D\,[D\text{ is }k\text{-edge-connected},\ \dot\varrho_D\ge f]&\iff \widetilde f(V)\le|E|\ \land\ \forall\mathcal P,\ i_G(V_0)+e_G(\mathcal P)\ge\widetilde f(V_0)+kq,\\ \exists D\,[D\text{ is }k\text{-edge-connected},\ \dot\varrho_D\le g]&\iff \widetilde g(V)\ge|E|\ \land\ \forall\mathcal P,\ e_G(V_0)-e_G(\mathcal P)\le\widetilde g(V_0)-kq,\\ \exists D\,[D\text{ is }k\text{-edge-connected},\ f\le\dot\varrho_D\le g]&\iff\text{ both partition inequalities hold.}\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The root-centered \((k,\ell)\)-connectivity requirements at \(r\) are
\[
\lambda_D(r,v)\geq k\quad\text{and}\quad\lambda_D(v,r)\geq\ell
\qquad(v\in V\setminus\{r\}).
\]
By directed cut characterizations, these hold exactly when
\[
\rho_D(X)\geq k\quad\text{and}\quad\delta_D(X)\geq\ell
\qquad\text{for every nonempty }X\subseteq V\setminus\{r\}.
\]
The parameters may differ, so outward and inward root connectivity are independently prescribed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Root-centered (k,l) connectivity requires k arc-disjoint paths from the root to every vertex and l in the reverse direction, equivalently corresponding cut inequalities.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(X\subseteq V\), let \(\rho_D(X)\) count arcs with tail in \(V\setminus X\) and head in \(X\), and let \(\delta_D(X)\) count arcs with tail in \(X\) and head in \(V\setminus X\). The orientation \(D\) satisfies the global \(k\)-connectivity requirement if
\[\rho_D(X)\ge k\qquad(\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq V).\]
Since \(\delta_D(X)=\rho_D(V\setminus X)\), this is equivalent to requiring both \(\rho_D(X)\ge k\) and \(\delta_D(X)\ge k\) for every nonempty proper \(X\subset V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every nontrivial vertex cut must have at least k oriented edges entering it, equivalently at least k arcs in each direction across the cut.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A rooted orientation \((D,r)\) satisfies the mixed \((k,\ell)\)-connectivity regime when every nonempty proper set obeys
\[\rho_D(X)\ge
\begin{cases}
k,&r\notin X,\\
\ell,&r\in X.
\end{cases}\]
Equivalently, every cut separating \(r\) from \(X\subseteq V\setminus\{r\}\) has at least \(k\) arcs directed from the root side toward \(X\) and at least \(\ell\) arcs directed from \(X\) toward the root side. Thus \(k\) and \(\ell\) independently control the two directions of rooted cut connectivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Across every root-separating cut, at least k arcs point away from the root side and at least ell point toward it.

children.title: Asymmetric Directional Requirements
children.top_down_role: Orientation regimes with unequal connectivity requirements in opposite directions.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite undirected multigraph and \(D\) is an orientation of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D\) meets the directional requirements exactly when \(\rho_D(X)\ge p(X)\) and \(\delta_D(X)\ge q(X)\) for every \(\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq V\).

notation.meaning: Numbers of arcs entering and leaving X, respectively.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(X\subseteq V\), let \(\rho_D(X)\) and \(\delta_D(X)\) denote the numbers of arcs entering and leaving \(X\). The orientation \(D\) satisfies the asymmetric directional system \((p,q)\) if
\[\rho_D(X)\ge p(X)\quad\text{and}\quad\delta_D(X)\ge q(X)\qquad(\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq V).\]
Because \(\delta_D(X)=\rho_D(V\setminus X)\), the same system can be written solely with in-cuts as
\[\rho_D(X)\ge\max\{p(X),q(V\setminus X)\}\qquad(\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq V).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each proper vertex set receives separate lower bounds on arcs entering and leaving it; complementary cuts combine these into one in-cut requirement.

children.top_down_role: Structural interaction between distinguished-root requirements and directional asymmetry.

assumptions_latex: \(D=(V,A)\) is a finite digraph with distinguished root \(r\in V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rooted outward and inward requirements are precisely the asymmetric cut system induced by \(p_r\) and \(q_r\).

notation.meaning: Number of arcs entering X.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Encoding rooted two-directional connectivity as an asymmetric set-function system.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define requirement functions on nonempty proper \(X\subset V\) by
\[p_r(X)=\begin{cases}k,&r\notin X,\\0,&r\in X,\end{cases}
\qquad
q_r(X)=\begin{cases}\ell,&r\notin X,\\0,&r\in X.\end{cases}\]
Then the asymmetric conditions \(\rho_D(X)\ge p_r(X)\) and \(\delta_D(X)\ge q_r(X)\) assert that every \(X\subseteq V\setminus\{r\}\), \(X\ne\varnothing\), has at least \(k\) entering arcs and at least \(\ell\) leaving arcs. Using \(\delta_D(X)=\rho_D(V\setminus X)\), these are exactly the two directional requirements across every root-separating cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rooted outward and inward connectivity are an asymmetric cut system obtained by assigning different entering and leaving demands to sets excluding the root.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Orientation Lemma for Prescribed In-Degrees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent subset criteria for realizing an integer vertex function as the in-degree vector of an orientation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $G=(V,E)$ be an undirected graph and $m:V\to\mathbb Z$ satisfy $\widetilde m(V)=|E|$, where $\widetilde m(X)=\sum_{v\in X}m(v)$. Then the following are equivalent: (i) $G$ has an orientation with $\varrho(v)=m(v)$ for every $v\in V$; (ii) $e_G(X)\ge\widetilde m(X)$ for every $X\subseteq V$; and (iii) $i_G(Y)\le\widetilde m(Y)$ for every $Y\subseteq V$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the prescribed in-degrees sum to the number of edges, an undirected graph admits an orientation realizing them exactly if and only if either of the equivalent subset edge-count inequalities holds for every vertex subset.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl[\exists\text{ an orientation of }G:\forall v\in V,\ \varrho(v)=m(v)\bigr]\iff\bigl[\forall X\subseteq V,\ e_G(X)\ge\widetilde m(X)\bigr]\iff\bigl[\forall Y\subseteq V,\ i_G(Y)\le\widetilde m(Y)\bigr].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Landau Characterization of Tournament In-Degree Sequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient inequalities for a nonincreasing integer sequence to be realized as the in-degree sequence of a tournament.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $m_1\ge m_2\ge\cdots\ge m_n$. The sequence is the in-degree sequence of a tournament on $n$ vertices if and only if $\sum_{i=1}^n m_i=\binom n2$ and, for every $k=1,\ldots,n$, $\sum_{i=1}^k m_i\le \binom k2+k(n-k)$. Equivalently, the total-sum equality may be combined with $\sum_{i=n-h+1}^n m_i\ge\binom h2$ for every $h=1,\ldots,n$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonincreasing sequence is realizable as the in-degree sequence of a tournament exactly when its total is the number of tournament arcs and every prefix satisfies the stated upper bound. Equivalently, every suffix of length h has sum at least h choose 2, together with the total-sum equality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (m_i)_{i=1}^n\text{ is a tournament in-degree sequence}\iff\left[\sum_{i=1}^n m_i=\binom n2\ \land\ \forall k\in\{1,\ldots,n\},\ \sum_{i=1}^k m_i\le\binom k2+k(n-k)\right].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bipartite prescribed-degree spanning trees as root-connected orientations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Here \(V=S\cup T\), and \(d(v)\) denotes the degree of \(v\) in the original bipartite graph.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Orientation Criterion for an F-Avoiding Subgraph
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An orientation-based sufficient condition for a spanning subgraph that avoids prescribed vertex degrees.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: k-Sparse Vertex Sets and the Forest-Partition Characterization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines induced-edge k-sparsity and records its equivalent forest-decomposition condition for the whole graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected graph. A set \(Z\subseteq V\) is \(k\)-sparse if \(i_G(X)\le k(|X|-1)\) for every nonempty \(X\subseteq Z\), where \(i_G(X)\) is the number of edges induced by \(X\). The graph \(G\) is \(k\)-sparse when \(V\) is \(k\)-sparse. Moreover, \(E\) can be partitioned into \(k\) forests if and only if \(G\) is \(k\)-sparse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vertex set is k-sparse when every nonempty subset induces at most k times one less than its number of vertices edges. A graph is k-sparse when its full vertex set has this property, equivalently when its edges can be partitioned into k forests.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Z\text{ is }k\text{-sparse}\iff \forall\varnothing\ne X\subseteq Z:\ i_G(X)\le k(|X|-1);\qquad E\text{ is partitionable into }k\text{ forests}\iff V\text{ is }k\text{-sparse}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bipartite Strong-Orientation In-Degree Min-Max Formula
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum aggregate in-degree into one side of a strongly oriented 2-edge-connected bipartite graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let G=(S,T;E) be a 2-edge-connected bipartite graph, and let \mu(G) be the minimum number of edges entering T among all strongly connected orientations of G. Then
\[
\mu(G)=\max\left\{\sum_{i=1}^{t}\sigma_G(T_i):\{T_1,\ldots,T_t\}\text{ is a partition of }T\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a 2-edge-connected bipartite graph, the minimum number of edges entering T in a strong orientation equals the maximum, over all partitions of T, of the sum of the corresponding sigma values.
assumptions_latex: \mu(G)=\min\{|\delta^-_{\vec G}(T)|:\vec G\text{ is a strongly connected orientation of }G\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mu(G)=\max_{\{T_1,\ldots,T_t\}\text{ partition of }T}\sum_{i=1}^{t}\sigma_G(T_i).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Path-Reorientation Algorithm for Minimum In-Degree Strong Orientations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative optimization of the number of edges entering one color class while preserving strong connectivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Start with any strong orientation of a bipartite graph G=(S,T;E). While there exist s\in S and t\in T joined by two edge-disjoint st-paths, detect such paths (for example by repeated max-flow/min-cut computations) and reorient one of them so that strong connectivity is preserved and |\delta^-(T)| decreases by one. When no such pair exists, the resulting strong orientation minimizes |\delta^-(T)|. If P(t) is determined for every t\in T as in the associated terminal characterization, the components of the hypergraph \{P(t):t\in T\} form an optimal partition of T for the corresponding min-max formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Begin with any strong orientation. Repeatedly find two edge-disjoint s-to-t paths with s in S and t in T and reorient one path in the prescribed way; each iteration preserves strong connectivity and reduces the in-degree of T by one. When no such pair remains, the orientation is optimal, and the components of the sets P(t) give an optimal partition of T.
assumptions_latex: G=(S,T;E)\text{ is bipartite and admits a strong orientation}
\text{the prescribed path reorientation preserves strong connectivity and decreases }|\delta^-(T)|\text{ by one}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{At termination, }|\delta^-(T)|\text{ is minimum over strong orientations, and the components of }\{P(t):t\in T\}\text{ form an optimal partition of }T.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subset Edge-Count Criterion for an F-Avoiding Subgraph
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A cut-indexed sufficient condition for the existence of a spanning subgraph avoiding prescribed vertex degrees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected graph, and for each \(v\in V\) let \(F(v)\subseteq\{0,1,\ldots,d_G(v)\}\) be a set of forbidden degrees. If \(e_G(X)\ge \sum_{v\in X}|F(v)|\) for every \(X\subseteq V\), then there exists a spanning subgraph \(G'=(V,E')\) such that \(d_{G'}(v)\notin F(v)\) for every \(v\in V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every vertex subset has at least as many incident cut edges as the total number of forbidden degrees assigned to its vertices, then the graph has a spanning subgraph avoiding all prescribed forbidden degrees.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists E'\subseteq E\;\forall v\in V:\ d_{(V,E')}(v)\notin F(v)

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite undirected multigraph without loops.
\(f,g:V\to\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}\) satisfy \(f(v)\le g(v)\) for every \(v\in V\).

Lower and upper in-degree bounds.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an orientation \(D\) of \(G\), the in-degree \(d_D^-(v)\) is the number of edges of \(G\) oriented with head \(v\), counted with multiplicity. The orientation satisfies the vertex in-degree interval \([f,g]\) when
\[f(v)\le d_D^-(v)\le g(v)\qquad\text{for every }v\in V.\]
Because each edge has exactly one head, every such orientation also satisfies the identity \(\sum_{v\in V}d_D^-(v)=|E|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every vertex must receive a number of incoming edges lying between its prescribed lower and upper bounds.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact In-Degree Specification on a Vertex Subset
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes orientations realizing prescribed in-degrees on selected vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected graph, \(U\subseteq V\), and \(m:U\to\mathbb Z_+\). An orientation with \(\varrho(v)=m(v)\) for every \(v\in U\) exists if and only if, for every \(X\subseteq U\), \(i_G(X)\leq \widetilde m(X)\leq e_G(X)\), where \(\widetilde m(X)=\sum_{v\in X}m(v)\), \(i_G(X)\) counts edges with both ends in \(X\), and \(e_G(X)\) counts edges with at least one end in \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An undirected graph can be oriented to realize prescribed in-degrees on a selected vertex set exactly when, for every subset of selected vertices, the sum of its prescribed in-degrees lies between the numbers of internal and incident edges.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl(\exists\text{ an orientation with }\varrho(v)=m(v)\ \forall v\in U\bigr)\iff\bigl(i_G(X)\leq\widetilde m(X)\leq e_G(X)\ \forall X\subseteq U\bigr)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasibility Criteria for Vertex In-Degree Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subset characterizations for lower, upper, and simultaneous vertex in-degree bounds in orientations of an undirected graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $G=(V,E)$ be an undirected graph and let $f,g:V\to\mathbb Z$. Then: (A) $G$ has an orientation with $\varrho(v)\ge f(v)$ for every $v\in V$ if and only if $e_G(X)\ge\widetilde f(X)$ for every $X\subseteq V$; (B) $G$ has an orientation with $\varrho(v)\le g(v)$ for every $v\in V$ if and only if $i_G(X)\le\widetilde g(X)$ for every $X\subseteq V$; and (C) $G$ has an orientation with $f(v)\le\varrho(v)\le g(v)$ for every $v\in V$ if and only if both families of subset inequalities hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lower in-degree bounds are orientable exactly when every subset satisfies the corresponding incident-edge lower condition; upper bounds are orientable exactly when every subset satisfies the internal-edge upper condition. Simultaneous lower and upper bounds are feasible exactly when both conditions hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}&\exists\mathcal O:\ \varrho_{\mathcal O}\ge f\iff \forall X\subseteq V,\ e_G(X)\ge\widetilde f(X),\\&\exists\mathcal O:\ \varrho_{\mathcal O}\le g\iff \forall X\subseteq V,\ i_G(X)\le\widetilde g(X),\\&\exists\mathcal O:\ f\le\varrho_{\mathcal O}\le g\iff\left(\forall X\subseteq V,\ e_G(X)\ge\widetilde f(X)\right)\land\left(\forall X\subseteq V,\ i_G(X)\le\widetilde g(X)\right).\end{aligned}

children.title: Joint Degree Feasibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility regimes for simultaneous incoming-degree and outgoing-degree bounds.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite undirected multigraph without loops.
\(a^-,b^-,a^+,b^+:V\to\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) are prescribed lower and upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Joint feasibility is equivalent to existence of an orientation satisfying the displayed in-degree intervals together with their induced out-degree intervals.

notation.meaning: Degree of v in the underlying undirected multigraph.
In-degree and out-degree in orientation D.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduction of paired in-out bounds to intersected in-degree intervals.

source_refs.locator: 2.3 Degree-constrained orientations p. 58

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The four bounds are jointly feasible when an orientation \(D\) exists such that
\[a^-(v)\le d_D^-(v)\le b^-(v),\qquad a^+(v)\le d_D^+(v)\le b^+(v)\quad(v\in V).\]
Since \(d_D^-(v)+d_D^+(v)=d_G(v)\), this is equivalent to the existence of an orientation satisfying
\[\max\{a^-(v),d_G(v)-b^+(v)\}\le d_D^-(v)\le
\min\{b^-(v),d_G(v)-a^+(v)\}\quad(v\in V).\]
In particular, every resulting interval must have its lower endpoint at most its upper endpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Paired in-out bounds are feasible exactly when one orientation meets the in-degree intervals obtained by intersecting the direct and complementary out-degree constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Joint Degree Feasibility

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An orientation \(D\) of \(G\) is feasible for the connectivity-and-degree instance when
\[\rho_D(X)\ge k\qquad(\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq V)\]
and, simultaneously,
\[a^-(v)\le d_D^-(v)\le b^-(v),\qquad a^+(v)\le d_D^+(v)\le b^+(v)\qquad(v\in V).\]
The cut inequalities impose global \(k\)-arc-connectivity, while the vertex inequalities impose local degree control. Feasibility means that one orientation satisfies both families; satisfying them in two different orientations is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One orientation must be globally k-arc-connected while simultaneously meeting every prescribed incoming and outgoing degree interval.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong Orientations with Vertex Indegree Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes existence of strongly connected orientations satisfying lower, upper, or simultaneous vertex-indegree bounds. The notation $\widetilde f$, $\widetilde g$, $e_G$, $i_G$, $\sigma$, and $\dot\varrho$ is retained from the extract; notably, its prose and displayed expansion for the upper-bound condition use different graph-set symbols.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $f:V\to\mathbb Z_+\cup\{-\infty\}$ and $g:V\to\mathbb Z_+\cup\{\infty\}$ satisfy $f\le g$, and let $G=(V,E)$ be a $2$-edge-connected undirected graph. Then $G$ has a strongly connected orientation satisfying: (A) $\dot\varrho\ge f$ if and only if $\widetilde f\le e_G-\sigma$, equivalently $\widetilde f(X)\le e_G(X)-\sigma(X)$ for every $X\subseteq V$; (B) $\dot\varrho\le g$ if and only if $\widetilde g\ge e_G+\sigma$, whose displayed subset condition in the extract is $\widetilde g(X)\ge i_G(X)+\sigma(X)$ for every $X\subseteq V$; and (C) $f\le\dot\varrho\le g$ if and only if both subset conditions hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a 2-edge-connected undirected graph and compatible extended-integer lower and upper vertex bounds, the existence of a strongly connected orientation meeting the lower bounds, upper bounds, or both is characterized by the corresponding cut-indexed inequalities for every vertex subset. The extract uses e_G in its summary of the upper condition but i_G in the displayed inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}&\exists\text{ a strongly connected orientation with }\dot\varrho\ge f\iff \forall X\subseteq V,\ \widetilde f(X)\le e_G(X)-\sigma(X);\\&\exists\text{ a strongly connected orientation with }\dot\varrho\le g\iff \forall X\subseteq V,\ \widetilde g(X)\ge i_G(X)+\sigma(X);\\&\exists\text{ a strongly connected orientation with }f\le\dot\varrho\le g\iff\text{ both displayed subset conditions hold.}\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An \(h\)-covering orientation is an orientation \(D\) satisfying \(\rho_D(X)\ge h(X)\) for every \(X\subseteq V\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an orientation \(D\) of \(G\) and a set \(X\subseteq V\), let \(\rho_D(X)\) be the number of edges directed from \(V\setminus X\) into \(X\). The orientation covers the set in-degree requirement \(h\) when
\[\rho_D(X)\ge h(X)\qquad\text{for every }X\subseteq V.\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bipartite Dijoin–Dicut Packing Theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Min-max equality and cross-free optimal packing for a consistently oriented bipartite graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let G=(S,T;E) be a bipartite graph, and let \overrightarrow G=(V,\overrightarrow E) be obtained by orienting every edge of G toward T. Then the minimum cardinality of a dijoin of \overrightarrow G equals the maximum number \nu(\overrightarrow G) of pairwise edge-disjoint dicuts. Moreover, some maximum family of pairwise edge-disjoint dicuts is cross-free.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When every edge of a bipartite graph is directed toward T, the smallest dijoin has the same size as the largest family of edge-disjoint dicuts, and a maximum such family can be chosen cross-free.
assumptions_latex: \overrightarrow G\text{ is obtained by orienting every edge of }G\text{ toward }T
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min\{|F|:F\text{ is a dijoin of }\overrightarrow G\}=\nu(\overrightarrow G)=\max\{|\mathcal C|:\mathcal C\text{ is a family of pairwise edge-disjoint dicuts}\},\quad\text{and an optimal }\mathcal C\text{ may be chosen cross-free}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Min–max formula for a minimum k-source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Here S_k is the set of vertices having in-degree at least k, and the maximum ranges over all subpartitions of S_k.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a digraph and \(S_k:=\{v\in V:\varrho_D(v)\ge k\}\). The minimum cardinality of a \(k\)-source equals
\[
|V\setminus S_k|+\max\left\{\sum_{i=1}^{t}\bigl(k-|\Gamma^-(X_i)|\bigr):\{X_1,\ldots,X_t\}\text{ is a subpartition of }S_k\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a directed graph, the minimum size of a k-source is the number of vertices whose in-degree is below k plus the maximum, over subpartitions of the vertices whose in-degree is at least k, of the sum of k minus each part's in-neighborhood size.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min\{|Q|:Q\text{ is a }k\text{-source}\}=|V\setminus S_k|+\max_{\{X_i\}\text{ subpartition of }S_k}\sum_i\left(k-|\Gamma^-(X_i)|\right).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounded parity-outdegree orientation criterion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes feasible orientations by component inequalities over every three-partition of the vertex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected graph and let \(l,u\in\mathbb Z_+^V\) satisfy \(l(v)\equiv u(v)\pmod 2\) for every \(v\in V\). There is an orientation \(D\) satisfying \(l(v)\leq\deg_D^{\mathrm{out}}(v)\leq u(v)\) and \(\deg_D^{\mathrm{out}}(v)\equiv u(v)\pmod 2\) for every \(v\) if and only if, for every partition \(T,U,W\) of \(V\), the number of components \(K\) of \(G[T]\) for which \(u(K)+|E[K]|+|E[K,U]|\) is odd is at most \(u(U)-l(W)-|E[U]|+|E[W]|+|\delta(W)|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An undirected graph admits an orientation whose outdegrees satisfy the prescribed lower bounds, upper bounds, and parity exactly when the stated component-count inequality holds for every partition of the vertices into T, U, and W.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists D\text{ satisfying the stated outdegree bounds and parities}\iff\forall\text{ partitions }(T,U,W)\text{ of }V,\ \#\{K\in\operatorname{comp}(G[T]):u(K)+|E[K]|+|E[K,U]|\text{ is odd}\}\leq u(U)-l(W)-|E[U]|+|E[W]|+|\delta(W)|

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cut Criterion for a k-Edge-Connected Partial Orientation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes when a selected edge set can be directed while preserving k-edge connectivity in the resulting mixed graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let G=(V,E) be a k-edge-connected graph and let E'\subseteq E. The edges of E' can be oriented so that the resulting mixed graph is k-edge-connected if and only if d_{E'}(X)\le 2\bigl(d_E(X)-k\bigr) for every nonempty proper subset X\subset V.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A selected subset of edges in a k-edge-connected graph can be oriented while leaving a k-edge-connected mixed graph exactly when, across every nonempty proper vertex cut, the number of selected edges is at most twice the cut's excess over k.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\text{ an orientation of }E'\text{ producing a }k\text{-edge-connected mixed graph}\iff d_{E'}(X)\le 2(d_E(X)-k)\quad\forall\,\emptyset\ne X\subset V.

assumptions_latex: \(H=(V,\mathcal E)\) is a finite hypergraph with every \(e\in\mathcal E\) nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An orientation selects one head in each hyperedge; its in-cut counts hyperedges meeting both sides whose selected head lies inside the set.

notation.meaning: Selected head vertex of hyperedge e.
Number of oriented hyperedges entering X.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Head-selection orientation convention for finite hypergraphs.

source_refs.locator: 1.4 Special hypergraphs and bi-set systems p. 35

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A head orientation of \(H\) is a map \(h:\mathcal E\to V\) satisfying \(h(e)\in e\) for every \(e\in\mathcal E\). For \(X\subseteq V\), its entering value is
\[\rho_h(X)=\bigl|\{e\in\mathcal E:h(e)\in X\ \text{and}\ e\setminus X\ne\varnothing\}\bigr|.\]
Thus only hyperedges meeting both \(X\) and \(V\setminus X\) can enter \(X\). A cut-connectivity requirement \(r:2^V\to\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) is covered when \(\rho_h(X)\ge r(X)\) for every \(X\subseteq V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Orienting a hyperedge selects its head vertex; a hyperedge enters a set when its head is inside and another incident vertex is outside.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partition characterization with lower and upper indegree bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient partition inequalities for a supermodular-covering graph orientation with prescribed indegree intervals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\), let \(f,g:V\to\mathbb Z\) satisfy \(0\le f(v)\le g(v)\le d_G(v)\) for every \(v\in V\), and let \(h\) be nonnegative and crossing \(G\)-supermodular. There is an orientation covering \(h\) with \(f(v)\le\varrho(v)\le g(v)\) for every \(v\in V\) if and only if, for every partition \(\mathcal P=\{U_0,U_1,\ldots,U_t\}\) of \(V\), where only \(U_0\) may be empty, \[e_G(\mathcal P)+i_G(U_0)\ge\sum_{j=1}^t h(U_j)+\widetilde f(U_0)\] and \[e_G(\mathcal P)-e_G(U_0)\ge\sum_{j=1}^t h(V\setminus U_j)-\widetilde g(U_0).\] Here \(e_G(X)\) denotes the number of edges having at least one endpoint in \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A graph has a supermodular-covering orientation whose indegree at each vertex lies between integral bounds f and g exactly when the two stated inequalities hold for every partition with a distinguished, possibly empty block U0.
assumptions_latex: 0\le f(v)\le g(v)\le d_G(v)\text{ for every }v\in V
\mathcal P=\{U_0,U_1,\ldots,U_t\}\text{ ranges over partitions of }V\text{ in which only }U_0\text{ may be empty}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\text{ an orientation covering }h\text{ with }f\le\varrho\le g\iff\left[e_G(\mathcal P)+i_G(U_0)\ge\sum_{j=1}^t h(U_j)+\widetilde f(U_0)\text{ and }e_G(\mathcal P)-e_G(U_0)\ge\sum_{j=1}^t h(V\setminus U_j)-\widetilde g(U_0)\text{ for every admissible }\mathcal P\right]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pairwise Rooted Orientation Characterization of (k,l)-Partition Connectivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equates partition connectivity with the existence of suitably rooted orientations for every ordered pair of distinct vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $0\le k\le\ell$ be integers. A hypergraph $H=(V,\mathcal E)$ is $(k,\ell)$-partition-connected if and only if, for every pair of distinct vertices $s,t\in V$, $H$ has a $k$-edge-connected orientation satisfying $\varrho(Z)\ge\ell$ for every $s\bar t$-set $Z$ (that is, every $Z\subseteq V$ with $s\in Z$ and $t\notin Z$).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nonnegative k at most l, a hypergraph is (k,l)-partition-connected exactly when every distinct pair s,t admits a k-edge-connected orientation having at least l entering hyperedges for every set containing s but not t.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H\text{ is }(k,\ell)\text{-partition-connected}\iff \forall s,t\in V,\ s\ne t,\ \exists\text{ a }k\text{-edge-connected orientation of }H\text{ such that }\forall Z\subseteq V,\ (s\in Z\land t\notin Z)\Rightarrow\varrho(Z)\ge\ell

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partition Criteria for Hypergraph (k,l)-Edge-Connected Orientations when k Is at Most l
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes $(k,\ell)$-edge-connected orientability in the parameter regime $0\le k\le\ell$ using two partition inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $0\le k\le\ell$ be integers, and let $H=(V,\mathcal E)$ be a hypergraph. Then $H$ has a $(k,\ell)$-edge-connected orientation if and only if, for every partition $\mathcal P$ of $V$, both $e_H(\mathcal P)\ge k(|\mathcal P|-1)+\ell$ and $\sum_{Z\in\mathcal E}(e_{\mathcal P}(Z)-1)\ge \ell(|\mathcal P|-1)+k$ hold, where $e_H(\mathcal P)$ counts hyperedges meeting at least two parts and $e_{\mathcal P}(Z)$ counts the parts intersecting $Z$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When k is at most l, a hypergraph admits a (k,l)-edge-connected orientation exactly when every vertex partition satisfies both the hyperedge-crossing inequality and the corresponding total part-incidence inequality.
assumptions_latex: e_H(\mathcal P)=|\{Z\in\mathcal E:Z\text{ intersects at least two members of }\mathcal P\}|
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H\text{ has a }(k,\ell)\text{-edge-connected orientation}\iff \forall\mathcal P,\ \left[e_H(\mathcal P)\ge k(|\mathcal P|-1)+\ell\ \land\ \sum_{Z\in\mathcal E}(e_{\mathcal P}(Z)-1)\ge\ell(|\mathcal P|-1)+k\right]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hypergraph Orientation Lemma
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact feasibility criterion for prescribed hypergraph indegrees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let H=(V,\mathcal E) be a hypergraph whose hyperedges all have size at least two, and let m:V\to\mathbf Z_+. There is an orientation of H with indegree \varrho(v)=m(v) for every v\in V if and only if \widetilde m(V)=|\mathcal E| and i_H(X)\leq\widetilde m(X) for every X\subseteq V.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hypergraph with no hyperedge smaller than two admits an orientation having prescribed indegree m(v) at every vertex exactly when the prescribed indegrees sum to the number of hyperedges and every induced subhypergraph satisfies the corresponding sum bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl[\exists\text{ an orientation with }\varrho(v)=m(v)\ \forall v\in V\bigr]\iff\bigl[\widetilde m(V)=|\mathcal E|\ \land\ \forall X\subseteq V,\ i_H(X)\leq\widetilde m(X)\bigr].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sparsity-Preserving Hypergraph Trimming
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence of an ordinary graph trimming satisfying prescribed induced-edge bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let H=(V,\mathcal E) be a hypergraph whose hyperedges all have size at least two, and let m:V\to\mathbf Z_+. If i_H(X)\leq \widetilde m(X):=\sum_{v\in X}m(v) for every X\subseteq V, then H can be trimmed to a graph G such that i_G(X)\leq \widetilde m(X) for every X\subseteq V.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every hyperedge has at least two vertices and the number of hyperedges induced by each vertex set X is at most the sum of m over X, then one can trim every hyperedge to an ordinary edge so that the resulting graph satisfies the same induced-edge bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\text{ a trimming }G\text{ of }H\text{ such that }\forall X\subseteq V,\ i_G(X)\leq\widetilde m(X).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H\text{ has a strongly connected orientation}\iff \forall\mathcal P\text{ partitioning }V,\ e_H(\mathcal P)\ge |\mathcal P|

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partition criterion for mixed edge-connected hypergraph orientations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes mixed rooted-global hypergraph orientability and identifies the simplified regime \(\ell\le k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=(V,\mathcal E)\) be a hypergraph with root \(r_0\), and let \(k,\ell\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\). Then \(H\) has a \((k,\ell)\)-edge-connected orientation if and only if every partition \(\mathcal P\) of \(V\) satisfies \[e_H(\mathcal P)\ge k(|\mathcal P|-1)+\ell\] and \[\sum_{Z\in\mathcal E}\bigl(e_{\mathcal P}(Z)-1\bigr)\ge \ell(|\mathcal P|-1)+k.\] Here \(e_{\mathcal P}(Z)\) is the number of blocks of \(\mathcal P\) intersecting \(Z\). If \(\ell\le k\), the first inequality implies the second and is therefore sufficient by itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rooted hypergraph admits a mixed (k,ℓ)-edge-connected orientation exactly when every partition satisfies the stated cross-hyperedge and incidence-excess bounds. When ℓ is at most k, the cross-hyperedge bound alone suffices.
assumptions_latex: H=(V,\mathcal E)\text{ is a hypergraph with root }r_0
\mathcal P\text{ ranges over all partitions of }V
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H\text{ is }(k,\ell)\text{-edge-connected orientable}\iff\left[e_H(\mathcal P)\ge k(|\mathcal P|-1)+\ell\text{ and }\sum_{Z\in\mathcal E}(e_{\mathcal P}(Z)-1)\ge\ell(|\mathcal P|-1)+k\ \forall\mathcal P\right];\quad \ell\le k\Rightarrow\text{the first inequality alone suffices}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partition characterization of supermodular-covering hypergraph orientations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient conditions for orienting a hypergraph to cover a nonnegative crossing-supermodular requirement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=(V,\mathcal E)\), and let \(h:2^V\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}\) be crossing supermodular with \(h(\varnothing)=h(V)=0\). There is an orientation of \(H\) covering \(h\) if and only if every partition \(\mathcal P=\{V_1,\ldots,V_t\}\) of \(V\) satisfies \[e_H(\mathcal P)\ge\sum_{j=1}^t h(V_j)\] and \[\sum_{Z\in\mathcal E}\bigl(e_{\mathcal P}(Z)-1\bigr)\ge\sum_{j=1}^t h(V\setminus V_j),\] where \(e_H(\mathcal P)\) is the number of hyperedges meeting at least two blocks and \(e_{\mathcal P}(Z)\) is the number of blocks intersecting \(Z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hypergraph has an orientation covering a nonnegative crossing-supermodular requirement, vanishing on the empty and full sets, exactly when every vertex partition satisfies both the cross-hyperedge inequality for its blocks and the incidence-excess inequality for their complements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H\text{ has an orientation covering }h\iff\left[e_H(\mathcal P)\ge\sum_jh(V_j)\text{ and }\sum_{Z\in\mathcal E}(e_{\mathcal P}(Z)-1)\ge\sum_jh(V\setminus V_j)\text{ for every }\mathcal P\right]

children.title: Mixed-Graph Orientation Extensions
children.top_down_role: Connectivity orientation problems on graphs containing edges and fixed arcs.

assumptions_latex: \(M=(V,A\cup E)\) is a finite mixed graph, with fixed arcs \(A\) and undirected edges \(E\).
\(f:2^V\to\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) is a prescribed in-cut requirement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An orientation extension is feasible exactly when its total in-cut, including fixed arcs, covers \(f(X)\) for every \(X\subseteq V\).

notation.meaning: Number of fixed arcs entering X.
Number of newly oriented edges entering X.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extension of cut-covering orientation models to mixed graphs with immutable arcs.

source_refs.locator: 9.5 Mixed graphs and orientations p. 312

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose an orientation \(D_E\) of every edge in \(E\), while leaving every arc in \(A\) unchanged. The resulting directed extension satisfies the set requirement \(f\) when
\[\rho_A(X)+\rho_{D_E}(X)\ge f(X)\qquad\text{for every }X\subseteq V.\]
Equivalently, the undirected edges must cover the residual requirement
\[f_A(X)=\max\{0,f(X)-\rho_A(X)\},\]
so that \(\rho_{D_E}(X)\ge f_A(X)\) for every \(X\subseteq V\). Fixed arcs contribute connectivity but cannot be reversed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed arcs remain unchanged, while undirected edges are oriented to cover whatever part of each in-cut requirement the fixed arcs do not supply.

children.title: Partial-Orientation Completion
children.top_down_role: Completion regimes for partially prescribed edge directions.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite undirected graph and \(E=E_0\mathbin{\dot\cup}E_1\).
\(D_0\) is a prescribed orientation of \(E_0\), and \(f:2^V\to\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) is an in-cut requirement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A completion exists exactly when the unoriented edges \(E_1\) admit an orientation covering the residual requirements left by \(D_0\).

notation.meaning: Prescribed partial orientation on E_0.
Orientation chosen for the remaining edges E_1.
Number of arcs of an orientation D entering X.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completion criterion expressed through residual cut demands after a fixed partial orientation.

source_refs.locator: 9.5 Mixed graphs and orientations p. 312

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A completion of \(D_0\) is an orientation \(D_1\) of \(E_1\); the union \(D=D_0\cup D_1\) preserves every prescribed direction. It is an \(f\)-covering completion when
\[\rho_{D_0}(X)+\rho_{D_1}(X)\ge f(X)\qquad(X\subseteq V).\]
Define the residual demand by \(f_0(X)=\max\{0,f(X)-\rho_{D_0}(X)\}\). Then an \(f\)-covering completion exists if and only if \(E_1\) has an orientation \(D_1\) satisfying \(\rho_{D_1}(X)\ge f_0(X)\) for every \(X\subseteq V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complete a partial orientation by directing every remaining edge so that the new arcs cover all cut demand not already met by prescribed arcs.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Arc Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut criterion for completing a partially oriented multigraph to a strong orientation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=(V,A\cup E)\) be a finite mixed multigraph, where arcs in \(A\) are fixed and edges in \(E\) remain unoriented. For \(X\subset V\), let \(\delta_E(X)\) be the unoriented edges crossing \((X,V\setminus X)\), and let \(\rho_A(X)\) be the fixed arcs entering \(X\). The fixed arcs are compatible with a strong completion precisely when
\[|\rho_A(X)|+|\delta_E(X)|\ge 1\qquad(\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq V).\]
Equivalently, no nontrivial cut is devoid of an edge that can be directed into its chosen side. Under this condition the edges in \(E\) can be oriented while every arc in \(A\) retains its prescribed direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partial orientation has a strongly connected completion exactly when every nontrivial vertex set has either a fixed entering arc or an unoriented crossing edge.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is finite; parallel edges are allowed and loops are irrelevant.
Only edges in \(E\) may be oriented.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\) admits a strong orientation extending \(A\) if and only if \(|\rho_A(X)|+|\delta_E(X)|\ge1\) for every \(\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq V\).

notation.meaning: Fixed arcs entering X
Unoriented edges crossing the cut of X

knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Cost Connectivity Orientations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum-cost strong orientation with direction-dependent edge costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite undirected multigraph. For each edge \(e=uv\), assign finite directional costs \(c_e(u,v)\) and \(c_e(v,u)\). A minimum-cost connectivity orientation is an orientation \(D\) of every edge minimizing
\[c(D)=\sum_{e=uv\in E}c_e(D(e))\]
subject to \(D\) being strongly connected, equivalently \(|\rho_D(X)|\ge1\) for every \(\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq V\). If no feasible orientation exists, the optimum value is \(+\infty\). More generally, replacing the right-hand side by \(k\) defines the minimum-cost \(k\)-arc-connected orientation problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose one direction for every edge at minimum total directional cost while ensuring at least one arc enters every nontrivial vertex set.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite, and directional costs are additive.
Strong connectivity is the required connectivity notion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{OPT}=\min\{c(D):D\text{ orients }G,\ |\rho_D(X)|\ge1\text{ for all }\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq V\}\).

notation.meaning: Direction assigned to edge e
Arcs of D entering X

knowledge_statements.title: Strongly Connected Reorientation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum-cost reversal of an existing orientation into a strongly connected digraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D_0=(V,A)\) be a finite digraph whose underlying undirected multigraph is \(G\), and assign each arc \(a\in A\) a nonnegative reversal cost \(w_a\). For \(R\subseteq A\), let \(D_0^R\) be obtained by reversing precisely the arcs in \(R\). The strongly connected reorientation problem is
\[\min\left\{\sum_{a\in R}w_a:R\subseteq A,\ D_0^R\text{ is strongly connected}\right\}.\]
Feasibility depends only on \(G\): a feasible reorientation exists exactly when \(G\) is connected and has no bridge. The unweighted version takes \(w_a=1\) and minimizes the number of reversed arcs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reverse a minimum-cost subset of existing arcs so that the resulting digraph is strongly connected; feasibility requires a bridgeless connected underlying graph.
assumptions_latex: \(D_0\) is finite, and every arc may be reversed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{OPT}=\min_{R\subseteq A}\{w(R):D_0^R\text{ is strong}\}\), with finite optimum exactly when the underlying graph is bridgeless and connected.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weighted Dijoin–Dicut Min-Max Theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The integer-cost capacitated extension of dijoin–dicut covering-packing duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a digraph and let \(c:A\to\mathbb Z_+\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Min-Max Theorem for Eulerian Arc Replication
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes the minimum number of parallel arc copies needed to balance a strongly connected digraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $D=(V,A)$ be strongly connected. The minimum number of new arcs, each parallel to an existing arc, whose addition makes $D$ Eulerian equals

knowledge_statements.title: Well-Balanced Orientations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise edge-connectivity form of the well-balanced orientation theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite undirected multigraph \(G=(V,E)\), let \(\lambda_G(u,v)\) denote the minimum size of an undirected cut separating distinct vertices \(u,v\). For an orientation \(D\) of \(G\), let \(\lambda_D(u,v)\) be the maximum number of pairwise arc-disjoint directed \(u\)-to-\(v\) paths. There exists an orientation \(D\) such that, for every ordered pair of distinct vertices,
\[\lambda_D(u,v)\ge \left\lfloor\frac{\lambda_G(u,v)}2\right\rfloor.\]
Such an orientation is called well-balanced. Consequently, both directed local connectivities between each unordered pair attain at least half the undirected local connectivity, rounded down.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every finite undirected multigraph can be oriented so each directed local connectivity is at least half the corresponding undirected connectivity, rounded down.
assumptions_latex: Local connectivity is measured by edge- or arc-disjoint paths.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There is an orientation \(D\) satisfying \(\lambda_D(u,v)\ge\lfloor\lambda_G(u,v)/2\rfloor\) for all distinct \(u,v\in V\).

notation.meaning: Undirected local edge connectivity
Directed local arc connectivity from u to v

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Admissible Odd-Node Pairings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions and boundary properties of the pairing certificate used to construct best-balanced orientations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an undirected graph $G=(V,E)$, abbreviate $R_{\lambda_G}$ by $R_G$ and define $b_G(X):=d_G(X)-\widehat R_G(X)$. Since $d_G(X)\ge R_G(X)$, one has $b_G(X)\ge0$. An odd-node pairing is a matching $M$ of the odd-degree vertices of $G$, whose elements are added pairs rather than edges of $E$. It is admissible if $d_M(X)\le b_G(X)$ for every $\varnothing\subset X\subset V$; a set $X\subseteq V$ is $M$-violating if $d_M(X)>b_G(X)$. Because $b_G$ and $d_M$ are symmetric, $X$ is violating if and only if $V\setminus X$ is violating. Furthermore, $d_M(X)\equiv b_G(X)\pmod 2$ and $b_G(X)\ge0$, so the admissibility inequality is automatic when $|X|\le1$ or $|V\setminus X|\le1$; such sets are called trivial. If $G$ is Eulerian, every Euler orientation of $G$ is best-balanced.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The slack function is the cut size minus the modified connectivity requirement and is nonnegative. An odd-node pairing matches the odd-degree vertices using added pairs. It is admissible when every nonempty proper cut uses at most its slack; otherwise the cut is violating. Violation is invariant under taking complements, and singleton, cosingleton, empty, and full cuts satisfy the bound automatically. For an Eulerian graph, every Euler orientation is best-balanced.
assumptions_latex: M\text{ is a matching of the odd-degree vertices of }G\text{ using pairs outside }E
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b_G\ge0;\quad M\text{ admissible}\iff(\forall\,\varnothing\subset X\subset V)\ d_M(X)\le b_G(X);\quad X\text{ violating}\iff d_M(X)>b_G(X)\iff V\setminus X\text{ violating};\quad \min\{|X|,|V\setminus X|\}\le1\Rightarrow d_M(X)\le b_G(X).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Skew Supermodularity of the Modified Requirement Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Technical uncrossing property of the modified requirement function used for well-balanced orientations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $R:=R_r$ and $\widehat R:=\widehat R_r$. For every $X,Y\subseteq V$, at least one of
\[\widehat R(X)+\widehat R(Y)\le \widehat R(X\cap Y)+\widehat R(X\cup Y)\]
or
\[\widehat R(X)+\widehat R(Y)\le \widehat R(X\setminus Y)+\widehat R(Y\setminus X)\]
holds. Moreover, if $R(X)\le\min\{R(X\cap Y),R(X\cup Y)\}$, then the first inequality holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The modified requirement function is skew supermodular: for every two subsets, either the intersection-union inequality or the two-differences inequality holds. Under the stated comparison for the original requirement function, the intersection-union inequality necessarily holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl[\widehat R(X)+\widehat R(Y)\le\widehat R(X\cap Y)+\widehat R(X\cup Y)\bigr]\;\lor\;\bigl[\widehat R(X)+\widehat R(Y)\le\widehat R(X\setminus Y)+\widehat R(Y\setminus X)\bigr],\quad R(X)\le\min\{R(X\cap Y),R(X\cup Y)\}\Rightarrow\text{the first inequality}.

knowledge_statements.title: Bridge Obstructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp bridge obstruction to strongly orienting an undirected multigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite connected undirected multigraph. If \(e\) is a bridge, then every orientation of \(e\) leaves one side of \(G-e\) with no directed arc entering it or no directed arc leaving it; hence no orientation of \(G\) is strongly connected. Conversely, if \(G\) has no bridge, then \(G\) admits a strongly connected orientation. Thus
\[G\text{ is strongly orientable}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad G\text{ is 2-edge-connected},\]
where 2-edge-connected means connected and bridgeless.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A connected undirected multigraph has a strongly connected orientation exactly when it has no bridge.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite connected undirected multigraph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G\) admits a strong orientation if and only if every nontrivial cut has at least two edges.

notation.meaning: Graph obtained by deleting edge e

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse-Cut Obstructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut-size obstruction and sharp threshold for globally arc-connected orientations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix an integer \(k\ge1\) and let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite undirected multigraph. If an orientation \(D\) is \(k\)-arc-connected, then every nonempty proper \(X\subset V\) has at least \(k\) arcs entering and \(k\) arcs leaving. Therefore
\[|\delta_G(X)|\ge2k\qquad(\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq V).\]
Any cut with fewer than \(2k\) edges is consequently an obstruction. Conversely, if every nontrivial cut of \(G\) has at least \(2k\) edges, then \(G\) admits a \(k\)-arc-connected orientation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An undirected graph admits a k-arc-connected orientation exactly when every nontrivial cut contains at least 2k edges.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G\) has a \(k\)-arc-connected orientation if and only if \(|\delta_G(X)|\ge2k\) for every \(\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq V\).

notation.meaning: Edges with exactly one endpoint in X

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of a numerical severity measure for failure of the cut condition for k-arc-connected orientability.

source_refs.locator: 1.2 Cut functions and connectivity concepts p. 19
9.1 Rooted k-edge-connected orientations and reorientations p. 285

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite undirected multigraph with \(|V|\ge 2\), and let \(k\ge 1\) be an integer. For every \(\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq V\), define the cut deficit by
\[\operatorname{def}_k(X)=\max\{0,2k-|\delta_G(X)|\},\]
and define the cut-deficit severity by
\[\Delta_k(G)=\max_{\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq V}\operatorname{def}_k(X).\]
A set \(X\) attaining a positive maximum is a verifiable certificate that no \(k\)-arc-connected orientation exists. Moreover, \(\Delta_k(G)=0\) exactly when every nontrivial cut has size at least \(2k\), equivalently when \(G\) admits a \(k\)-arc-connected orientation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cut-deficit severity is the largest shortfall of a nontrivial cut from size 2k. A positive maximizing cut certifies that a k-arc-connected orientation is impossible, while zero severity characterizes orientability.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary local degree capacity for global k-arc-connectivity.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite undirected multigraph, let \(D\) be a \(k\)-arc-connected orientation of \(G\), where \(k\ge 1\), and let \(b^+,b^-:V\to\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}\) be prescribed outdegree and indegree upper bounds. Applying the directed cut requirements to \(\{v\}\) gives
\[d_D^+(v)\ge k,\qquad d_D^-(v)\ge k\qquad(v\in V),\]
and hence \(d_G(v)\ge 2k\). Therefore the bounds \(d_D^+(v)\le b^+(v)\) and \(d_D^-(v)\le b^-(v)\) conflict with \(k\)-arc-connectivity whenever \(b^+(v)<k\), \(b^-(v)<k\), or \(d_G(v)<2k\) for some \(v\in V\). These local inequalities are necessary but not generally sufficient for a degree-constrained connectivity orientation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A k-arc-connected orientation needs at least k incoming and k outgoing arcs at every vertex, so an upper bound below k or an undirected degree below 2k immediately obstructs feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Orientation Extension Obstructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut certificates preventing extension of fixed arcs to k-arc-connectivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=(V,A\cup E)\) be a finite mixed multigraph, with fixed arcs \(A\) and unoriented edges \(E\), and let \(k\ge1\). For every nonempty proper \(X\subset V\), any completion \(D\) satisfies
\[|\rho_D(X)|\le |\rho_A(X)|+|\delta_E(X)|.\]
Consequently, if
\[|\rho_A(X)|+|\delta_E(X)|<k\]
for some \(X\), then no orientation of \(E\) extending the fixed arcs can be \(k\)-arc-connected. Such a set \(X\), together with its fixed entering arcs and crossing unoriented edges, is a directly checkable extension-obstruction certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed partial orientation cannot extend to k-arc-connectivity if some set has fewer than k possible entering arcs, even after orienting every crossing free edge inward.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is finite, and arcs in \(A\) cannot be reversed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(|\rho_A(X)|+|\delta_E(X)|<k\) for some nontrivial \(X\), no \(k\)-arc-connected completion exists.

notation.meaning: Fixed arcs entering X
Unoriented edges crossing the cut of X

knowledge_statements.title: Orientation Tractability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algorithmic boundary for unconstrained strong orientability of undirected multigraphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite undirected multigraph \(G=(V,E)\) in adjacency-list representation, feasibility of a strongly connected orientation can be decided in \(O(|V|+|E|)\) time by computing connected components and bridges. If \(G\) is connected and bridgeless, a depth-first-search ear-orientation construction produces a strong orientation within the same asymptotic time; otherwise a component separation or bridge is an infeasibility certificate. This bound concerns unconstrained strong orientation only and does not classify variants with fixed arcs, degree restrictions, multiple connectivity levels, or additional side constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unconstrained strong orientability is decidable and constructible in linear time by testing connectivity and bridges; constrained variants fall outside this bound.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite undirected multigraph stored by adjacency lists.
The task has no costs, fixed directions, or degree side constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strong-orientation feasibility and construction require \(O(|V|+|E|)\) time in the adjacency-list model.

children.title: Reorientation Hardness Regimes
children.top_down_role: Complexity changes arising from modification costs, fixed directions, or connectivity targets.

knowledge_statements.title: Reorientation Hardness Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decision template separating reorientation variants by permitted reversals and side constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A constrained reorientation decision instance consists of a digraph \(D_0=(V,A)\), a reversible set \(F\subseteq A\), reversal costs \(w:F\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}\), a budget \(B\), and a specified connectivity predicate \(\mathcal C\). Its question is whether there exists \(R\subseteq F\) such that
\[\sum_{a\in R}w(a)\le B\quad\text{and}\quad D_0^R\in\mathcal C.\]
A hardness regime is determined by the choices of \(\mathcal C\), restrictions on \(F\), and any degree or local-connectivity side constraints. The template itself makes no uniform hardness claim: distinct specializations can have different computational complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reorientation hardness regime fixes which arcs may reverse, a budget, a target connectivity property, and any side constraints; complexity depends on that specialization.
assumptions_latex: Costs and the budget are encoded as part of the instance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The associated decision predicate is \(\exists R\subseteq F:\ w(R)\le B\text{ and }D_0^R\in\mathcal C\).

notation.meaning: Set of arcs eligible for reversal
Digraph after reversing precisely R
Required connectivity class
