knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ears and Ear Decompositions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General undirected-graph definitions, including proper ears and both forms of ear decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected graph. An ear is a path or circuit \(P\) of length at least \(1\) whose internal vertices all have degree \(2\) in \(G\); in particular, a single edge is an ear. An ear is proper when it is a path with distinct ends. If \(I\) is the set of internal vertices of \(P\), then adding \(P\) to \(G-I\) is called adding an ear. An ear decomposition is a sequence \(G_0,\ldots,G_k\) with \(G_0=K_1\), \(G_k=G\), and each \(G_i\) obtained from \(G_{i-1}\) by adding an ear. A proper ear decomposition instead has \(G_0=K_2\) and adds a proper ear at every step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In an undirected graph, an ear is a positive-length path or circuit whose internal vertices have graph degree two; a single edge qualifies. A proper ear is a path with distinct ends. An ear decomposition builds the graph from one vertex by successive ear additions, while a proper ear decomposition builds it from a single edge using only proper ears.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The notions of ear, proper ear, ear addition, ear decomposition, and proper ear decomposition are as specified above.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Double Wheels and Quartic Planar and Möbius Ladders
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions of three graph families for integers \(n\ge3\), together with their stated small-order isomorphisms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\ge3\). The double wheel \(D_n\) is obtained from \(\mathcal W_n\) by adding a new vertex adjacent to every rim vertex. The quartic planar ladder \(X_n\) is obtained from vertex-disjoint cycles \(u_1,\ldots,u_n\) and \(v_1,\ldots,v_n\), in cyclic order, by adding \(\{u_iv_i,u_iv_{i+1}:1\le i\le n\}\), where \(v_{n+1}=v_1\). The quartic Möbius ladder \(Y_n\) is obtained from a cycle with vertices \(w_1,\ldots,w_{2n-1}\), in cyclic order, by adding \(\{w_iw_{i+n-1},w_iw_{i+n}:1\le i\le n-1\}\cup\{w_nw_{2n-1}\}\). Moreover, \(D_3\cong K_5-e\), \(Y_3\cong K_5\), and \(D_4\cong X_3\), both being isomorphic to the octahedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For n at least three, D_n is the double wheel formed by adding a second hub adjacent to every rim vertex of a wheel; X_n is the quartic planar ladder formed from two disjoint n-cycles with the specified cross edges; and Y_n is the quartic Möbius ladder formed from the specified cycle and chords. The small cases satisfy D_3 is K_5 minus an edge, Y_3 is K_5, and D_4 and X_3 are octahedra.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D_n,\ X_n,\text{ and }Y_n\text{ are defined by the stated constructions, with }D_3\cong K_5-e,\ Y_3\cong K_5,\text{ and }D_4\cong X_3\cong\text{the octahedron}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimum edge count for prescribed edge connectivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The unrestricted family may contain parallel edges; a simple optimum is guaranteed when $k\le n-1$.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For positive integers $k,n$ with $n\ge2$, the minimum number $m_e(k,n)$ of edges of a $k$-edge-connected undirected graph on $n$ vertices is
\[
m_e(k,n)=\begin{cases}
n-1,&k=1,\\
\left\lceil kn/2\right\rceil,&k>1.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent Characterizations of 2-Edge-Connectivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Paths and circuits are understood in the graph, and ear endpoints may coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a graph \(G=(V,E)\), the following are equivalent: (i) \(G\) is 2-edge-connected; (ii) every pair of vertices is joined by two edge-disjoint paths; (iii) \(G\) is connected and every edge lies in a circuit; (iv) \(G\) has an ear decomposition \(G_0,\ldots,G_q=G\), where \(G_0\) is one vertex with no edge and each \(G_i\) is obtained from \(G_{i-1}\) by adding a path whose possibly equal endpoints lie in \(G_{i-1}\) and whose possibly empty set of internal vertices is disjoint from \(G_{i-1}\); (v) \(G\) can be constructed from one vertex by repeatedly adding an edge between two existing vertices, with loops allowed, or subdividing an edge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A graph is 2-edge-connected exactly when every vertex pair has two edge-disjoint connecting paths, exactly when it is connected and every edge lies on a circuit, exactly when it admits the stated ear decomposition, and exactly when it can be built from one vertex by adding edges between existing vertices or subdividing edges.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{(i)}\iff\mathrm{(ii)}\iff\mathrm{(iii)}\iff\mathrm{(iv)}\iff\mathrm{(v)}

knowledge_statements.title: Deficient Cut Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut-indexed residual requirements for an edge-connectivity augmentation instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H=(V,E_H)\) be a finite undirected multigraph and let \(r:2^V\to\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) specify required cut connectivities, with \(r(\varnothing)=r(V)=0\). For \(X\subseteq V\), define the residual cut deficiency
\[p_H(X)=\max\{0,r(X)-|\delta_H(X)|\}.\]
The deficient cut family is
\[\mathcal F_H=\{X:\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq V,\ p_H(X)>0\}.\]
If an augmenting edge set \(J\) makes every cut meet its requirement, then it must cover each deficiency: \(|\delta_J(X)|\ge p_H(X)\) for every \(X\in\mathcal F_H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deficient cuts are vertex sets whose current cut size is below its requirement; any augmentation must add enough crossing edges to cover every residual deficit.
assumptions_latex: \(r(X)\) is an integer cut requirement with \(r(\varnothing)=r(V)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every feasible augmentation \(J\) satisfies \(|\delta_J(X)|\ge p_H(X)\) for all \(X\in\mathcal F_H\).

notation.meaning: Residual connectivity deficiency of X

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Flow-constrained directed source location as a deficient-set transversal
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the directed source-location problem and its deficient-set hypergraph representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a digraph and let \(k,\ell\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\). A nonempty proper set \(X\subset V\) is in-deficient if \(\varrho(X)<k\), out-deficient if \(\delta(X)<\ell\), and deficient if either condition holds. A deficient set is minimal when none of its proper subsets is deficient; let \(H_{k\ell}\) be the hypergraph of minimal deficient sets. The FDSL problem seeks a minimum-cardinality \(S\subseteq V\) such that contracting \(S\) to a root \(s\) yields a rooted \((k,\ell)\)-edge-connected digraph, and this is equivalent to finding a minimum transversal of the deficient sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given a digraph and nonnegative connectivity requirements k and l, an in-deficient set has fewer than k entering arcs and an out-deficient set has fewer than l leaving arcs. The flow-constrained directed source-location problem is equivalent to finding a smallest vertex set that meets every deficient set, equivalently every minimal deficient set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min\{|S|:D/S\text{ is rooted }(k,\ell)\text{-edge-connected at }s\}=\tau(H_{k\ell})

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite simple undirected graph, let \(k\in\mathbb Z_{+}\), let \(F\subseteq \binom{V}{2}\setminus E\) be a set of candidate edges, and let \(J\subseteq F\). A biset is a pair \(\hat X=(X,X^{+})\) with \(X\subseteq X^{+}\subseteq V\). Its boundary is \(\Gamma(\hat X)=X^{+}\setminus X\), and its outer complement is \(X^{*}=V\setminus X^{+}\). For an edge set \(H\), let \(d_H(A,B)\) denote the number of edges of \(H\) joining disjoint sets \(A\) and \(B\). For \(X\ne\varnothing\) and \(X^{*}\ne\varnothing\), define \[p_G(\hat X)=\max\{0,\,k-|\Gamma(\hat X)|-d_E(X,X^{*})\}.\] The set \(J\) covers \(\hat X\) when \(d_J(X,X^{*})\ge p_G(\hat X)\), and the biset deficiency model imposes this inequality for every such biset.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A biset records an inner side, its boundary, and an outer complement. Its deficiency is the target vertex-connectivity minus the boundary size and the number of existing edges between the separated sides; selected candidate edges must cover the positive shortfall.

knowledge_statements.title: Representation Equivalence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact equivalence between ordered set pairs and proper bisets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every ordered set pair \((U,W)\) of nonempty disjoint subsets of \(V\), define \(\hat X=(U,V\setminus W)\). Conversely, for every biset \(\hat X=(X,X^{+})\) with nonempty inner set and outer complement, define \((U,W)=(X,V\setminus X^{+})\). These maps are inverse, and \[\Gamma(\hat X)=V\setminus(U\cup W),\qquad X^{*}=W.\] Consequently, \[p_G(U,W)=p_G(\hat X),\qquad d_J(U,W)=d_J(X,X^{*}).\] Hence the set-pair and biset covering systems have identical feasible augmentations whenever their deficiencies use these corresponding formulas.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proper bisets and ordered disjoint set pairs are bijective. Under the mapping, their boundaries, deficiencies, covering edges, and feasible augmentations coincide.
assumptions_latex: The set-pair and biset deficiencies use the same graph \(G\) and target \(k\).
Only set pairs with two nonempty sides and bisets with nonempty inner and outer-complement sides are included.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two representations define the same covering inequalities after the substitution \(\hat X=(U,V\setminus W)\).

notation.meaning: Biset corresponding to the ordered set pair.
Outer complement, corresponding to W.

knowledge_statements.title: Deficiency Uncrossing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uncrossing rule for skew-supermodular deficiency functions on cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p:2^{V}\to\mathbb R_{+}\) be skew-supermodular: for every \(X,Y\subseteq V\), at least one inequality \[p(X)+p(Y)\le p(X\cap Y)+p(X\cup Y)\] or \[p(X)+p(Y)\le p(X\setminus Y)+p(Y\setminus X)\] holds. Let \(x\ge0\) satisfy \(x(\delta(Z))\ge p(Z)\) for all \(Z\subseteq V\). If crossing sets \(X,Y\) are tight and one displayed inequality is the applicable skew-supermodular inequality, submodularity or posimodularity of the cut function implies that the corresponding uncrossed sets are also tight.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two crossing tight deficient cuts can be replaced by their intersection and union, or by their differences, whenever the matching skew-supermodular inequality applies.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is finite and \(p\) is nonnegative and skew-supermodular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The applicable uncrossed pair is tight and may replace \(X,Y\) without losing the tightness certificate.

notation.meaning: Edges with exactly one endpoint in X.
Total x-value on the cut of X.
Cut-deficiency requirement function.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimal Deficiency Cores
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inclusion-minimal positive members of a deficiency system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p:2^{V}\to\mathbb R_{+}\) be a deficiency function. A set \(C\subseteq V\) is a minimal deficiency core if \[p(C)>0\quad\text{and}\quad p(Z)=0\ \text{for every proper subset }Z\subsetneq C.\] Relative to a current augmentation vector \(x\), a residual core is defined analogously using \(p_x(Z)=\max\{0,p(Z)-x(\delta(Z))\}\). Thus a residual core is an inclusion-minimal set whose covering inequality remains violated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deficiency core is an inclusion-minimal set with positive deficiency; residually, it is a minimal set whose covering inequality is still violated.
assumptions_latex: \(p:2^{V}\to\mathbb R_{+}\) is a specified deficiency function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\) is a core exactly when it has positive deficiency and every proper subset has zero deficiency.

notation.meaning: A minimal deficiency core.
Deficiency remaining after augmentation vector x.

children.title: Laminar Deficiency Families

knowledge_statements.title: Laminar Deficiency Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Laminar optimal support obtained by uncrossing a cut-covering dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p:2^{V}\to\mathbb Z_{+}\) be skew-supermodular and let \(c\in\mathbb R_{+}^{E}\). Consider the dual cut-packing system \[\max\left\{\sum_{X\subseteq V}p(X)y_X:\ \sum_{X:e\in\delta(X)}y_X\le c_e\ \text{for all }e\in E,\ y\ge0\right\}.\] If this finite linear program has an optimum, then it has an optimal solution \(y\) whose positive support is laminar: for any supported \(X,Y\), either \(X\subseteq Y\), \(Y\subseteq X\), or \(X\cap Y=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a skew-supermodular cut requirement, an optimal dual packing can be chosen with laminar positive support.
assumptions_latex: The displayed dual has an optimal solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists an optimal dual solution whose support \(\{X:y_X>0\}\) is laminar.

knowledge_statements.title: Connector Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Connector sets for a family of deficient separations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a set of candidate edges and let \(\mathcal D\) be a family of deficient set pairs with integer demands \(p(U,W)>0\). An edge \(e=uv\in F\) connects \((U,W)\) if one endpoint lies in \(U\) and the other in \(W\). A set \(J\subseteq F\) is a connector for \((\mathcal D,p)\) if \[d_J(U,W)\ge p(U,W)\qquad\text{for every }(U,W)\in\mathcal D.\] For unit demands, every deficient pair must be connected by at least one selected edge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A connector is a candidate-edge set containing enough direct edges between the two sides of every deficient set pair.
assumptions_latex: Each demand \(p(U,W)\) is a positive integer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J\) is a connector exactly when it supplies at least \(p(U,W)\) connecting edges to every member of \(\mathcal D\).

notation.meaning: Family of deficient set pairs.
Number of selected edges directly joining U and W.
Required connector multiplicity for the pair.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The connector definition is plausible and definition is the appropriate content kind, but the vertex ground set and admissibility conditions on each set pair are not stated. No source with a specific locator supports the terminology or model.

knowledge_statements.title: Cover–Connector Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incidence-preserving equivalence of cut covers and connectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Associate with each deficient set pair \((U,W)\) the cut-like object whose covering candidates are \(\delta_F(U,W)=\{uv\in F:u\in U,v\in W\text{ or }u\in W,v\in U\}\). For every \(J\subseteq F\), \[|J\cap\delta_F(U,W)|=d_J(U,W).\] Therefore the covering inequality \(|J\cap\delta_F(U,W)|\ge p(U,W)\) is identical to the connector inequality \(d_J(U,W)\ge p(U,W)\). Applying this identity to every deficient pair gives a bijection between feasible cut covers and feasible connectors, preserving selected edges and total edge cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A candidate edge covers a deficient pair exactly when it connects its two sides, so feasible covers and connectors are the same edge sets with the same costs.
assumptions_latex: Cut-cover and connector models use the same candidate set \(F\).
Both models assign the same demand \(p(U,W)\) to each deficient pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The identity map on subsets of \(F\) is a cost-preserving bijection between feasible covers and feasible connectors.

notation.meaning: Candidate edges joining the two sides of a set pair.
Selected augmentation-edge set.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The incidence identity is mathematically immediate, but the claimed model correspondence has no cited source. It is an equivalence of representations, not a duality, so representation is the appropriate content kind once the claim is sourced.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounded Fixed-Size Undirected Edge-Connectivity Augmentation Criterion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes a fixed-total \(k\)-augmentation vector subject to componentwise lower and upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be undirected, let \(k\ge2\) and \(\gamma\ge0\) be integers, and let \(f:V\to\mathbf Z\cup\{-\infty\}\) and \(g:V\to\mathbf Z\cup\{\infty\}\) satisfy \(f\le g\). Define
\[
p(X)=\begin{cases}(k-d_G(X))^+,&\varnothing\subset X\subset V,\\0,&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}
\]
There exists a \(k\)-augmentation vector \(m\) with \(f\le m\le g\) and \(\widetilde m(V)=2\gamma\) if and only if
\[
\widetilde f(V)\le2\gamma\le\widetilde g(V),\qquad \widetilde g(X)\ge p(X)\quad(X\subseteq V),
\]
and, for every partition \(\{X_0,X_1,\ldots,X_t\}\) of \(V\), where \(t\ge1\) and only \(X_0\) may be empty,
\[
\widetilde f(X_0)+\sum_{i=1}^t p(X_i)\le2\gamma.
\]
It suffices to test the subset inequality only for \(X\in\mathcal S_G\) and the partition inequality only when \(X_i\in\mathcal S_G\) for \(i=1,\ldots,t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed-size k-edge-connectivity augmentation satisfying vertexwise lower and upper bounds exists exactly when the total bounds contain 2γ, every vertex subset has enough upper-bound capacity to cover its connectivity deficit, and every permitted partition satisfies the stated lower-bound-plus-deficit inequality. The subset and partition tests may be restricted to the designated family S_G.
assumptions_latex: f:V\to\mathbf Z\cup\{-\infty\},\quad g:V\to\mathbf Z\cup\{\infty\},\quad f\le g
p(X)=(k-d_G(X))^+\text{ for }\varnothing\subset X\subset V,\text{ and }p(X)=0\text{ otherwise}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists m\text{ a }k\text{-augmentation vector}: f\le m\le g,\ \widetilde m(V)=2\gamma\iff \bigl[\widetilde f(V)\le2\gamma\le\widetilde g(V),\ \widetilde g(X)\ge p(X)\ \forall X\subseteq V,\ \widetilde f(X_0)+\sum_{i=1}^t p(X_i)\le2\gamma\text{ for every admissible partition}\bigr].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Disjoint-Set Characterization of Bounded-Size k-Edge-Connectors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient feasibility characterization for undirected edge-connectivity augmentation with a cardinality budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected graph and let \(k,\gamma\in\mathbb Z_+\) with \(k\ge2\). The graph \(G\) has a \(k\)-edge-connector of cardinality at most \(\gamma\) if and only if, for every collection \(\mathcal P\) of pairwise disjoint nonempty proper subsets of \(V\), \[2\gamma\ge\sum_{U\in\mathcal P}\bigl(k-d_E(U)\bigr).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An undirected graph admits a k-edge-connector using at most gamma edges exactly when the total connectivity deficit of every collection of pairwise disjoint nonempty proper vertex sets is at most twice gamma.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists F\;\bigl[F\text{ is a }k\text{-edge-connector and }|F|\le\gamma\bigr]\iff\forall\mathcal P\subseteq 2^V\;\left[\begin{array}{l}\mathcal P\text{ consists of pairwise disjoint nonempty proper subsets of }V\\{}\Longrightarrow 2\gamma\ge\sum_{U\in\mathcal P}(k-d_E(U))\end{array}\right].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Min-max formula for minimum-cardinality r-edge-connectors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives a marginal-component reduction and a disjoint-set min-max characterization when no marginal component remains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected graph and let \(r:V\times V\to\mathbb Z_+\) satisfy \(r(u,v)=r(v,u)\ge\lambda_G(u,v)\) for all \(u,v\in V\) and \(r(u,w)\ge\min\{r(u,v),r(v,w)\}\) for all \(u,v,w\in V\). Let \(R\) and marginal components be defined as above. If \(K\) is a marginal component, then \[\gamma(G,r)=\gamma(G-K,r')+R(K),\] where \(r'\) is the restriction of \(r\) to \((V\setminus K)\times(V\setminus K)\). If \(G\) has no marginal components, then \[\gamma(G,r)=\max_{\mathcal P}\left\lceil\frac12\sum_{U\in\mathcal P}\left(R(U)-d_E(U)\right)\right\rceil,\] where \(\mathcal P\) ranges over all collections of pairwise disjoint nonempty proper subsets of \(V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A marginal component contributes exactly R(K) to the minimum connector size and can be removed recursively. If no marginal component exists, the minimum number of added edges is the maximum rounded half-sum of cut deficits over collections of pairwise disjoint nonempty proper vertex subsets.
assumptions_latex: R\text{ and marginal components are defined by (63.59) and the preceding definition}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K\text{ marginal}\Rightarrow\gamma(G,r)=\gamma(G-K,r')+R(K);\qquad G\text{ has no marginal components}\Rightarrow\gamma(G,r)=\max_{\mathcal P}\left\lceil\frac12\sum_{U\in\mathcal P}(R(U)-d_E(U))\right\rceil

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Degree-Bounded Undirected Edge-Connectivity Augmentation Criterion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes augmentation under vertex-degree upper bounds, including the exceptional odd-total obstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a graph, let \(k\ge2\) be an integer, and let \(g:V\to\mathbf Z_+\cup\{\infty\}\). There exists a graph \(H=(V,F)\) such that \(G+H\) is \(k\)-edge-connected and \(d_H(v)\le g(v)\) for every \(v\in V\) if and only if
\[
\widetilde g(X)\ge k-d_G(X)\qquad(\varnothing\subset X\subset V),
\]
and there is no partition \(\{X_0,X_1,\ldots,X_t\}\) of \(V\), with \(t\ge1\) and only \(X_0\) possibly empty, such that
\[
\widetilde g(X_0)=0,\qquad \widetilde g(X_i)=k-d_G(X_i)\ (i=1,\ldots,t),\qquad \widetilde g(V)\text{ is odd}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A k-edge-connectivity augmentation respecting vertex-degree upper bounds exists exactly when every nonempty proper vertex set has enough available degree capacity to cover its connectivity deficit and no tight partition produces the stated odd-total obstruction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists H=(V,F):\ G+H\text{ is }k\text{-edge-connected and }d_H(v)\le g(v)\ \forall v\in V\iff \left[\widetilde g(X)\ge k-d_G(X)\ \forall\varnothing\subset X\subset V\text{ and no stated tight odd partition exists}\right].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Degree-Specified Pairwise Edge-Connectivity Augmentation Criterion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut characterization for realizing prescribed augmentation degrees and pairwise connectivity demands.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let G=(V,E), let m be a degree specification with \widetilde m(V) even, and let r be a demand function on vertex pairs. Assume that no component C of G satisfies \widetilde m(C)=1. Define R_r(\varnothing)=R_r(V)=0 and, for \varnothing\subset X\subset V, R_r(X)=\max\{r(x,y):x\in X,\ y\in V\setminus X\}. knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An augmentation having exactly the prescribed degree at every vertex and meeting every pairwise edge-connectivity demand exists exactly when, for every vertex subset, its available modified degree total is at least the maximum demand across the cut minus the number of original edges crossing that cut.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reverse-Greedy Construction of a Feasible Degree Specification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the extracted reverse-greedy procedure without asserting an unstated optimality or running-time guarantee; condition (11.4) is retained symbolically because its formula is not present in the extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Order V=\{v_1,\ldots,v_n\} so that c(v_1)\ge c(v_2)\ge\cdots\ge c(v_n). Initialize m(v_i)=k+1 for i=1,\ldots,n-1 and m(v_n)=\max\{k+1,2\gamma\}. Then, for i=1,\ldots,n, decrease m(v_i) as far as possible while preserving condition (11.4) and \widetilde m(V)\ge2\gamma.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sort the vertices by nonincreasing node cost. Initialize every degree coordinate except the last to k plus one and initialize the last to the larger of k plus one and twice gamma. Visit vertices in that order and reduce each coordinate maximally while retaining condition (11.4) and total specified degree at least twice gamma.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: m(v_i)\text{ is successively made minimal in the stated order subject to (11.4) and }\widetilde m(V)\ge2\gamma.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: r-edge-connectivity and r-edge-connectors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines pairwise-demand edge connectivity and augmentation, gives the cut representation, and records the stated costed-versus-cardinality complexity boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\) and \(r:V\times V\to\mathbb Z_+\), \(G\) is \(r\)-edge-connected if every \(u,v\in V\) are joined by at least \(r(u,v)\) edge-disjoint paths. Equivalently, \(d_E(U)\ge r(u,v)\) for every \(U\subseteq V\), \(u\in U\), and \(v\in V\setminus U\). An \(r\)-edge-connector is an edge set \(F\) on \(V\), with parallel edges allowed, such that \(\lambda_{(V,E\uplus F)}(u,v)\ge r(u,v)\) for all \(u,v\in V\), and \(\gamma(G,r)\) is the minimum cardinality of such an \(F\). The minimum-cost version with \(k:V\times V\to\mathbb Q_+\) is NP-complete as stated in the source, already for \(E=\varnothing\) and \(r\equiv2\), whereas the cardinality case has a polynomial-time algorithm and a min-max formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pairwise edge-connectivity demands have equivalent path and cut descriptions. An r-edge-connector adds edges, allowing parallel copies, until every pair meets its demand, and gamma(G,r) is its minimum size. The source states that the costed problem is NP-complete even for an empty graph and uniform demand two, while the cardinality problem is polynomially solvable and has a min-max formula.
assumptions_latex: k:V\times V\to\mathbb Q_+\text{ in the costed variant}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G\text{ is }r\text{-edge-connected}\iff d_E(U)\ge r(u,v)\ \forall U\subseteq V,\ u\in U,\ v\notin U;\quad \gamma(G,r)=\min\{|F|:F\text{ is an }r\text{-edge-connector}\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimum-Cardinality and Fractional Connectivity Augmentation Min-Max Formula
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integral and fractional optimum values for undirected pair-demand edge-connectivity augmentation without marginal components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let G=(V,E) and the pair-demand function r satisfy the hypotheses of the cardinality-bounded augmentation theorem, including the absence of marginal components. Put \Delta(\mathcal P)=\sum_{X\in\mathcal P}(R_r(X)-d_G(X)) for each subpartition \mathcal P of V. The minimum number of new edges required to obtain \lambda_{G+H}(x,y)\ge r(x,y) for all x,y\in V is \max_{\mathcal P}\left\lceil\Delta(\mathcal P)/2\right\rceil. If fractional-capacity edges are allowed, the minimum total added capacity is \max_{\mathcal P}\Delta(\mathcal P)/2, and an optimal fractional augmentation can be chosen half-integral.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without marginal components, the minimum number of added edges is the maximum, over all subpartitions, of half the total cut deficit rounded upward. With fractional edge capacities, no rounding is needed, and a half-integral optimum exists.
assumptions_latex: r\text{ is a demand function on vertex pairs}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{edge}}=\max_{\mathcal P}\left\lceil\frac12\sum_{X\in\mathcal P}(R_r(X)-d_G(X))\right\rceil,\qquad \operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{frac}}=\max_{\mathcal P}\frac12\sum_{X\in\mathcal P}(R_r(X)-d_G(X)),\quad\text{with a half-integral fractional optimum}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounded-Size Degree-Constrained Augmentation Criterion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the hypotheses and deficit function of the fixed-size bounded-augmentation theorem; the displayed factor \(2\gamma k\) is retained as extracted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be undirected, let \(k\ge2\) and \(\gamma\ge0\) be integers, let \(f:V\to\mathbf Z\cup\{-\infty\}\) and \(g:V\to\mathbf Z\cup\{\infty\}\) satisfy \(f\le g\), and define \(p(X)=(k-d_G(X))^+\) for \(\varnothing\subset X\subset V\) and \(p(X)=0\) otherwise. There exists a \(k\)-augmentation vector \(m\) with \(f\le m\le g\) and \(\widetilde m(V)\le2\gamma\) if and only if
\[
\widetilde f(V)\le2\gamma,
\qquad \widetilde g(X)\ge p(X)\quad(X\subseteq V),
\]
\[
\widetilde f(X_0)+\sum_{i=1}^t p(X_i)\le2\gamma k
\]
for every partition \(\{X_0,X_1,\ldots,X_t\}\) of \(V\), where \(t\ge1\) and only \(X_0\) may be empty, and, when \(\widetilde g(V)\) is finite and odd, there is no such partition satisfying
\[
\widetilde f(X_0)=\widetilde g(X_0),\qquad \widetilde g(X_i)=p(X_i)\quad(i=1,\ldots,t).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A k-augmentation satisfying lower and upper vertex bounds and having total value at most 2γ exists exactly under the stated total lower-bound, subset-capacity, partition, and exceptional odd-total conditions.
assumptions_latex: f:V\to\mathbf Z\cup\{-\infty\},\quad g:V\to\mathbf Z\cup\{\infty\},\quad f\le g
p(X)=(k-d_G(X))^+\text{ for }\varnothing\subset X\subset V,\text{ and }p(X)=0\text{ otherwise}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists m\text{ a }k\text{-augmentation vector}: f\le m\le g,\ \widetilde m(V)\le2\gamma\iff\text{ conditions (11.13)--(11.15) and the stated finite-odd partition exclusion hold}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subpartition characterization of bounded-size hypergraph connectivity augmentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient condition for augmenting a hypergraph by hyperedges of bounded total cardinality to satisfy all pairwise local edge-connectivity demands.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H_0=(V,\mathcal E_0)\) be a hypergraph and let \(r(u,v)\) be a demand for every unordered pair of vertices. There exists a hypergraph \(H=(V,\mathcal E)\) such that \(\lambda_{H_0+H}(u,v)\ge r(u,v)\) for all \(u,v\in V\) and \(\sum_{Z\in\mathcal E}|Z|\le\gamma\) if and only if, for every subpartition \(\mathcal P\) of \(V\), \[\sum_{X\in\mathcal P}\bigl(R_r(X)-d_{H_0}(X)\bigr)\le\gamma.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hypergraph can be augmented by hyperedges whose total cardinality is at most gamma so that every vertex pair meets its prescribed local edge-connectivity demand if and only if the sum of the demand deficit R_r(X) minus the existing boundary value d_H0(X) is at most gamma for every subpartition of the vertex set.
assumptions_latex: r(u,v)\text{ is specified for every unordered vertex pair}
\mathcal P\text{ ranges over all subpartitions of }V
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists H=(V,\mathcal E):\ \bigl[\lambda_{H_0+H}(u,v)\ge r(u,v)\ \forall u,v\in V\bigr]\land\bigl[\sum_{Z\in\mathcal E}|Z|\le\gamma\bigr]\iff\forall\mathcal P,\ \sum_{X\in\mathcal P}\left(R_r(X)-d_{H_0}(X)\right)\le\gamma.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Characterization of Degree-Specified k-Edge-Connectivity Augmentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A cut-condition and parity characterization; the cut tests may be restricted to solid sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let G=(V,E), let k\ge 2 be an integer, and let m:V\to\mathbb Z_+. knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A prescribed nonnegative augmentation-degree vector can be realized by an added graph that makes G k-edge-connected exactly when its total degree is even and its degree supply on every nonempty proper vertex set covers that set's connectivity deficit. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Node-Induced Edge Costs and Solid-Set Deficit Demands
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the additive endpoint-cost regime and its solid-set connectivity-deficit function, while recording the stated general hardness boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the complete graph on V with potential edge set E^*, an edge-cost function c^*:E^*\to\mathbb R is node-induced if there exists c:V\to\mathbb R, possibly with negative values, such that c^*(uv)=c(u)+c(v) for every uv\in E^*. For the proper solid-set family \mathcal S'=\mathcal S_G\setminus\{V\}, define p(X)=(k-d_G(X))^+ for X\in\mathcal S'. The unrestricted minimum-cost k-edge-connected augmentation problem is NP-complete even when k=2 and G has no edges, whereas node-induced costs constitute a tractable special cost class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Edge costs are node-induced when every potential edge costs the sum of costs assigned to its endpoints; endpoint costs may be negative. For each proper solid set, its demand is the positive part of its k-connectivity deficit. The unrestricted cost problem is NP-complete already for k=2 and an edgeless input graph, while this additive cost regime is a tractable special class.
assumptions_latex: E^*\text{ is the edge set of the complete graph on }V
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c^*\text{ is node-induced}\iff\exists c:V\to\mathbb R\ \forall uv\in E^*,\ c^*(uv)=c(u)+c(v);\qquad p(X)=(k-d_G(X))^+\ \forall X\in\mathcal S'.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Characterization of Pairwise-Demand Augmentation Vectors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut-requirement representation and degree-vector feasibility certificate for nonuniform local edge-connectivity augmentation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $G=(V,E)$ be an undirected graph, and assign each unordered pair $\{u,v\}$ a demand $r(u,v)\ne1$. Define $R_r(X):=\max\{r(u,v):|\{u,v\}\cap X|=1\}$. Then $R_r$ is skew supermodular and hence near supermodular. An augmentation $G^+=G+H$ covers $R_r$, meaning $d_{G^+}(X)\ge R_r(X)$ for every $X\subseteq V$, if and only if $\lambda_{G^+}(u,v)\ge r(u,v)$ for every unordered pair $\{u,v\}$. The degree vector $m(v)=d_H(v)$ of such an $H$ is an $\mathbf r$-augmentation vector, and $m$ is an $\mathbf r$-augmentation vector if and only if $\widetilde m(V)$ is even and $\widetilde m(X)\ge R_r(X)-d_G(X)$ for every $X\subseteq V$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an undirected graph with a demand other than 1 on every vertex pair, the maximum demand separated by a cut defines a skew-supermodular, hence near-supermodular, cut requirement. Covering all these cut requirements is equivalent to meeting every pairwise local edge-connectivity demand. A nonnegative integral degree vector is realizable by such an augmentation exactly when its total is even and its sum on every vertex set X is at least the cut requirement minus the existing cut size.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_r\text{ is skew supermodular and near supermodular};\quad d_{G+H}\ge R_r\iff\forall\{u,v\},\ \lambda_{G+H}(u,v)\ge r(u,v);\quad m\text{ is an }\mathbf r\text{-augmentation vector}\iff\left[\widetilde m(V)\equiv0\pmod2\right]\land\left[\forall X\subseteq V,\ \widetilde m(X)\ge R_r(X)-d_G(X)\right].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimum Cardinality of an Undirected k-Edge-Connectivity Augmentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Min–max characterization by connectivity deficits over vertex subpartitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let G=(V,E) be undirected, let k\ge2, and let \gamma be a nonnegative integer. The graph G can be made k-edge-connected by adding at most \gamma edges if and only if 2\gamma\ge\sum_i[k-d_G(X_i)] for every subpartition \{X_1,\ldots,X_t\} of V. Consequently, the minimum number of added edges is \max_{\{X_i\}}\left\lceil\frac12\sum_i(k-d_G(X_i))\right\rceil, where the maximum ranges over all subpartitions of V; it suffices to consider subpartitions of proper solid sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An undirected graph admits a k-edge-connected augmentation with at most gamma new edges exactly when twice gamma dominates the total connectivity deficit of every vertex subpartition. The optimum number of new edges is the corresponding maximum half-deficit rounded upward, and proper solid-set subpartitions suffice.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists F,\ |F|\le\gamma,\ G+F\text{ is }k\text{-edge-connected}\iff 2\gamma\ge\sum_i[k-d_G(X_i)]\ \forall\text{ subpartitions }\{X_i\}\text{ of }V;\quad \operatorname{opt}=\max_{\{X_i\}}\left\lceil\frac{\sum_i(k-d_G(X_i))}{2}\right\rceil,\text{ with proper solid sets sufficient}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tight Solid-Set Cover for a Locally Minimal Degree Specification

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Interpolation of Lower and Upper Degree Bounds for Fixed-Size Augmentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combines separately witnessed lower-bound and upper-bound feasibility at the same augmentation size.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Edge-Connectivity Augmentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut formulation of bridge elimination in an undirected graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a connected undirected graph and let \(F\) be candidate edges. Define \[p_2(X)=\max\{0,\,2-d_E(X,V\setminus X)\}\qquad(\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq V).\] An augmentation \(J\subseteq F\) makes \(G+J\) two-edge-connected if and only if \[d_J(X,V\setminus X)\ge p_2(X)\qquad\text{for every nonempty proper }X\subset V.\] Equivalently, every bridge cut of \(G\) is crossed by a selected candidate edge; cuts already containing at least two original edges impose no residual demand.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two-edge-connectivity augmentation selects edges crossing every bridge cut; equivalently, each proper cut must contain at least two original or added edges.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) consists of additional undirected edges on \(V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G+J\) is two-edge-connected exactly when \(d_E(X,V\setminus X)+d_J(X,V\setminus X)\ge2\) for every proper nonempty \(X\).

notation.meaning: Residual demand needed to raise cut X to size two.
Graph obtained by adding J to G.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimum 2-Edge-Connector Size for a Forest
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact cardinality formula for possibly disconnected forests in terms of leaves and isolated vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a forest with at least two vertices. If \(p\) is the number of vertices of degree \(1\) and \(q\) is the number of isolated vertices, then the minimum cardinality of a 2-edge-connector for \(G\) is \(\left\lceil p/2\right\rceil+q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a forest with at least two vertices, the minimum number of augmenting edges needed for 2-edge-connectivity is half the number of leaves rounded up, plus the number of isolated vertices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min\{|F|:F\text{ is a 2-edge-connector for }G\}=\left\lceil\frac p2\right\rceil+q.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimum 2-Edge-Connector Size from Component Cut Degrees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact formula for a non-2-edge-connected undirected graph using its 2-edge-connected components of external cut degree zero or one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a non-2-edge-connected undirected graph. For \(i\in\{0,1\}\), let \(p_i\) be the number of 2-edge-connected components \(K\) satisfying \(d_E(K)=i\). Then the minimum cardinality of a 2-edge-connector is \(\left\lceil p_1/2\right\rceil+p_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a non-2-edge-connected undirected graph, count the 2-edge-connected components having external cut degree one and zero. The minimum connector size is half the first count rounded up, plus the second count.
assumptions_latex: G=(V,E)\text{ is an undirected graph that is not 2-edge-connected}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min\{|F|:F\text{ is a 2-edge-connector for }G\}=\left\lceil\frac{p_1}{2}\right\rceil+p_0.

children.title: Higher Edge-Connectivity Augmentation
children.top_down_role: Global undirected augmentation beyond bridge elimination.

knowledge_statements.title: Higher Edge-Connectivity Augmentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global cut formulation for undirected target edge-connectivity \(k\ge3\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected graph, let \(F\) be candidate edges, and fix \(k\ge3\). For every nonempty proper \(X\subset V\), define \[p_k(X)=\max\{0,\,k-d_E(X,V\setminus X)\}.\] An augmentation \(J\subseteq F\) makes \(G+J\) globally \(k\)-edge-connected if and only if \[d_J(X,V\setminus X)\ge p_k(X)\qquad\text{for every nonempty proper }X\subset V.\] Thus higher edge-connectivity augmentation is precisely the covering of all residual cut deficiencies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: To reach global edge-connectivity k, added edges must cover every proper cut's shortfall below k.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) and \(F\) are finite undirected graphs on the same vertex set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G+J\) is \(k\)-edge-connected exactly when every nontrivial cut has at least \(k\) original or added edges.

notation.meaning: Residual k-edge-connectivity demand of cut X.
Number of original edges crossing cut X.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Characterization of Undirected $k$-Augmentation Vectors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degree-sequence feasibility certificate for augmenting a non-$k$-edge-connected undirected graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $k\ge2$ and let $G=(V,E)$ be an undirected graph that is not $k$-edge-connected. A vector $m:V\to\mathbf Z_+$ is a $k$-augmentation vector if there exists a graph $H=(V,F)$ such that $G+H$ is $k$-edge-connected and $d_H(v)=m(v)$ for every $v\in V$. If $\mathcal S_G$ is the laminar family of solid sets of $G$, then $m$ is a $k$-augmentation vector if and only if $\widetilde m(V)$ is even and $\widetilde m(X)\ge k-d_G(X)$ for every solid set $X\subset V$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For k at least 2 and an undirected graph G that is not k-edge-connected, a nonnegative integral degree specification is realizable by an augmenting graph that makes G k-edge-connected exactly when its total degree is even and its degree sum on every solid set X is at least k minus the size of the cut of X.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal S_G\text{ is the laminar family of solid sets of }G
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: m\text{ is a }k\text{-augmentation vector}\iff\left[\widetilde m(V)\equiv0\pmod2\right]\land\left[\forall X\in\mathcal S_G\text{ with }X\subset V,\ \widetilde m(X)\ge k-d_G(X)\right].

knowledge_statements.title: Rooted Edge-Connectivity Augmentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut characterization of augmentation from a designated root.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected graph with root \(r\in V\), let \(F\) be candidate edges, and fix \(k\ge1\). For every nonempty \(X\subseteq V\setminus\{r\}\), define \[p_r(X)=\max\{0,\,k-d_E(X,V\setminus X)\}.\] An augmentation \(J\subseteq F\) provides \(k\) edge-disjoint paths from \(r\) to every vertex \(v\ne r\) if and only if \[d_J(X,V\setminus X)\ge p_r(X)\qquad\text{for every nonempty }X\subseteq V\setminus\{r\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rooted k-edge-connectivity is obtained exactly when added edges cover every cut separating the root from at least one other vertex up to capacity k.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) and \(F\) are finite undirected graphs on \(V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(v\ne r\), the graph \(G+J\) contains \(k\) edge-disjoint \(r\)-to-\(v\) paths exactly when all rooted cut inequalities hold.

notation.meaning: Designated root vertex.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Degree-bounded directed edge-connectivity augmentation criterion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut characterization without a prescribed augmentation-cardinality bound, together with implied subpartition bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let D=(V,A) be a digraph and let g_{\mathrm{in}},g_{\mathrm{out}}:V\to\mathbf Z_+\cup\{\infty\}. There exists H=(V,F) such that D+H is k-edge-connected and \varrho_H(v)\le g_{\mathrm{in}}(v),\ \delta_H(v)\le g_{\mathrm{out}}(v) for every v\in V if and only if \widetilde g_{\mathrm{in}}(X)\ge k-\varrho_D(X) and \widetilde g_{\mathrm{out}}(X)\ge k-\delta_D(X) for every \varnothing\subset X\subset V. Moreover, every subpartition \{V_1,\ldots,V_t\} of V satisfies \sum_i[k-\varrho_D(V_i)]\le\widetilde g_{\mathrm{out}}(V) and \sum_i[k-\delta_D(V_i)]\le\widetilde g_{\mathrm{in}}(V).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A directed k-edge-connectivity augmentation respecting vertexwise added in-degree and out-degree caps exists exactly when the corresponding capped cut inequalities hold for every nonempty proper subset. These conditions also imply aggregate deficit bounds for every subpartition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists H=(V,F):\ D+H\text{ is }k\text{-edge-connected},\ \forall v\in V\ [\varrho_H(v)\le g_{\mathrm{in}}(v),\ \delta_H(v)\le g_{\mathrm{out}}(v)]\iff\forall\varnothing\subset X\subset V\ [\widetilde g_{\mathrm{in}}(X)\ge k-\varrho_D(X),\ \widetilde g_{\mathrm{out}}(X)\ge k-\delta_D(X)]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Directed edge-connectivity augmentation with vertexwise degree bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The extracted statement refers to numbered conditions (11.30)–(11.33), whose formulas are not included in this item.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let D=(V,A) be a digraph and let g_{in},g_{out}:V\to\mathbf Z_+\cup\{\infty\}. (A) A digraph H=(V,F) exists such that D+H is k-edge-connected and \varrho_H(v)\le g_{in}(v) for every v\in V if and only if conditions (11.30) and (11.33) hold. (B) Such an H with \delta_H(v)\le g_{out}(v) for every v\in V exists if and only if conditions (11.31) and (11.32) hold. (C) Such an H satisfying both vertexwise bounds exists if and only if both one-sided augmentation problems (A) and (B) are feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a digraph with prescribed vertexwise upper bounds on added indegrees and outdegrees, feasibility of a k-edge-connected augmentation is characterized separately by conditions (11.30) and (11.33) for the indegree bounds and by conditions (11.31) and (11.32) for the outdegree bounds. An augmentation satisfying both sets of bounds exists exactly when both one-sided problems are feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}&\exists H:\ D+H\text{ is }k\text{-edge-connected and }\varrho_H\le g_{in}\iff (11.30)\wedge(11.33),\\&\exists H:\ D+H\text{ is }k\text{-edge-connected and }\delta_H\le g_{out}\iff (11.31)\wedge(11.32),\\&\exists H:\ D+H\text{ is }k\text{-edge-connected},\ \varrho_H\le g_{in},\ \delta_H\le g_{out}\iff (A)\text{ and }(B)\text{ are feasible}.\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.title: Strong Arc-Connectivity Augmentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum-cost augmentation to global directed arc-connectivity at least \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a finite digraph, let \(F\subseteq V\times V\) be candidate arcs with costs \(c:F\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\), and let \(k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1}\). Strong arc-connectivity augmentation seeks \(J\subseteq F\) minimizing \(c(J)=\sum_{e\in J}c(e)\) such that \(D+J=(V,A\cup J)\) is \(k\)-arc-strong. Equivalently, every nonempty proper set \(X\subset V\) satisfies \[|\delta^-_{D+J}(X)|\ge k\quad\text{and}\quad |\delta^+_{D+J}(X)|\ge k.\] Parallel candidate arcs may be represented as distinct elements of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose minimum-cost candidate arcs so every nontrivial vertex set has at least k entering and k leaving arcs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Find \(J\subseteq F\) of minimum cost with \(D+J\) \(k\)-arc-strong.

notation.meaning: Arcs entering and leaving X in D.
Digraph obtained by adjoining candidate arcs J.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence criterion for a degree-prescribed k-arc-connector
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes global directed augmentation with exact added indegrees and outdegrees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $D=(V,A)$ be a directed graph, $k\in\mathbb Z_+$, and $x,y:V\to\mathbb Z_+$. There exists a $k$-arc-connector $B$ satisfying $\deg_B^{\mathrm{in}}(v)=x_v$ and $\deg_B^{\mathrm{out}}(v)=y_v$ for every $v\in V$ if and only if $x(V)=y(V)$ and, for every nonempty proper subset $U\subset V$, $$x(U)\ge k-d_A^{\mathrm{in}}(U),\qquad y(U)\ge k-d_A^{\mathrm{out}}(U).$$
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A directed graph has a k-arc-connector with prescribed added indegrees x and outdegrees y exactly when the total prescribed indegree equals the total prescribed outdegree and every nonempty proper vertex subset has enough prescribed entering and leaving degree to cover its connectivity deficits.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists B\;\Bigl[B\text{ is a }k\text{-arc-connector},\ \deg_B^{\mathrm{in}}(v)=x_v,\ \deg_B^{\mathrm{out}}(v)=y_v\ \forall v\Bigr]\iff\Bigl[x(V)=y(V)\ \land\ \forall\varnothing\ne U\subsetneq V:\ x(U)\ge k-d_A^{\mathrm{in}}(U),\ y(U)\ge k-d_A^{\mathrm{out}}(U)\Bigr].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Directed k-arc-connector
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines global directed arc-connectivity augmentation, including the treatment of parallel arcs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $D=(V,A)$ and $(V,B)$ be directed graphs. The arc set $B$ is a $k$-arc-connector for $D$ if $(V,A\cup B)$ is $k$-arc-connected, where an arc occurring in both $A$ and $B$ is represented by parallel copies in the union. For $k=1$, the $k$-arc-connectors are precisely the strong connectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: B is a k-arc-connector for a directed graph D when adding its arcs makes D k-arc-connected. An arc present in both the original and added graphs is retained as parallel copies. For k=1, these are exactly strong connectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B\text{ is a }k\text{-arc-connector for }D\iff(V,A\cup B)\text{ is }k\text{-arc-connected};\qquad k=1\Rightarrow B\text{ is a strong connector.}

knowledge_statements.title: Rooted Directed Connectivity Augmentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outward rooted arc-connectivity; the inward version reverses all arcs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a finite digraph, let \(r\in V\), let \(F\subseteq V\times V\) be a set of candidate arcs, let \(c:F\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\), and let \(k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1}\). Outward rooted directed connectivity augmentation seeks \(J\subseteq F\) minimizing \(c(J)=\sum_{e\in J}c(e)\) such that, for every \(v\in V\setminus\{r\}\), the digraph \(D+J=(V,A\cup J)\) contains \(k\) pairwise arc-disjoint directed \(r\)-to-\(v\) paths. Equivalently, \[|\delta^-_{D+J}(X)|\ge k\qquad(\varnothing\ne X\subseteq V\setminus\{r\}).\] Inward augmentation requires \(k\) pairwise arc-disjoint directed \(v\)-to-\(r\) paths for every \(v\ne r\), equivalently the displayed condition after reversing every arc.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add minimum-cost candidate arcs to obtain k arc-disjoint directed paths from the root to every other vertex; reversing all arcs gives the inward variant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Find minimum-cost \(J\subseteq F\) satisfying \(|\delta^-_{D+J}(X)|\ge k\) for every nonempty \(X\subseteq V\setminus\{r\}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Min–max theorem for augmenting a packing of rooted arborescences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact weighted augmentation of a digraph from k to k+1 arc-disjoint arborescences rooted at a designated vertex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a digraph, let \(r\in V\), and let \(k\in\mathbb Z_+\) be such that \(D\) contains \(k\) arc-disjoint \(r\)-arborescences. Let \(D'=(V,A')\) and \(l\in\mathbb Z_+^{A'}\). Then
\[
\min\left\{l(C): C\subseteq A',\ (V,A\cup C)\text{, with arc multiplicities, contains }k+1\text{ arc-disjoint }r\text{-arborescences}\right\}
\]
equals the maximum cardinality \(t\) of a family of nonempty sets \(U_1,\ldots,U_t\subseteq V\setminus\{r\}\) such that \(d_D^{\mathrm{in}}(U_j)=k\) for every \(j\), and each arc \(a\in A'\) enters at most \(l(a)\) of the sets \(U_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a digraph already contains k arc-disjoint arborescences rooted at r, the minimum total l-cost of candidate arcs required to obtain k+1 such arborescences equals the largest size of a family of nonempty tight sets excluding r, each with exactly k entering arcs in the original digraph, for which every candidate arc a enters at most l(a) members of the family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min\{l(C):C\subseteq A',\ (V,A\cup C)\text{, with arc multiplicities, contains }k+1\text{ arc-disjoint }r\text{-arborescences}\}=\max\{t:\exists\,\varnothing\ne U_1,\ldots,U_t\subseteq V\setminus\{r\},\ d_D^{\mathrm{in}}(U_j)=k\ \forall j,\ |\{j:a\text{ enters }U_j\}|\le l(a)\ \forall a\in A'\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimum edge count for prescribed vertex connectivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The final regime follows the source's connectivity convention, under which the complete graph supplies the stated value when $k\ge n$.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For positive integers $k,n$ with $n\ge2$, the minimum number $m_v(k,n)$ of edges of a $k$-vertex-connected undirected graph on $n$ vertices is
\[
m_v(k,n)=\begin{cases}
n-1,&k=1,\\
\left\lceil kn/2\right\rceil,&1<k<n,\\
n(n-1)/2,&k\ge n.
\end{cases}
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For n at least 2, the minimum edge count is n−1 when k=1, ceiling(kn/2) when 1<k<n, and n(n−1)/2 when k is at least n, using the source's connectivity convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{\substack{|V(G)|=n\\G\ k\text{-vertex-connected}}}|E(G)|=\begin{cases}n-1,&k=1,\\\lceil kn/2\rceil,&1<k<n,\\n(n-1)/2,&k\ge n.\end{cases}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Directed k-vertex-connectors, good pairs, and good collections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions used by the directed vertex-connectivity augmentation min-max theorem; the extract also records the special k=1 equivalence and the ineffectiveness of parallel arcs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) and \((V,B)\) be directed graphs. The arc set \(B\) is a \(k\)-vertex-connector for \(D\) if \((V,A\cup B)\) is \(k\)-vertex-connected. A pair \((X,Y)\) of subsets of \(V\) is good if \(X\ne\varnothing\), \(Y\ne\varnothing\), \(X\cap Y=\varnothing\), and \(D\) has no arc from \(X\) to \(Y\). A collection \(\mathcal F\) of good pairs is good if, for every two distinct \((X,Y),(X',Y')\in\mathcal F\), either \(X\cap X'=\varnothing\) or \(Y\cap Y'=\varnothing\). Parallel arcs do not improve vertex connectivity, and directed 1-vertex-connectors coincide with directed 1-arc-connectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A directed k-vertex-connector is an added arc set that makes the augmented digraph k-vertex-connected. A good pair consists of disjoint nonempty vertex sets with no arc from the first set to the second. A collection is good when any two pairs have disjoint first sets or disjoint second sets. Parallel arcs do not improve vertex connectivity, and the vertex- and arc-connector notions coincide when k equals one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B\text{ is a }k\text{-vertex-connector for }D\iff(V,A\cup B)\text{ is }k\text{-vertex-connected; good pairs and good collections are defined by the stated separation conditions.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Certificate for a bounded-size undirected 2-vertex-connector
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary-and-sufficient feasibility certificate for a connector-size bound; N(U) retains its graph-neighborhood meaning from the source context.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a non-2-vertex-connected graph. knowledge_statements.title: Splitting-Off Augmentation Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduction by admissible undirected or directed splitting-off at an auxiliary vertex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite graph or digraph \(H\), a vertex \(v\), and required pairwise connectivities on \(V(H)\setminus\{v\}\). In the undirected case, choose incident edges \(uv,vw\), delete them, and add \(uw\). In the directed case, choose arcs \(uv,vw\), delete them, and add \(uw\). Accept the split only if every required connectivity between vertices distinct from \(v\) remains at least its prescribed value. Repeat admissible splits until no eligible pair remains or \(v\) becomes isolated; delete an isolated \(v\), solve the reduced augmentation instance, and reverse the recorded splits to reconstruct an augmentation of the original instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly replace two edges or consecutive arcs through an auxiliary vertex by one link while preserving all required external connectivities.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is finite and the connectivity requirements exclude the split vertex \(v\).
Each chosen split is admissible for all prescribed terminal pairs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure outputs a reduced instance together with a reversible log of connectivity-preserving splits.

knowledge_statements.title: Connectivity-Preserving Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissibility condition for reductions used in connectivity augmentation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a graph or digraph, let \(R(H)\) be the result of a proposed reduction, and let \(P\subseteq V(H)\times V(H)\) index terminal pairs unaffected by deleted auxiliary vertices. For a required connectivity function \(r:P\to\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}\), the reduction is connectivity-preserving precisely when \[\lambda_{R(H)}(s,t)\ge r(s,t)\qquad\text{for every }(s,t)\in P,\] where \(\lambda\) denotes the relevant edge-, arc-, or internally vertex-disjoint path connectivity. If \(H\) already meets the requirements, the stronger equality condition \(\lambda_{R(H)}(s,t)=\lambda_H(s,t)\) for every \((s,t)\in P\) is sufficient and preserves all pairwise connectivity values of interest.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Instance Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reverse lifting of a reduced augmentation through recorded reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I_0,I_1,\ldots,I_m\) be augmentation instances with recorded reductions \(R_i:I_{i-1}\to I_i\). Assume each reduction has a lifting map \(L_i\) such that every feasible augmentation \(J_i\) of \(I_i\) is mapped to a feasible augmentation \(L_i(J_i)\) of \(I_{i-1}\), with \(c(L_i(J_i))\le c(J_i)+\alpha_i\). Solve \(I_m\) to obtain \(J_m\), then set \[J_{i-1}=L_i(J_i)\qquad(i=m,m-1,\ldots,1).\] Output \(J_0\). The reconstruction is exact when every \(\alpha_i=0\) and each lifting map preserves the objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lift a reduced solution by undoing recorded reductions in reverse order; feasibility is preserved and lifting overhead accumulates additively.

Each lifting step has certified cost overhead at most \(\alpha_i\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(J_0\) is feasible and satisfies \(c(J_0)\le c(J_m)+\sum_{i=1}^{m}\alpha_i\).

knowledge_statements.title: Cactus Cut Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cactus encoding of an undirected graph's global minimum cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite connected undirected graph, and let \(\mathcal{M}\) be the family of shores of its global minimum cuts. There exist a cactus \(K\) and a map \(\phi:V\to V(K)\) such that \(\mathcal{M}\) consists exactly of the inverse images under \(\phi\) of shores obtained either by deleting one bridge of \(K\) or by deleting two edges belonging to a common cycle of \(K\). Thus every \(X\in\mathcal{M}\) has the form \(X=\phi^{-1}(W)\) for a component vertex set \(W\subset V(K)\) produced by an allowed deletion, and every such shore of \(K\) pulls back to a global minimum-cut shore of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All global minimum-cut shores of a finite connected undirected graph can be encoded by bridge deletions or two-edge deletions on cycles of a cactus.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite connected undirected graph.
\(\mathcal{M}\) is the family of shores of global minimum cuts of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exist a cactus \(K\) and map \(\phi:V\to V(K)\) encoding exactly \(\mathcal{M}\) through the stated deletions.

notation.meaning: A connected graph in which every edge lies on at most one cycle.

knowledge_statements.title: Block Decomposition Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-cut decomposition at articulation vertices of an undirected graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite connected undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\). Run depth-first search, recording discovery times and low-link values. Declare a nonroot vertex \(v\) an articulation vertex when some DFS child \(w\) satisfies \(\operatorname{low}(w)\ge\operatorname{disc}(v)\); declare the root an articulation vertex when it has at least two DFS children. Pop edges from the DFS edge stack at each such event to form maximal blocks having no articulation vertex internally. Output the bipartite block-cut graph whose nodes are the blocks and articulation vertices, with incidence given by containment. This graph is a tree and exposes subinstances attached through single articulation vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A DFS partitions a connected graph into maximal blocks and articulation vertices, producing a block-cut tree for separable processing.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite connected undirected graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm outputs all maximal blocks, all articulation vertices, and their block-cut tree.

notation.meaning: DFS discovery time of v.
Earliest discovery time reachable from v's DFS subtree by at most one back edge.

knowledge_statements.title: Component-Decomposition Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive decomposition into maximal undirected k-edge-connected vertex classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\) and an integer \(k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}\). For a current nonempty set \(U\subseteq V\), if \(\lambda_G(s,t)\ge k\) for every distinct \(s,t\in U\), output \(U\). Otherwise choose \(s,t\in U\) with \(\lambda_G(s,t)<k\), compute an \(s\)-\(t\) cut \((X,V\setminus X)\) of size less than \(k\), and recurse on the two nonempty sets \(U\cap X\) and \(U\setminus X\). Starting with \(U=V\), the output sets are the equivalence classes of \[u\sim_k v\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad u=v\ \text{ or }\ \lambda_G(u,v)\ge k.\] They are exactly the maximal vertex sets whose distinct members have pairwise edge-connectivity at least \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recursively intersect the current vertex set with the shores of cuts smaller than k to obtain the maximal classes whose vertices are pairwise k-edge-connected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output partitions \(V\) into the equivalence classes of \(\sim_k\).

notation.meaning: Minimum size of an undirected u-v edge cut.
Pairwise k-edge-connectivity relation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: TDI Theorem for Capacitated Supermodular Digraph Covers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: TDI and laminar-dual structure for an arc-capacitated covering system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\), let \(p:2^V\to\mathbb Z_+\) be positively intersecting supermodular, and let \(g:A\to\mathbb Z_+\cup\{\infty\}\) satisfy \(\varrho_g(Z)\ge p(Z)\) for every \(Z\subseteq V\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Integral Truncated Base Polyhedron for Supermodular Covering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral integrality and nonemptiness criterion underlying degree-bounded supermodular digraph covering; notation follows the extracted covering framework.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\ge0\) be an integer-valued positively crossing supermodular set-function on \(V\) with \(p(V)=0\), and let \(\gamma\in\mathbb Z\) satisfy \(\gamma\ge \widehat p(X)+\widehat p(Y)=p(V\setminus X)+p(V\setminus Y)\) for every pair of disjoint \(X,Y\subseteq V\). Let \(g:V\to\mathbb Z_+\cup\{\infty\}\) satisfy \(\gamma\le\widetilde g(V)\), and set \(T(\le g)=\{x\in\mathbb R^V:x\le g\}\). Then \(p^\gamma\) is positively intersecting supermodular, and both \(B'(p^\gamma)\) and \(B'(p^\gamma)\cap T(\le g)\) are integral base polyhedra. Moreover, \(B'(p^\gamma)\cap T(\le g)\ne\varnothing\) if and only if \(p(X)\le\widetilde g(X)\) for every \(X\subseteq V\) and \(\sum_i p(V_i)\le\gamma\) for every partition \(\{V_1,\ldots,V_t\}\) of \(V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated disjoint-set bound on gamma, the gamma-modification of p is positively intersecting supermodular and its associated base polyhedron remains integral after imposing coordinatewise upper bounds. The bounded polyhedron is nonempty exactly when every subset respects its upper-bound capacity and every partition has total p-value at most gamma.
assumptions_latex: p:2^V\to\mathbb Z_+\text{ is nonnegative and positively crossing supermodular}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p^\gamma\text{ is positively intersecting supermodular};\ B'(p^\gamma),\ B'(p^\gamma)\cap T(\le g)\text{ are integral base polyhedra};\ B'(p^\gamma)\cap T(\le g)\ne\varnothing\iff [\forall X\subseteq V,\ p(X)\le\widetilde g(X)]\land[\forall\text{ partitions }\{V_i\},\ \sum_i p(V_i)\le\gamma]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Degree-Specified Covering of a Crossing Supermodular Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence characterization for a digraph covering a set-function with prescribed in- and out-degree vectors, including the loopless boundary condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p:2^V\to\mathbb Z_+\) be positively crossing supermodular with \(p(\varnothing)=p(V)=0\). Let \(m_{\mathrm{in}},m_{\mathrm{out}}:V\to\mathbb Z_+\) and \(\gamma\in\mathbb Z\) satisfy \(\widetilde m_{\mathrm{in}}(V)=\gamma=\widetilde m_{\mathrm{out}}(V)\). There exists a digraph \(H=(V,F)\) covering \(p\) with \(\dot\varrho_H=m_{\mathrm{in}}\) and \(\dot\delta_H=m_{\mathrm{out}}\) if and only if \(p(X)\le\widetilde m_{\mathrm{in}}(X)\) and \(\widehat p(X)\le\widetilde m_{\mathrm{out}}(X)\) for every \(X\subseteq V\). Such an \(H\) can be required to be loopless if and only if, additionally, \(m_{\mathrm{in}}(v)+m_{\mathrm{out}}(v)\le\gamma\) for every \(v\in V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Balanced nonnegative integer degree specifications are realizable by a digraph covering the positively crossing supermodular requirement p exactly when the in-degree capacities dominate p and the out-degree capacities dominate its complementary function. Looplessness additionally requires each vertex's prescribed in- and out-degrees to sum to at most the total number of arcs.
assumptions_latex: p:2^V\to\mathbb Z_+\text{ is positively crossing supermodular}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists H\text{ covering }p:\ \dot\varrho_H=m_{\mathrm{in}},\ \dot\delta_H=m_{\mathrm{out}}\iff p\le\widetilde m_{\mathrm{in}},\ \widehat p\le\widetilde m_{\mathrm{out}};\quad H\text{ may be loopless}\iff \forall v\in V,\ m_{\mathrm{in}}(v)+m_{\mathrm{out}}(v)\le\gamma

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Separate and Simultaneous Bounds in Supermodular Digraph Covering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes separate in-degree, out-degree, and arc-cardinality restrictions and states their simultaneous compatibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\ge0\) be positively crossing supermodular on \(V\) with \(p(V)=0\), let \(g_{\mathrm{in}},g_{\mathrm{out}}:V\to\mathbb Z_+\cup\{\infty\}\), and let \(\gamma\in\mathbb Z_+\). (A) A digraph \(H\) covering \(p\) with \(\dot\varrho_H\le g_{\mathrm{in}}\) exists if and only if \(p(X)\le\widetilde g_{\mathrm{in}}(X)\) for all \(X\subseteq V\) and \(\sum_i\widehat p(V_i)\le\widetilde g_{\mathrm{in}}(V)\) for every partition \(\{V_i\}\) of \(V\). (B) Such an \(H\) with \(\dot\delta_H\le g_{\mathrm{out}}\) exists if and only if \(\widehat p(X)\le\widetilde g_{\mathrm{out}}(X)\) for all \(X\subseteq V\) and \(\sum_i p(V_i)\le\widetilde g_{\mathrm{out}}(V)\) for every partition. (C) Such an \(H=(V,F)\) with \(|F|\le\gamma\) exists if and only if every partition satisfies both \(\sum_i p(V_i)\le\gamma\) and \(\sum_i\widehat p(V_i)\le\gamma\). (D) If covering digraphs exist separately for (A), (B), and (C), then one covering digraph satisfies all three restrictions simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The in-degree, out-degree, and arc-count restrictions each have an exact subset-and-partition characterization. Moreover, separate feasibility of all three restrictions guarantees their simultaneous feasibility in one covering digraph.
assumptions_latex: p:2^V\to\mathbb R_+\text{ is positively crossing supermodular}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (A),(B),(C)\text{ have the stated subset-and-partition characterizations, and }[(A)\text{ feasible}]\land[(B)\text{ feasible}]\land[(C)\text{ feasible}]\Rightarrow\exists H\text{ satisfying }(A),(B),(C)\text{ simultaneously}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bi-set-function covering with degree and cardinality bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence criteria and simultaneous realizability for digraphs covering a positively crossing supermodular bi-set-function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\ge 0\) be a positively crossing supermodular bi-set-function on \(V\), with \(p(X)=0\) for every trivial bi-set \(X\). Let \(g_{in},g_{out}:V\to\mathbb Z_+\cup\{\infty\}\) and \(\gamma\in\mathbb Z_+\). Then: (A) a digraph \(H=(V,F)\) covering \(p\) with \(\dot\varrho_H\le g_{in}\) exists iff \(p_{in}\le\widetilde g_{in}\); (B) one with \(\dot\delta_H\le g_{out}\) exists iff \(p_{out}\le\widetilde g_{out}\); and (C) one with \(|F|\le\gamma\) exists iff \(\widetilde p(\mathcal F)\le\gamma\) for every independent set \(\mathcal F\) of bi-sets. Moreover, if separate covering digraphs exist satisfying respectively the in-degree bound, the out-degree bound, and the edge bound, then one covering digraph satisfies all three bounds simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonnegative positively crossing supermodular bi-set-function vanishing on trivial bi-sets, the stated inequalities characterize the existence of covering digraphs subject separately to prescribed in-degree, out-degree, or total-edge bounds. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Degree- and Cardinality-Bounded Supermodular Digraph Covering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous feasibility characterization with vertexwise in-degree and out-degree upper bounds and an arc-cardinality bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p:2^V\to\mathbb Z_+\) be positively crossing supermodular with \(p(V)=0\). knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient partition inequalities for orienting an undirected graph to cover a crossing-supermodular requirement.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Incidence polyhedron of rooted \((k,g)\)-connected spanning subgraphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral and TDI characterization using bi-set in-cut inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a rooted \((k,g)\)-connected digraph with root \(r_0\). Then the convex hull of the incidence vectors of all \(F\subseteq A\) such that \((V,F)\) is rooted \((k,g)\)-connected is
\[
\left\{x\in\mathbb R^A:0\le x\le\mathbf 1,\quad \varrho_x(Z)\ge k-w_g(Z)\text{ for every bi-set }Z\text{ with }\varnothing\subset Z_I\subseteq Z_O\subseteq V-\{r_0\}\right\}.
\]
This system is totally dual integral and defines a submodular-flow polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a rooted (k,g)-connected digraph, the incidence-vector convex hull of its rooted (k,g)-connected spanning subgraphs is exactly the unit-box polyhedron satisfying every stated bi-set in-cut inequality. The inequality system is TDI and defines a submodular-flow polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{conv}\{\chi^F:F\subseteq A,\ (V,F)\text{ is rooted }(k,g)\text{-connected}\}=\{x\in[0,1]^A:\varrho_x(Z)\ge k-w_g(Z)\ \forall Z,\ \varnothing\subset Z_I\subseteq Z_O\subseteq V-\{r_0\}\},\text{ and this system is TDI and defines a submodular-flow polyhedron.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Terminal rooted-connectivity augmentation polyhedron
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incidence-hull and TDI description for selectable terminal-headed edges added to a fixed subgraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H=(V,F_0\cup A)\) have root \(r_0\) and terminal set \(T\subseteq V-\{r_0\}\), with the head of every edge of \(A\) in \(T\). Suppose \(H\) is \((k,g)\)-connected from \(r_0\) to \(T\). The convex hull of incidence vectors of the sets \(F\subseteq A\) for which \((V,F_0\cup F)\) is \((k,g)\)-connected from \(r_0\) to \(T\) is
\[
\{x\in\mathbb R^A:0\le x\le\mathbf1,\ \varrho_x(Z)\ge p_1(Z)\text{ for every bi-set }Z\},
\]
where, for \(Z=(Z_O,Z_I)\),
\[
p_1(Z)=\begin{cases}k-\varrho_{F_0}(Z)-w_g(Z),&Z_I\cap T\ne\varnothing\text{ and }Z_O\subseteq V-\{r_0\},\\-\infty,&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}
\]
The system is totally dual integral and defines a submodular-flow polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When selectable edges all enter the terminal set and the full digraph is (k,g)-connected from the root to the terminals, the feasible augmenting edge sets have an exact unit-box incidence-hull description by the stated bi-set inequalities. The system is TDI and defines a submodular-flow polyhedron.
assumptions_latex: H=(V,F_0\cup A),\quad r_0\in V,\quad T\subseteq V-\{r_0\}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{conv}\{\chi^F:F\subseteq A,\ (V,F_0\cup F)\text{ is }(k,g)\text{-connected from }r_0\text{ to }T\}=\{x\in[0,1]^A:\varrho_x(Z)\ge p_1(Z)\ \forall\text{ bi-sets }Z\},\text{ and the system is TDI and defines a submodular-flow polyhedron.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Prescribed-degree r-edge-connector criterion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes undirected pairwise-demand augmentation with an exact prescribed added degree at every vertex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected graph, let \(r:V\times V\to\mathbb Z_+\) be symmetric, and let \(x:V\to\mathbb Z_+\) satisfy \(x(K)\ne1\) for every component \(K\) of \(G\). Then an \(r\)-edge-connector \(F\) satisfying \(\deg_F(v)=x_v\) for every \(v\in V\) exists if and only if \(x(V)\) is even and \[x(U)+d_E(U)\ge r(u,v)\] for every \(U\subseteq V\), \(u\in U\), and \(v\in V\setminus U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Provided no connected component has total prescribed added degree one, an exact-degree r-edge-connector exists exactly when the total prescribed degree is even and every separating cut has sufficient existing and prescribed incidence for each separated pair's demand.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists F:\ F\text{ is an }r\text{-edge-connector and }\deg_F(v)=x_v\ \forall v\in V\iff x(V)\text{ is even and }x(U)+d_E(U)\ge r(u,v)\ \forall U\subseteq V,\ u\in U,\ v\notin U

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Degree-bounded cardinality criterion for a k-edge-connector
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes feasibility of undirected k-edge-connectivity augmentation subject to a cardinality limit and lower and upper added-degree bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected graph, let \(k,\gamma\in\mathbb Z_+\) with \(k\ge2\), and let \(l,u\in\mathbb Z_+^V\) with \(l\le u\). Then \(G\) has a \(k\)-edge-connector \(F\) satisfying \(|F|\le\gamma\) and \(l(v)\le\deg_F(v)\le u(v)\) for every \(v\in V\) if and only if \(2\gamma\le u(V)\), \(k-d_E(U)\le u(U)\) for every nonempty proper subset \(U\subset V\), and \[2\gamma\ge l\!\left(V\setminus\bigcup\mathcal P\right)+\sum_{U\in\mathcal P}\left(k-d_E(U)\right)\] for every collection \(\mathcal P\) of pairwise disjoint nonempty proper subsets of \(V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A k-edge-connector meeting the cardinality and added-degree bounds exists exactly when the stated total upper-degree, cut upper-degree, and disjoint-family inequalities hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists F:\ |F|\le\gamma,\ l(v)\le\deg_F(v)\le u(v)\ \forall v\in V\iff 2\gamma\le u(V),\ k-d_E(U)\le u(U)\ \forall\varnothing\ne U\subsetneq V,\ \text{and }2\gamma\ge l(V\setminus\bigcup\mathcal P)+\sum_{U\in\mathcal P}(k-d_E(U))\ \forall\mathcal P

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Complexity regimes of connectivity augmentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies the four basic directed/undirected and arc-or-edge/vertex connectivity-augmentation variants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the minimum-cardinality augmentation problem, directed $k$-arc-connectivity, undirected $k$-edge-connectivity, and directed $k$-vertex-connectivity admit min--max relations and polynomial-time algorithms. Undirected $k$-vertex-connectivity augmentation is polynomial-time solvable for each fixed $k$, while its complexity when $k$ is part of the input is open.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Directed arc-, undirected edge-, and directed vertex-connectivity augmentation have min-max characterizations and polynomial-time algorithms. Undirected vertex-connectivity augmentation is polynomial-time solvable for fixed k, but its complexity for unrestricted k is open.
assumptions_latex: \text{The objective is to add a minimum number of edges or arcs to attain }k\text{-connectivity.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}&\text{The directed arc, undirected edge, and directed vertex variants have min--max relations and polynomial-time algorithms;}\\&\text{the undirected vertex variant is polynomial-time solvable for fixed }k,\text{ while the general-}k\text{ complexity is open.}\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the specified path, candidate links, and costs, both \(F_1=\{ad\}\) and \(F_2=\{ac,bd\}\) yield \(2\)-edge-connected augmented graphs. Hence minimum cardinality and minimum nonuniform cost select different augmentations on this instance.

children.title: Global versus Subset-Connectivity Boundary
children.top_down_role: The transition from uniform global connectivity to terminal-pair requirements.

assumptions_latex: Each unordered terminal pair \(s,t\) has an integral requirement \(r_{st}\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pairwise edge-connectivity requirements are equivalent to nonuniform cut bounds \(d_H(X)\ge R(X)\); global connectivity is their constant-demand special case.

notation.meaning: Maximum requirement separated by cut X
Size of the edge boundary of X in H

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut-demand transition from uniform global edge connectivity to pair-specific terminal connectivity.

source_refs.locator: 9.2 Global k-edge-connection p. 297
11.3 Augmenting ST-edge- and node-connectivity of digraphs p. 386

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(R(X)=\max\{r_{st}:|\{s,t\}\cap X|=1\}\), taking the maximum of an empty set as zero. By the edge form of Menger's theorem, \(H\) contains at least \(r_{st}\) edge-disjoint \(s\)-\(t\) paths for every pair if and only if \[d_H(X)\ge R(X)\qquad\text{for every }\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq V.\] Global \(k\)-edge-connectivity is the special case \(r_{st}=k\) for all distinct \(s,t\), when \(R(X)=k\) on every nontrivial cut. Nonuniform terminal requirements therefore replace one scalar cut threshold by a cut-dependent demand function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pair-specific terminal connectivity uses the maximum separated-pair demand on each cut; uniform global connectivity is the constant-demand special case.

knowledge_statements.title: Tree Augmentation Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes edge-connectivity augmentation on a tree and identifies why the path-cover formulation is tree-specific.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T=(V,E_T)\) be a finite tree and let \(L\subseteq \binom{V}{2}\setminus E_T\) be candidate links. For each \(\ell=uv\in L\), let \(P_T(\ell)\) denote the unique \(u\)-to-\(v\) path in \(T\). A set \(F\subseteq L\) makes \(T+F\) two-edge-connected if and only if
\[
\bigcup_{\ell\in F}E(P_T(\ell))=E_T,
\]
equivalently, every cut induced by deleting one tree edge is crossed by a link in \(F\). The tree assumption is essential to this exact path-cover characterization: for the cyclic backbone \(G=C_3\), the graph \(G\) is already two-edge-connected with \(F=\varnothing\), although no backbone edge is covered by a selected link path.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tree augmentation is exactly a covering problem for unique tree paths. This formulation ceases to characterize feasibility on cyclic backbones, which may already be two-edge-connected without covering their edges.
assumptions_latex: \(L\subseteq \binom{V}{2}\setminus E_T\) is a finite set of candidate augmentation edges.
\(F\subseteq L\) is the selected augmentation set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T+F\) is two-edge-connected exactly when every edge of \(T\) lies on \(P_T(\ell)\) for some \(\ell\in F\); this equivalence does not extend unchanged to non-tree backbones, as witnessed by \(C_3\) with \(F=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: The unique path between vertices u and v in the tree T.
The graph with vertex set V and edge set consisting of the tree edges and selected links.
The undirected cycle on three vertices.
